```text
=== HID_DevAddRecord (template) ===
 * Function         HID_DevAddRecord
 *
 * Description      Creates SDP record for HID device
 *
 * Returns          tHID_STATUS
 *
 ******************************************************************************/
tHID_STATUS HID_DevAddRecord(uint32_t handle, char *p_name, char *p_description, char *p_provider, uint16_t subclass,
                             uint16_t desc_len, uint8_t *p_desc_data)
{
    bool result = TRUE;

    HIDD_TRACE_API("%s", __func__);

    // Service Class ID List
    if (result) {
        uint16_t uuid = UUID_SERVCLASS_HUMAN_INTERFACE;
        result &= SDP_AddServiceClassIdList(handle, 1, &uuid);
    }
    // Protocol Descriptor List
    if (result) {
        tSDP_PROTOCOL_ELEM proto_list[2];
        proto_list[0].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_L2CAP;
        proto_list[0].num_params = 1;
        proto_list[0].params[0] = BT_PSM_HIDC;
        proto_list[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;
        proto_list[1].num_params = 0;
        result &= SDP_AddProtocolList(handle, 2, proto_list);
    }
    // Language Base Attribute ID List
    if (result) {
        result &=
            SDP_AddLanguageBaseAttrIDList(handle, LANG_ID_CODE_ENGLISH, LANG_ID_CHAR_ENCODE_UTF8, LANGUAGE_BASE_ID);
    }
    // Additional Protocol Descriptor List
    if (result) {
        tSDP_PROTO_LIST_ELEM add_proto_list;
        add_proto_list.num_elems = 2;
        add_proto_list.list_elem[0].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_L2CAP;
        add_proto_list.list_elem[0].num_params = 1;
        add_proto_list.list_elem[0].params[0] = BT_PSM_HIDI;
        add_proto_list.list_elem[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;
        add_proto_list.list_elem[1].num_params = 0;
        result &= SDP_AddAdditionProtoLists(handle, 1, &add_proto_list);
    }
    // Service Name (O)
    // Service Description (O)
    // Provider Name (O)
    if (result) {
        const char *srv_name = p_name;
        const char *srv_desc = p_description;
        const char *provider_name = p_provider;
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_SERVICE_NAME, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, strlen(srv_name) + 1,
                                   (uint8_t *)srv_name);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_SERVICE_DESCRIPTION, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, strlen(srv_desc) + 1,
                                   (uint8_t *)srv_desc);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_PROVIDER_NAME, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, strlen(provider_name) + 1,
                                   (uint8_t *)provider_name);
    }
    // Bluetooth Profile Descriptor List
    if (result) {
        const uint16_t profile_uuid = UUID_SERVCLASS_HUMAN_INTERFACE;
        const uint16_t version = 0x0100;
        result &= SDP_AddProfileDescriptorList(handle, profile_uuid, version);
    }
    // HID Parser Version
    if (result) {
        uint8_t *p;
        const uint16_t rel_num = 0x0100;
        const uint16_t parser_version = 0x0111;
        const uint16_t prof_ver = 0x0100;
        const uint8_t dev_subclass = subclass;
        const uint8_t country_code = 0x21;
        const uint8_t bool_false = 0x00;
        const uint8_t bool_true = 0x01;
        uint16_t temp;
        p = (uint8_t *)&temp;
        UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, rel_num);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_DEVICE_RELNUM, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&temp);
        p = (uint8_t *)&temp;
        UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, parser_version);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_PARSER_VERSION, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&temp);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_DEVICE_SUBCLASS, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&dev_subclass);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_COUNTRY_CODE, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&country_code);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_VIRTUAL_CABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
        result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_RECONNECT_INITIATE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
        {
            static uint8_t cdt = 0x22;
            uint8_t *p_buf;
            uint8_t seq_len = 4 + desc_len;
            p_buf = (uint8_t *)osi_malloc(2048);
            if (p_buf == NULL) {
                HIDD_TRACE_ERROR("%s: Buffer allocation failure for size = 2048 ", __func__);
                return HID_ERR_NOT_REGISTERED;
            }
            p = p_buf;
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, seq_len);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_ONE_BYTE);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, cdt);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, desc_len);
            ARRAY_TO_BE_STREAM(p, p_desc_data, (int)desc_len);
            result &= SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_DESCRIPTOR_LIST, DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE, p - p_buf, p_buf);
            osi_free(p_buf);
        }
        {
            uint8_t lang_buf[8];
            p = lang_buf;
            uint8_t seq_len = 6;
            uint16_t lang_english = 0x0409;
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, seq_len);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_TWO_BYTES);
            UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, lang_english);
            UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_TWO_BYTES);
            UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, LANGUAGE_BASE_ID);
            result &=
                SDP_AddAttribute(handle, ATTR_ID_HID_LANGUAGE_ID_BASE, DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE, p - lang_buf, lang_buf);
        }
```

```text
} esp_bt_l2cap_cb_param_t;
```

```c
#include <string.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

/* Bluedroid internal SDP database API (not part of the public esp_sdp API, which
 * cannot host an arbitrary record). Include dirs are added in CMakeLists.txt. */
#include "stack/bt_types.h"
#include "stack/sdpdefs.h"
#include "stack/sdp_api.h"

#include "wiimote_sdp.h"

static const char *TAG = "fauxmote.sdp";

#define ATTR_ID_HID_SUPERVISION_TIMEOUT 0x020C

/* The real Wiimote HID report descriptor (217 bytes) — see docs/wiimote-sdp.md. */
static const uint8_t s_hid_descriptor[] = {
    0x05, 0x01, 0x09, 0x05, 0xA1, 0x01,
    0x85, 0x10, 0x15, 0x00, 0x26, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x75, 0x08, 0x95, 0x01, 0x06, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x11, 0x95, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,   0x85, 0x12, 0x95, 0x02, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x13, 0x95, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,   0x85, 0x14, 0x95, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x15, 0x95, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,   0x85, 0x16, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x17, 0x95, 0x06, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,   0x85, 0x18, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x19, 0x95, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,   0x85, 0x1A, 0x95, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0x91, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x20, 0x95, 0x06, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x21, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x22, 0x95, 0x04, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x30, 0x95, 0x02, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x31, 0x95, 0x05, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x32, 0x95, 0x0A, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x33, 0x95, 0x11, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x34, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x35, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x36, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x37, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x3D, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0x85, 0x3E, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,   0x85, 0x3F, 0x95, 0x15, 0x09, 0x01, 0x81, 0x00,
    0xC0,
};

static const char k_name[]     = "Nintendo RVL-CNT-01";
static const char k_provider[] = "Nintendo";

bool WiimoteSdp_Register(void)
{
    uint32_t h = SDP_CreateRecord();
    if (h == 0) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "SDP_CreateRecord failed");
        return false;
    }

    bool ok = true;
    uint16_t u16;
    uint8_t *p;
    const uint8_t bool_true = 1, bool_false = 0;

    /* Service Class ID List: HID */
    uint16_t hid_uuid = UUID_SERVCLASS_HUMAN_INTERFACE;
    ok &= SDP_AddServiceClassIdList(h, 1, &hid_uuid);

    /* Protocol Descriptor List: L2CAP (PSM 0x11 = HID control) + HIDP */
    tSDP_PROTOCOL_ELEM proto[2];
    proto[0].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_L2CAP; proto[0].num_params = 1; proto[0].params[0] = BT_PSM_HIDC;
    proto[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;  proto[1].num_params = 0;
    ok &= SDP_AddProtocolList(h, 2, proto);

    /* Language Base Attribute ID List */
    ok &= SDP_AddLanguageBaseAttrIDList(h, LANG_ID_CODE_ENGLISH, LANG_ID_CHAR_ENCODE_UTF8, LANGUAGE_BASE_ID);

    /* Additional Protocol Descriptor List: L2CAP (PSM 0x13 = HID interrupt) + HIDP */
    tSDP_PROTO_LIST_ELEM add_proto;
    add_proto.num_elems = 2;
    add_proto.list_elem[0].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_L2CAP; add_proto.list_elem[0].num_params = 1; add_proto.list_elem[0].params[0] = BT_PSM_HIDI;
    add_proto.list_elem[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;  add_proto.list_elem[1].num_params = 0;
    ok &= SDP_AddAdditionProtoLists(h, 1, &add_proto);

    /* Names */
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_SERVICE_NAME, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, sizeof(k_name), (uint8_t *)k_name);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_SERVICE_DESCRIPTION, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, sizeof(k_name), (uint8_t *)k_name);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_PROVIDER_NAME, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, sizeof(k_provider), (uint8_t *)k_provider);

    /* Bluetooth Profile Descriptor List: HID v1.00 */
    ok &= SDP_AddProfileDescriptorList(h, UUID_SERVCLASS_HUMAN_INTERFACE, 0x0100);

    /* HID attribute values — Wiimote-exact (cf. docs/wiimote-sdp.md). */
    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0100);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_DEVICE_RELNUM, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0111);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_PARSER_VERSION, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
    const uint8_t subclass = 0x04;
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_DEVICE_SUBCLASS, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&subclass);
    const uint8_t country = 0x33;
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_COUNTRY_CODE, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&country);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_VIRTUAL_CABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_RECONNECT_INITIATE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);

    /* HID Descriptor List: sequence{ uint8 descriptor-type 0x22, text-string descriptor }. */
    static uint8_t desc_attr[8 + sizeof(s_hid_descriptor)];
    p = desc_attr;
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (uint8_t)(4 + sizeof(s_hid_descriptor)));
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_ONE_BYTE);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x22);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (uint8_t)sizeof(s_hid_descriptor));
    ARRAY_TO_BE_STREAM(p, s_hid_descriptor, (int)sizeof(s_hid_descriptor));
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_DESCRIPTOR_LIST, DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE, (uint32_t)(p - desc_attr), desc_attr);

    /* HID Language ID Base List: English / base 0x0100. */
    uint8_t lang[8];
    p = lang;
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 6);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_TWO_BYTES);
    UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0409);
    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_TWO_BYTES);
    UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, LANGUAGE_BASE_ID);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_LANGUAGE_ID_BASE, DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE, (uint32_t)(p - lang), lang);

    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_SDP_DISABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_BATTERY_POWER, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_REMOTE_WAKE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0100);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_PROFILE_VERSION, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0C80);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_SUPERVISION_TIMEOUT, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_NORMALLY_CONNECTABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_BOOT_DEVICE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);

    /* Browse group */
    uint16_t browse = UUID_SERVCLASS_PUBLIC_BROWSE_GROUP;
    ok &= SDP_AddUuidSequence(h, ATTR_ID_BROWSE_GROUP_LIST, 1, &browse);

    if (!ok) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "failed building Wiimote SDP record");
        return false;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote SDP record registered (handle 0x%08x)", (unsigned)h);
    return true;
}
```

```c
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_bt.h"
#include "esp_bt_main.h"
#include "esp_bt_device.h"
#include "esp_gap_bt_api.h"
#include "esp_l2cap_bt_api.h"

#include "bt_hid_device.h"
#include "wiimote_sdp.h"

static const char *TAG = "fauxmote.bt";

#define FAUXMOTE_BT_NAME "Nintendo RVL-CNT-01"
#define PSM_HID_CONTROL  0x0011
#define PSM_HID_INTERRUPT 0x0013

static void log_bda(const char *what, const uint8_t *bda)
{
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "%s %02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x", what,
             bda[0], bda[1], bda[2], bda[3], bda[4], bda[5]);
}

/* Advertise as a Wiimote: Class of Device 0x002504 (peripheral/joystick, with the
 * limited-discoverable service bit) + limited-discoverable scan mode. The Wii's
 * SYNC scan uses a limited inquiry (LIAC), so general discovery isn't enough. */
static void set_wiimote_discoverable(void)
{
    esp_bt_cod_t cod = {0};
    cod.minor = 0x01;
    cod.major = ESP_BT_COD_MAJOR_DEV_PERIPHERAL;
    cod.service = 0x01;
    esp_bt_gap_set_cod(cod, ESP_BT_SET_COD_ALL);
    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_LIMITED_DISCOVERABLE);
}

static void gap_cb(esp_bt_gap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_gap_cb_param_t *param)
{
    switch (event) {
    case ESP_BT_GAP_PIN_REQ_EVT: {
        /* Console-SYNC (bonding) pairing: PIN = the host's BD_ADDR, reversed. */
        esp_bt_pin_code_t pin;
        for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
            pin[i] = param->pin_req.bda[5 - i];
        }
        log_bda("PIN request from", param->pin_req.bda);
        esp_bt_gap_pin_reply(param->pin_req.bda, true, 6, pin);
        break;
    }
    case ESP_BT_GAP_AUTH_CMPL_EVT:
        if (param->auth_cmpl.stat == ESP_BT_STATUS_SUCCESS) {
            log_bda("auth OK with", param->auth_cmpl.bda);
        } else {
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "auth FAILED, status=%d", param->auth_cmpl.stat);
        }
        break;
    default:
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "gap event %d", event);
        break;
    }
}

static void l2cap_cb(esp_bt_l2cap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_l2cap_cb_param_t *param)
{
    switch (event) {
    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_INIT_EVT:
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP init status=%d; starting HID servers", param->init.status);
        esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_CONTROL);
        esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT);
        break;
    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_START_EVT:
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP server up status=%d handle=%u",
                 param->start.status, (unsigned)param->start.handle);
        break;
    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT:
        log_bda("L2CAP OPEN from", param->open.rem_bda);
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "  status=%d handle=%u fd=%d mtu=%d",
                 param->open.status, (unsigned)param->open.handle,
                 param->open.fd, (int)param->open.tx_mtu);
        break;
    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_CLOSE_EVT:
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "L2CAP CLOSE handle=%u async=%d",
                 (unsigned)param->close.handle, param->close.async);
        break;
    default:
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "l2cap event %d", event);
        break;
    }
}

void Fauxmote_BtStart(void)
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_mem_release(ESP_BT_MODE_BLE));
    esp_bt_controller_config_t cfg = BT_CONTROLLER_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_init(&cfg));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_enable(ESP_BT_MODE_CLASSIC_BT));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_init());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_enable());

    const uint8_t *bda = esp_bt_dev_get_address();
    if (bda) {
        /* Our BD_ADDR — also the 1+2 temporary-pairing PIN (this, reversed). */
        log_bda("BD_ADDR", bda);
    }

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_register_callback(gap_cb));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_set_device_name(FAUXMOTE_BT_NAME));

    /* Legacy PIN pairing (SSP disabled in sdkconfig): we answer each PIN request. */
    esp_bt_gap_set_pin(ESP_BT_PIN_TYPE_VARIABLE, 0, NULL);

    /* Serve the exact Wiimote SDP record, then listen for the Wii's HID L2CAP
     * connections on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). */
    if (!WiimoteSdp_Register()) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Wiimote SDP registration failed");
    }
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_register_callback(l2cap_cb));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_init());

    set_wiimote_discoverable();
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "fauxmote up: custom Wiimote SDP + L2CAP 0x11/0x13, limited-discoverable");
}

```

Custom-SDP build is written. Summary of the new shape:

- **[main/wiimote_sdp.c](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote_sdp.c)** — builds the **byte-exact Wiimote SDP record** via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/… (modeled on the stack's own `HID_DevAddRecord`, but with Wiimote-exact values: subclass `0x04`, country `0x33`, virtual-cable `false`, the real 217-byte descriptor, etc.).
- **[main/bt_hid_device.c](firmware/fauxmote/main/bt_hid_device.c)** — dropped `esp_hidd` entirely; now registers that SDP record and listens on PSM `0x11`/`0x13` via `esp_bt_l2cap`, logging every connection. Keeps the working discovery/COD/PIN logic.
- **[main/CMakeLists.txt](firmware/fauxmote/main/CMakeLists.txt)** — adds the internal Bluedroid include dirs.
- **[sdkconfig.defaults](firmware/fauxmote/sdkconfig.defaults)** — enables L2CAP and raises the SDP buffers to 512/1024.

## Build & test

The new sdkconfig defaults only apply if you regenerate, so:

```sh
idf.py set-target esp32      # re-applies sdkconfig.defaults (L2CAP + SDP limits)
idf.py build flash monitor
```

**Heads up:** this is the first compile of code that reaches into Bluedroid's *internal* headers, so a build error or two (a missing internal include path, a constant name) is likely. **Paste any build errors** and I'll fix them fast — that's expected for this step, not a setback.

**Once it builds and flashes**, press the Wii's red SYNC button. The milestone — proof the custom SDP works — is:

```
fauxmote.sdp: Wiimote SDP record registered (handle 0x...)
fauxmote.bt: L2CAP server up ... (x2, for 0x11 and 0x13)
...after SYNC...
fauxmote.bt: PIN request from <Wii bda>
fauxmote.bt: L2CAP OPEN from <Wii bda>   ← the Wii accepted our SDP and opened the HID control channel
```

That `L2CAP OPEN` is the whole game for this phase — it means the Wii got past SDP validation (which `esp_hidd` could never satisfy) and is treating us as a real Wiimote. If instead it still disconnects right after the SDP read (no `L2CAP OPEN`), we compare our record against the real one attribute-by-attribute.

Paste the build result (errors or boot log + sync behavior) and we'll take the next step.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-12 20:10:10Z)**_

Your read is exactly right — that's **normal Wii idle behavior**, not a fault. After ~5 min (timestamp 310514 ms) with no controller activity the Wii dims, drops to sniff/unsniff, then tears down both HID channels and the ACL (`rsn 0x13` = it terminated). A *real* Wiimote disconnects the same way; you wake it by pressing a button. We got clean `L2CAP CLOSE` events for both handles — graceful, nothing wrong.

One detail that's actually a Phase-2 signpost:
```
W BT_BTC: btc_l2cap_cb_handler slot rx data will be discard in 20000 milliseconds!
```
That's the Wii's initial HID reports (status/reporting-mode/LED) sitting unread in our fd buffer — because we don't read the fd yet — getting discarded. Exactly what Phase 2 fixes.

And your instinct on keep-awake is correct: once we send input reports / button activity (Phase 2, and ultimately Marvin's gameplay), each report resets the Wii's idle timer, so the link stays up. A real controller keeps the console awake the same way. (Separately, the SDP `ReconnectInitiate=true` we set means a real Wiimote would auto-reconnect on a button press after sleep — we'd implement that initiation later if we want hands-off wake-from-sleep.)

So: clean, expected, link tears down gracefully and the board's still advertising for the next connection.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-12 20:13:29Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-12 20:13:40Z)**_

Great thing to lock down now, because it shapes Phase 2. Short version: **the building blocks are in place, but we have to implement the reconnect — it's not automatic.** Let me separate two cases, because they behave very differently on Wii:

**1. Reconnect the controller (console still ON, it dropped us for idle — what you just saw).**
This is recoverable, and we already set the right groundwork:
- Our SDP advertises `HIDReconnectInitiate = true` → the *device* is expected to initiate reconnection (the Wii won't chase us).
- We captured the Wii's BD_ADDR at pairing (`00:17:ab:07:2c:21`).
- `esp_bt_l2cap_connect(...)` lets us open PSM 0x11→0x13 back to that address.

So the capability exists; Phase 2/3 needs to add: store the bonded Wii address, and on a trigger (a button from Marvin) call `esp_bt_l2cap_connect` to re-establish, then resume reports. I'll bake "device-initiated reconnect" into the Phase 2 plan so it's not forgotten.

**2. Wake the console from full standby (red light).**
Set expectations here: **a Wiimote cannot power a Wii on from standby** — in standby the Wii's Bluetooth radio is off, so no controller can wake it (unlike some consoles). That's a console-power-button action. So "wake the Wii" only means case #1 (reconnect when the console is already running). Worth knowing before Marvin's design assumes BT can cold-start the Wii.

**Keep-awake — yes, an occasional message works,** with one nuance: the Wii's idle-disconnect watches for *input activity*, so the keep-alive should be an occasional **input report (a button report)**, not just any packet. During actual gameplay this is free — Marvin streams strum/fret inputs constantly, which keeps both the link and the console awake. For idle/menu periods, a periodic no-op button nudge does it.

I'll record both (reconnect + keep-awake + the standby caveat) in the journal as Phase 2 scope so it's accounted for.

Now I can see the real flow, and there's a concrete bug to fix. Two findings:

1. **The channels work as before** — SDP read on CID 0x40 (our 14/250/234-byte responses), then HID control + interrupt open (fd 3, fd 4), `auth OK`, `BTA_JvL2capRead`. Good.
2. **Our reader is exiting instantly:** `fd 3 read=0; reader exit`. `read()` returns **0** right at open (before any data), and I wrongly treated `<= 0` as EOF. These VFS fds are evidently non-blocking, so `0` means "no data yet," not "closed." I need to block properly (via `select`/`poll`) and only exit on a real close.

```text
                if (slot->close_alarm && osi_alarm_is_active(slot->close_alarm)) {
                    osi_alarm_cancel(slot->close_alarm);
                    osi_alarm_set(slot->close_alarm, 0);
                }
                osi_mutex_unlock(&l2cap_local_param.l2cap_slot_mutex);
                break;
            }
        } else {
            osi_mutex_unlock(&l2cap_local_param.l2cap_slot_mutex);
            BTC_TRACE_ERROR("%s peer close, data will be discarded!\n", __func__);
            errno = EPIPE;
            item_size = -1;
            break;
        }
        osi_mutex_unlock(&l2cap_local_param.l2cap_slot_mutex);

        if (p_buf->len <= size) {
            memcpy(dst, p_buf->data + p_buf->offset, p_buf->len);
            size -= p_buf->len;
            item_size += p_buf->len;
            dst += p_buf->len;
            p_buf->offset += p_buf->len;
            p_buf->len = 0; // indicate the p_buf is unused
        } else {
            memcpy(dst, p_buf->data + p_buf->offset, size);
            item_size += size;
            p_buf->offset += size;
            p_buf->len -= size;
            size = 0;
        }
    }
    return item_size;
}

            ret = ESP_BT_L2CAP_NEED_INIT;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-12 20:25:03Z)**_

That explains it. `l2cap_vfs_read` is **non-blocking and never blocks**: empty queue → returns **0**; only a peer close returns **-1** (errno `EPIPE`). I wrongly treated `0` as EOF, so the reader bailed instantly. Fix: poll (0 = "no data yet, retry"), exit only on `< 0`. There's no `select` support on this VFS, so a short poll delay is the right approach.

**Read path works** — we're now receiving the Wii's output reports. Decoding what you captured on fd 4 (the data channel, PSM 0x13):

```
a2 17 00 00 17 70 00 01
│  │  └──────────────┘
│  │   payload: flags=0x00, addr=0x001770, size=0x0001
│  └ report 0x17 = "Read Memory/Registers" request
└ 0xa2 = host→device output report
```

So the Wii's first move is a **memory read**, and it's now **waiting for our `0x21` (Read Data) reply** before it proceeds — which is why you likely saw just that one frame (it's blocked on us). This is exactly the handshake entry point.

That confirms Phase 2a (read path) is done, and it lands us at the real work: the **Wiimote report state machine** (Phase 2b). To get a live, assigned controller we need to answer:
- `0x15` (status request) → send `0x20` status (battery, LEDs, extension flags)
- `0x17` (read) → send `0x21` read-data (calibration EEPROM, extension ID, etc.)
- `0x16` (write) → `0x22` ack
- `0x12` (reporting mode), `0x11` (LEDs) → store + ack
- then stream input reports (`0x30` core buttons)

This is a substantial new module — I'll model it on `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator`'s `wm_reports.c` (which I have locally) + wiibrew. It's the core emulation that Phases 2-3 build on.

```text
void report_queue_push_ack(struct wiimote_state *state, uint8_t report, uint8_t result)
{
  //push acknowledgement report x22
  struct report * rpt = report_queue_push(state);
  rpt->len = 6;
  rpt->data.io = 0xa1;
  rpt->data.type = 0x22;

  struct report_ack * ack = (struct report_ack *)rpt->data.buf;
  ack->report = report;
  ack->result = result;
}

void report_queue_push_status(struct wiimote_state * state)
{
  //push status report x20
  struct report * rpt = report_queue_push(state);
  rpt->len = 8;
  rpt->data.io = 0xa1;
  rpt->data.type = 0x20;

  struct report_status * status = (struct report_status *)rpt->data.buf;
  status->low_battery         = state->sys.low_battery;
  status->extension_connected = state->sys.extension_connected;
  status->speaker_enabled     = state->sys.speaker_enabled;
  status->ircam_enabled       = state->sys.ircam_enabled;
  status->led_1               = state->sys.led_1;
  status->led_2               = state->sys.led_2;
  status->led_3               = state->sys.led_3;
  status->led_4               = state->sys.led_4;
  status->battery_level       = state->sys.battery_level;
}

void report_format_mem_resp(struct wiimote_state * state, struct report * rpt,
  int size, int error, uint16_t addr, uint8_t * buf, bool encrypt)
{
  struct report_mem_resp * resp = (struct report_mem_resp *)rpt->data.buf;

  rpt->len = 23;
  rpt->data.io = 0xa1;
  rpt->data.type = 0x21;

  resp->size = size - 1;
  resp->error = error;
  resp->addr = htons(addr);
  if (buf != NULL) //buf will be null for error reports
  {
    memcpy(resp->data, buf, size);

    if (encrypt)
    {
      ext_encrypt_bytes(&state->sys.extension_crypto_state, resp->data, addr & 0x7, size);
    }
  }
}

void report_append_buttons(struct wiimote_state * state, uint8_t * buf)
{
  struct report_buttons * rpt = (struct report_buttons *)buf;

  rpt->left  = state->usr.left;
  rpt->right = state->usr.right;
  rpt->down  = state->usr.down;
  rpt->up    = state->usr.up;
  rpt->one   = state->usr.one;
  rpt->two   = state->usr.two;
  rpt->a     = state->usr.a;
  rpt->b     = state->usr.b;
  rpt->plus  = state->usr.plus;
  rpt->minus = state->usr.minus;
  rpt->home  = state->usr.home;
}
```

```c
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "esp_log.h"

#include "wiimote.h"

static const char *TAG = "fauxmote.wm";

#define EEPROM_SIZE       0x1700u   /* readable EEPROM range is 0x0000..0x16FF */
#define EEPROM_READ_MAX   0x16FFu
#define SENDER_PERIOD_MS  15
#define SENDER_STACK      3072

/* HID transaction prefixes (HIDP): host->device output, device->host input. */
#define HIDP_OUTPUT  0xA2
#define HIDP_INPUT   0xA1

static int     s_data_fd = -1;       /* the HID data channel (carries 0xa2 output reports) */
static uint8_t s_leds;               /* player LEDs (nibble), set by the Wii via report 0x11 */
static uint8_t s_rumble;
static bool    s_streaming;          /* true once the Wii has set a reporting mode (0x12) */
static uint8_t s_btn0, s_btn1;       /* core button state (0 = nothing pressed) */
static uint8_t s_eeprom[EEPROM_SIZE];

static StaticTask_t s_sender_tcb;
static StackType_t  s_sender_stack[SENDER_STACK];

/* Accelerometer calibration the Wii reads from EEPROM 0x16 (mirrored at 0x20).
 * Canonical zero-G 0x85 / 1G 0xA0 per axis + checksum (from a real RVL-CNT-01). */
static const uint8_t k_accel_cal[10] = {
    0x85, 0x85, 0x85, 0x00, 0xA0, 0xA0, 0xA0, 0x00, 0x40, 0x04,
};

static void wm_send(int fd, uint8_t report_id, const uint8_t *payload, int paylen)
{
    uint8_t frame[2 + 21];
    frame[0] = HIDP_INPUT;
    frame[1] = report_id;
    if (paylen > 0) {
        memcpy(frame + 2, payload, paylen);
    }
    write(fd, frame, 2 + paylen);
}

static void send_status(int fd)
{
    uint8_t p[6] = {0};
    p[0] = s_btn0;
    p[1] = s_btn1;
    p[2] = (uint8_t)(s_leds << 4);   /* flags: LEDs in 4..7; no extension/speaker/IR */
    p[5] = 0xC0;                     /* battery level (near full) */
    wm_send(fd, 0x20, p, sizeof(p));
}

static void send_ack(int fd, uint8_t report_id, uint8_t result)
{
    uint8_t p[4] = { s_btn0, s_btn1, report_id, result };
    wm_send(fd, 0x22, p, sizeof(p));
}

/* 0x21 read-data: size_minus1 in 0..15, error in low nibble, 16-bit addr, data. */
static void send_read_data(int fd, uint8_t size_minus1, uint8_t error, uint16_t addr,
                           const uint8_t *data)
{
    uint8_t p[21] = {0};
    p[0] = s_btn0;
    p[1] = s_btn1;
    p[2] = (uint8_t)((size_minus1 << 4) | (error & 0x0F));
    p[3] = (uint8_t)(addr >> 8);
    p[4] = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
    if (data) {
        memcpy(p + 5, data, size_minus1 + 1);
    }
    wm_send(fd, 0x21, p, sizeof(p));
}

static void read_eeprom(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
{
    if (size == 0 || offset + size > EEPROM_READ_MAX) {
        send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);   /* error: invalid address */
        return;
    }
    uint32_t addr = offset;
    uint16_t left = size;
    while (left > 0) {
        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, &s_eeprom[addr]);
        addr += chunk;
        left -= chunk;
    }
}

void Wiimote_HandleRx(int fd, const uint8_t *data, int len)
{
    if (len < 2 || data[0] != HIDP_OUTPUT) {
        return;   /* not a HID output report (e.g. control-channel HIDP transaction) */
    }
    s_data_fd = fd;                 /* this fd is the data channel — reply / stream here */
    uint8_t report = data[1];
    const uint8_t *p = data + 2;
    int plen = len - 2;
    if (plen >= 1) {
        s_rumble = p[0] & 0x01;     /* rumble bit rides the first payload byte of every report */
    }

    switch (report) {
    case 0x11:                      /* player LEDs */
        if (plen >= 1) s_leds = (p[0] >> 4) & 0x0F;
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x12:                      /* data reporting mode */
        s_streaming = true;
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x10:                      /* rumble only */
    case 0x13: case 0x1A:           /* IR camera enable */
    case 0x14: case 0x19:           /* speaker enable / mute */
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x15:                      /* status request */
        send_status(fd);
        break;
    case 0x16:                      /* write memory/registers */
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x17:                      /* read memory/registers */
        if (plen >= 6) {
            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
            uint16_t size = (uint16_t)((p[4] << 8) | p[5]);
            if (p[0] & 0x04) {      /* register space — no extension yet, report error */
                send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);
            } else {
                read_eeprom(fd, offset, size);
            }
        }
        break;
    default:
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    }
}

void Wiimote_NotifyFdClosed(int fd)
{
    if (fd == s_data_fd) {
        s_data_fd = -1;
        s_streaming = false;
    }
}

static void sender_task(void *arg)
{
    (void)arg;
    for (;;) {
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SENDER_PERIOD_MS));
        if (s_streaming && s_data_fd >= 0) {
            uint8_t p[2] = { s_btn0, s_btn1 };
            wm_send(s_data_fd, 0x30, p, sizeof(p));   /* core-buttons input report */
        }
    }
}

void Wiimote_Start(void)
{
    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x16], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x20], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
    xTaskCreateStatic(sender_task, "wm_tx", SENDER_STACK, NULL, 6,
                      s_sender_stack, &s_sender_tcb);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote report state machine started");
}

```

```
fauxmote.wm: Wiimote report state machine started

fauxmote.bt: fd N RX report 0x17 (8 B)     ← read (we reply 0x21)
fauxmote.bt: fd N RX report 0x15 (...)      ← status request (we reply 0x20)
fauxmote.bt: fd N RX report 0x11 (...)      ← LED assignment  ← we're accepted
fauxmote.bt: fd N RX report 0x12 (...)      ← reporting mode → we start streaming 0x30
```

**The milestone to watch on the hardware itself:**
- **A solid player-1 LED** on the "controller" (the Wii assigning us a slot via that `0x11` report) instead of the blinking sync pattern.
- **The connection stays up** (we now stream `0x30` every 15 ms, so the Wii sees activity and won't idle-drop us as fast).

Buttons aren't wired to anything yet (that's the Phase 4 command source), so the cursor won't move — but an *assigned, persistent* Wiimote is the Phase 2 win. In the Wii's "Wii Remote settings" screen it should show a connected remote in slot 1.

**This is working!** Look past the noise and the signal is excellent:

- `fd 4 RX report 0x17` → we replied (`L2CA_DataWrite ... Len 23` = our `0x21` read-data). ✓
- `fd 4 RX report 0x12` (set reporting mode) → ack (`Len 6` = our `0x22`). ✓
- `fd 4 RX report 0x1a` (enable IR) → ack. ✓
- The flood of **`L2CA_DataWrite ... Len 4`** = our **`0x30` button reports streaming**, and `BTA_JvL2capRead` shows **the Wii is consuming them**. ✓

The Wii setting a reporting mode + enabling IR and continuously reading our reports means it's **treating us as a live, assigned controller** — it wouldn't configure a rejected device. Phase 2 core is essentially done.

The "overwhelmed with messages" is two things, both noise: (1) the verbose Bluedroid debug logs I turned on for the SDP debugging, and (2) the per-write power-mode churn the stack logs at that level. We don't need them anymore — pairing + handshake work. Let me turn them off so you can actually watch:

```c
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "driver/gpio.h"

#include "wiimote.h"
#include "status_led.h"

#define LED_GPIO     GPIO_NUM_13   /* onboard red user LED on the Feather V2 */
#define LED_STACK    2048

static StaticTask_t s_tcb;
static StackType_t  s_stack[LED_STACK];

static void led_task(void *arg)
{
    (void)arg;
    gpio_reset_pin(LED_GPIO);
    gpio_set_direction(LED_GPIO, GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT);
    bool on = false;

    for (;;) {
        if (Wiimote_IsAssigned()) {
            gpio_set_level(LED_GPIO, 1);                 /* solid = assigned + live */
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(200));
        } else if (Wiimote_IsConnected()) {
            on = !on;
            gpio_set_level(LED_GPIO, on);                /* fast blink = connected */
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(120));
        } else {
            gpio_set_level(LED_GPIO, 1);                 /* slow heartbeat = waiting */
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(80));
            gpio_set_level(LED_GPIO, 0);
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(920));
        }
    }
}

void StatusLed_Start(void)
{
    xTaskCreateStatic(led_task, "status_led", LED_STACK, NULL, 3, s_stack, &s_tcb);
}

```

**Watch the red LED on the board:**
- **Slow heartbeat** (~1 blink/sec) = up and waiting for the Wii
- **Fast blink** = connected, mid-handshake
- **Solid on** = the Wii assigned us a player slot (received `0x11`) → live/assigned controller

And the monitor will finally be readable — just the boot lines, `L2CAP OPEN` ×2, `auth OK`, and a few `RX report 0x17/0x12/0x15/0x11/0x1a` during the handshake, then quiet.

So the test: press SYNC and watch the LED go **heartbeat → fast blink → solid**, and stay solid while connected. That's your "assigned and alive" indicator standing in for the Wiimote's player LED.

(One build note: if `esp_driver_gpio` isn't recognized in `REQUIRES`, change it to `driver` — the component got renamed across IDF versions and I picked the v6 name.)

If you want it *more* Wiimote-like later, the onboard NeoPixel (GPIO0, power on GPIO2) could show the actual slot number as a color — but the red LED is the robust first cut.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:08:03Z)**_

Good instinct — a manual test CLI before guitar will make everything downstream easier. Let me answer your questions precisely, since they determine the design:

## Reporting modes — how they work

**Yes, the Wii tells the Wiimote which mode to use** — via the output report **`0x12`** (which we already receive and ack). Its 2-byte payload is `[flags, mode]`:
- `flags` bit 2 (`0x04`) = *continuous* (report every poll vs. only on change)
- `mode` = the **report ID** the Wiimote must now send (`0x30`–`0x3f`)

The Wiimote doesn't choose — it **obeys the last `0x12`**, and the Wii can **change it at any time** (the system menu uses an IR-bearing mode for pointing; a game sets whatever it needs). So the contract is: Wii sets mode → we stream that report ID until it sets a different one.

The modes differ by payload: `0x30` = buttons only (2 B), `0x31` = +accel, `0x33` = +accel +12 IR bytes, `0x37` = +accel +10 IR +6 ext, `0x34` = buttons +19 ext (the guitar one), etc.

## How many do we support right now: effectively **one**

We **ignore the requested mode and always send `0x30`** (buttons only). That's why:
- **Buttons already work** in any mode (the Wii parses by report ID; A/B/+/−/Home/dpad register).
- **Pointer doesn't** — the menu sets a mode expecting **IR data**, and we never emit IR (or accel). No IR dots → no cursor.

So to "IR point at the Home screen," we need to (a) honor the requested mode, and (b) actually synthesize IR camera data (two dots from a pointer position) + a level accel for a stable cursor.

## Proposed plan (core Wiimote first, two steps)

**Step A — test CLI + honor reporting mode + buttons**
- Add an `esp_console` REPL over the USB serial: `btn a 1` / `tap home` / `dpad up`, etc. (it updates the shared button state the sender streams).
- Store mode + continuous from `0x12` (and log the mode byte so we see what the menu/game asks for); build & stream the *requested* report ID, populating buttons (accel/IR zeroed for now).
- Test: `tap home` opens the Home menu, button presses register.

**Step B — IR pointer emulation**
- Track IR enable/config (the `0x13`/`0x1a` + `0x16` register-`0xb0` writes we currently just ack), keep a pointer `(x,y)` set via CLI (`point 0.5 0.5`, `point off`), synthesize the two sensor-bar dots into the mode's IR format, and report a level accel.
- Test: point + `tap a` to actually navigate/select in the menu.

Then the guitar extension (Phase 3) slots in as "another report mode + extension registers."

I'd build **Step A first** (quick, proves the CLI + mode-honoring + buttons end-to-end), then **Step B** (IR). Sound good — start on Step A with `esp_console` for the CLI? Or would you rather a different command interface?

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>

```c
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "esp_log.h"

#include "wiimote.h"

static const char *TAG = "fauxmote.wm";

#define EEPROM_SIZE       0x1700u   /* readable EEPROM range is 0x0000..0x16FF */
#define EEPROM_READ_MAX   0x16FFu
#define SENDER_PERIOD_MS  15
#define SENDER_STACK      3072
#define ACCEL_NEUTRAL     0x85      /* zero-g raw value (matches the EEPROM calibration) */

/* HID transaction prefixes (HIDP): host->device output, device->host input. */
#define HIDP_OUTPUT  0xA2
#define HIDP_INPUT   0xA1

static int     s_data_fd = -1;       /* the HID data channel (carries 0xa2 output reports) */
static uint8_t s_leds;               /* player LEDs (nibble), set by the Wii via report 0x11 */
static uint8_t s_rumble;
static bool    s_streaming;          /* true once the Wii has set a reporting mode (0x12) */
static uint8_t s_report_mode = 0x30; /* report ID the Wii told us to send (default core buttons) */
static bool    s_reporting_continuous;
static uint8_t s_btn0, s_btn1;       /* core button state (0 = nothing pressed) */
static uint8_t s_eeprom[EEPROM_SIZE];

static StaticTask_t s_sender_tcb;
static StackType_t  s_sender_stack[SENDER_STACK];

/* Accelerometer calibration the Wii reads from EEPROM 0x16 (mirrored at 0x20).
 * Canonical zero-G 0x85 / 1G 0xA0 per axis + checksum (from a real RVL-CNT-01). */
static const uint8_t k_accel_cal[10] = {
    0x85, 0x85, 0x85, 0x00, 0xA0, 0xA0, 0xA0, 0x00, 0x40, 0x04,
};

/* Core button names → (byte index, bit mask) in the 2-byte button field. */
static const struct { const char *name; uint8_t byte; uint8_t mask; } k_buttons[] = {
    { "left",  0, 0x01 }, { "right", 0, 0x02 }, { "down", 0, 0x04 }, { "up", 0, 0x08 },
    { "plus",  0, 0x10 },
    { "two",   1, 0x01 }, { "one",   1, 0x02 }, { "b",    1, 0x04 }, { "a",  1, 0x08 },
    { "minus", 1, 0x10 }, { "home",  1, 0x80 },
};

static void wm_send(int fd, uint8_t report_id, const uint8_t *payload, int paylen)
{
    uint8_t frame[2 + 21];
    frame[0] = HIDP_INPUT;
    frame[1] = report_id;
    if (paylen > 0) {
        memcpy(frame + 2, payload, paylen);
    }
    write(fd, frame, 2 + paylen);
}

static void send_status(int fd)
{
    uint8_t p[6] = {0};
    p[0] = s_btn0;
    p[1] = s_btn1;
    p[2] = (uint8_t)(s_leds << 4);   /* flags: LEDs in 4..7; no extension/speaker/IR */
    p[5] = 0xC0;                     /* battery level (near full) */
    wm_send(fd, 0x20, p, sizeof(p));
}

static void send_ack(int fd, uint8_t report_id, uint8_t result)
{
    uint8_t p[4] = { s_btn0, s_btn1, report_id, result };
    wm_send(fd, 0x22, p, sizeof(p));
}

/* 0x21 read-data: size_minus1 in 0..15, error in low nibble, 16-bit addr, data. */
static void send_read_data(int fd, uint8_t size_minus1, uint8_t error, uint16_t addr,
                           const uint8_t *data)
{
    uint8_t p[21] = {0};
    p[0] = s_btn0;
    p[1] = s_btn1;
    p[2] = (uint8_t)((size_minus1 << 4) | (error & 0x0F));
    p[3] = (uint8_t)(addr >> 8);
    p[4] = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
    if (data) {
        memcpy(p + 5, data, size_minus1 + 1);
    }
    wm_send(fd, 0x21, p, sizeof(p));
}

static void read_eeprom(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
{
    if (size == 0 || offset + size > EEPROM_READ_MAX) {
        send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);   /* error: invalid address */
        return;
    }
    uint32_t addr = offset;
    uint16_t left = size;
    while (left > 0) {
        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, &s_eeprom[addr]);
        addr += chunk;
        left -= chunk;
    }
}

void Wiimote_HandleRx(int fd, const uint8_t *data, int len)
{
    if (len < 2 || data[0] != HIDP_OUTPUT) {
        return;   /* not a HID output report (e.g. control-channel HIDP transaction) */
    }
    s_data_fd = fd;                 /* this fd is the data channel — reply / stream here */
    uint8_t report = data[1];
    const uint8_t *p = data + 2;
    int plen = len - 2;
    if (plen >= 1) {
        s_rumble = p[0] & 0x01;     /* rumble bit rides the first payload byte of every report */
    }

    switch (report) {
    case 0x11:                      /* player LEDs */
        if (plen >= 1) s_leds = (p[0] >> 4) & 0x0F;
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x12:                      /* data reporting mode */
        if (plen >= 2) {
            s_reporting_continuous = (p[0] & 0x04) != 0;
            s_report_mode = p[1];
        }
        s_streaming = true;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "reporting mode 0x%02x (continuous=%d)", s_report_mode, s_reporting_continuous);
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x10:                      /* rumble only */
    case 0x13: case 0x1A:           /* IR camera enable */
    case 0x14: case 0x19:           /* speaker enable / mute */
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x15:                      /* status request */
        send_status(fd);
        break;
    case 0x16:                      /* write memory/registers */
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x17:                      /* read memory/registers */
        if (plen >= 6) {
            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
            uint16_t size = (uint16_t)((p[4] << 8) | p[5]);
            if (p[0] & 0x04) {      /* register space — no extension yet, report error */
                send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);
            } else {
                read_eeprom(fd, offset, size);
            }
        }
        break;
    default:
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    }
}

/* Build the input report the Wii's current mode expects: buttons in the first two
 * bytes (except 0x3d), neutral accelerometer where present, IR/extension zeroed
 * (filled in later phases). Returns the payload length, or 0 for an unknown mode. */
static int build_report(uint8_t mode, uint8_t *p)
{
    memset(p, 0, 21);
    if (mode != 0x3d) {
        p[0] = s_btn0;
        p[1] = s_btn1;
    }
    switch (mode) {
    case 0x30: return 2;
    case 0x31: p[2] = p[3] = p[4] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL; return 5;
    case 0x32: return 10;
    case 0x33: p[2] = p[3] = p[4] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL; return 17;
    case 0x34: return 21;
    case 0x35: p[2] = p[3] = p[4] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL; return 21;
    case 0x36: return 21;
    case 0x37: p[2] = p[3] = p[4] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL; return 21;
    case 0x3d: case 0x3e: case 0x3f: return 21;
    default:   return 0;
    }
}

bool Wiimote_SetButton(const char *name, bool pressed)
{
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_buttons) / sizeof(k_buttons[0]); i++) {
        if (strcmp(name, k_buttons[i].name) == 0) {
            uint8_t *b = (k_buttons[i].byte == 0) ? &s_btn0 : &s_btn1;
            if (pressed) {
                *b |= k_buttons[i].mask;
            } else {
                *b &= ~k_buttons[i].mask;
            }
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

void Wiimote_NotifyFdClosed(int fd)
{
    if (fd == s_data_fd) {
        s_data_fd = -1;
        s_streaming = false;
    }
}

bool Wiimote_IsConnected(void)  { return s_data_fd >= 0; }
bool Wiimote_IsAssigned(void)   { return s_leds != 0; }
uint8_t Wiimote_ReportMode(void) { return s_report_mode; }

static void sender_task(void *arg)
{
    (void)arg;
    uint8_t p[21];
    for (;;) {
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SENDER_PERIOD_MS));
        if (s_streaming && s_data_fd >= 0) {
            uint8_t mode = s_report_mode;
            int len = build_report(mode, p);
            if (len == 0) {                 /* unknown mode → fall back to core buttons */
                mode = 0x30;
                len = build_report(mode, p);
            }
            wm_send(s_data_fd, mode, p, len);
        }
    }
}

void Wiimote_Start(void)
{
    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x16], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x20], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
    xTaskCreateStatic(sender_task, "wm_tx", SENDER_STACK, NULL, 6,
                      s_sender_stack, &s_sender_tcb);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote report state machine started");
}
```

```text
84	static void hid_reader_task(void *arg)

93	        } else if (n == 0) {
94	            /* esp_bt_l2cap read is non-blocking: 0 = no data yet, so poll. */
95	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
96	        } else {
97	            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "fd %d closed (errno %d); reader exit", l->fd, errno);
98	            break;

101	    Wiimote_NotifyFdClosed(l->fd);
102	    l->in_use = false;
103	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "esp_console.h"
#include "esp_bt_device.h"

#include "console_cli.h"
#include "bt_hid_device.h"
#include "wiimote.h"

static void print_bda(const char *label, const uint8_t *bda)
{
    if (bda) {
        printf("%s %02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x\n", label,
               bda[0], bda[1], bda[2], bda[3], bda[4], bda[5]);
    } else {
        printf("%s (none)\n", label);
    }
}

static int cmd_pair(int argc, char **argv)
{
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    Fauxmote_EnterPairing();
    printf("pairing mode ON — press the Wii's red SYNC button now\n");
    return 0;
}

static int cmd_stop(int argc, char **argv)
{
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    Fauxmote_StopPairing();
    printf("pairing mode OFF\n");
    return 0;
}

static int cmd_reconnect(int argc, char **argv)
{
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    Fauxmote_Reconnect();
    return 0;
}

static int cmd_status(int argc, char **argv)
{
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    print_bda("bd_addr   ", esp_bt_dev_get_address());
    print_bda("bonded Wii", Fauxmote_WiiAddr());
    printf("discoverable=%d connected=%d assigned=%d report_mode=0x%02x\n",
           Fauxmote_IsDiscoverable(), Wiimote_IsConnected(), Wiimote_IsAssigned(),
           Wiimote_ReportMode());
    return 0;
}

static int cmd_btn(int argc, char **argv)
{
    if (argc < 3) {
        printf("usage: btn <a|b|one|two|plus|minus|home|up|down|left|right> <0|1>\n");
        return 1;
    }
    bool pressed = atoi(argv[2]) != 0;
    if (!Wiimote_SetButton(argv[1], pressed)) {
        printf("unknown button '%s'\n", argv[1]);
        return 1;
    }
    printf("%s %s\n", argv[1], pressed ? "down" : "up");
    return 0;
}

static int cmd_tap(int argc, char **argv)
{
    if (argc < 2) {
        printf("usage: tap <button>\n");
        return 1;
    }
    if (!Wiimote_SetButton(argv[1], true)) {
        printf("unknown button '%s'\n", argv[1]);
        return 1;
    }
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(120));
    Wiimote_SetButton(argv[1], false);
    printf("tapped %s\n", argv[1]);
    return 0;
}

static void register_cmd(const char *name, const char *help, esp_console_cmd_func_t fn)
{
    const esp_console_cmd_t cmd = { .command = name, .help = help, .hint = NULL, .func = fn };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_console_cmd_register(&cmd));
}

void Cli_Start(void)
{
    esp_console_repl_t *repl = NULL;
    esp_console_repl_config_t repl_config = ESP_CONSOLE_REPL_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    repl_config.prompt = "fauxmote>";
    esp_console_dev_uart_config_t uart_config = ESP_CONSOLE_DEV_UART_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_console_new_repl_uart(&uart_config, &repl_config, &repl));

    register_cmd("pair", "enter pairing/sync mode (then press the Wii SYNC button)", cmd_pair);
    register_cmd("stop", "leave pairing mode (idle)", cmd_stop);
    register_cmd("reconnect", "device-initiated reconnect to the last bonded Wii", cmd_reconnect);
    register_cmd("status", "show BT / connection state", cmd_status);
    register_cmd("btn", "btn <name> <0|1> — hold/release a button", cmd_btn);
    register_cmd("tap", "tap <name> — brief press+release", cmd_tap);
    esp_console_register_help_command();

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_console_start_repl(repl));
}
```

Confirmed in the IDF source — `btc_storage` saves the classic **LINK_KEY to NVS** and reloads bonded devices at boot (`BTA_DmAddDevice` with the stored key). So:

**Yes — the *bond itself* (the pairing link key) is kept in NVS automatically by the Bluetooth stack.** After a reboot/power-cycle you do **not** need to re-PIN-pair; the cryptographic pairing is remembered. (That's what `nvs_flash_init()` in `main.c` is partly for.)

**But two app-level gaps:**
1. Our record of *which Wii* (`s_wii_bda`) is **RAM-only** — so after a reboot, `status`/`reconnect` forget the address until you `pair` again, even though the stack still holds the link key.
2. We don't auto-reconnect on boot.

The clean fix for #1 is to not store it ourselves at all — ask the stack, since it already reloaded the bond from NVS. Let me wire that in so `reconnect` survives a power-cycle:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:25:30Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:25:37Z)**_

Yes — a normal reflash keeps it. Here's the precise breakdown:

- **`idf.py flash` (what you've been running):** writes only the bootloader, partition table, and the **app** partition. It does **not** touch the **NVS** partition (where the bond/link key lives), so **the pairing survives reflashing.** You can iterate on firmware all day and stay bonded.

- **What *does* wipe it:**
  - `idf.py erase-flash` (or esptool `erase_flash`) — erases the whole chip including NVS → bond gone, re-pair needed.
  - `idf.py erase-otadata` / `erase-nvs`-style targeted erases.
  - Changing the **partition table** (offsets/sizes) so NVS moves or is reinitialized.
  - `nvs_flash_init()` only erases NVS if it's *full* or the layout version changed — not on a normal boot, so that won't bite you.

One caveat worth knowing: the bond is **two-sided**. The Wii also stores us in its sync registry. A normal reflash keeps *our* link key and the Wii keeps *its*, so `reconnect` works. But if you ever full-erase the ESP32 (wiping our key) while the Wii still has us registered, the keys won't match — you'd `pair` + SYNC again to re-establish both sides.

So: routine `idf.py flash` → bond persists and `reconnect` keeps working across reflashes; only a deliberate full erase or partition-table change resets it. (And if you *want* a deliberate reset without erasing everything, that's the `unpair`/`esp_bt_gap_remove_bond_device` command I offered — just say the word.)

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:34:54Z)**_

Both are real gaps — good catches.

**1. Turn off discovery once connected** — yes. A real Wiimote stops advertising after it's connected. I'll switch to `CONNECTABLE + NON_DISCOVERABLE` on the L2CAP open (stays reachable for reconnects, but no longer shows up in inquiry scans).

**2. Disconnect cleanup** — the log shows the teardown works (both channels close, readers exit on `errno 9`=EBADF, ACL drops), but two things aren't handled:
- **State isn't reset:** we never clear `s_leds`, so `IsAssigned()` stays true → the LED would stay solid after the Wii's gone. And buttons/taps linger.
- **The `bta_jv_l2cap_write() ... p_cback == NULL` error** is our report sender writing one last `0x30` into the dying channel during the ~10 ms window before the reader exits and clears `s_data_fd`. Benign, but avoidable by stopping the stream the instant we see the close.

Fix: handle the L2CAP `CLOSE` event immediately (stop streaming + reset state), so the sender halts at once and the LED returns to idle.

Both handled. Net behavior now:

- **Discovery turns off on connect** — once a HID channel opens we go `CONNECTABLE + NON_DISCOVERABLE`, so we stop appearing in inquiry scans but stay reachable for reconnects. `status` will show `discoverable=0` once connected.
- **Clean disconnect** — the L2CAP `CLOSE` event now immediately calls `Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected()`: stops the report stream, clears LEDs/buttons/pending taps. So when the Wii powers off, the LED drops back to **idle (off)**, state is reset for the next session, and the `bta_jv_l2cap_write ... p_cback == NULL` error should be gone (or down to a rare single line, since the sender now halts the instant the close fires rather than ~10 ms later when the reader exits).

After a disconnect you're left bonded + connectable-but-not-discoverable, so you can `reconnect` (device-initiated) or just `pair` again.

4. `unlink` → `status` shows no bonded Wii.

```text
static void btc_l2cap_start_srv(btc_l2cap_args_t *arg)
```

The direction matters here: during sync the **Wii connects to us** (we're the L2CAP *server* on 0x11/0x13), but our `reconnect` does a *client* connect on those same PSMs — and in Bluedroid a client connect registers the PSM as *outgoing-only*, which shadows the server. So after a reconnect (or possibly any connection cycle) the server can't accept the Wii's next sync. Let me confirm whether the server slot also gets consumed on accept:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:50:29Z)**_

That's the smoking gun. Reading the stack: on `BTA_JV_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT` the **listening server slot itself becomes the connection** (`slot->connected = TRUE` on the same slot) — so once the Wii connects, our `start_srv` listeners on 0x11/0x13 are **consumed**, and on close they're freed. We only `start_srv` once (at boot), so after any connection cycle there's no listener for the next pair → the Wii's conn req gets rejected, and only a reboot (which re-runs `start_srv`) recovers. (The `reconnect` client-connect makes it worse by leaving an outgoing-only registration, which is the exact "outgoing-only PSM 17" wording.)

Fix: **re-arm the HID servers after a full disconnect.** I'll count open HID channels and restart both servers when the count returns to zero (which also covers the reconnect case, since those connections close through the same path).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:51:53Z)**_

Fixed. The HID server slots are consumed when the Wii connects, so I now **re-arm them on full disconnect**: a counter tracks open HID channels, and when it hits zero (both channels closed) `start_hid_servers()` re-registers PSM 0x11/0x13 as fresh listeners. This covers both paths — a Wii-initiated connection ending, and a `reconnect` client-connection ending (which is what left the "outgoing-only" registration). No reboot needed anymore.

Build/test (source-only):
```sh
idf.py build flash monitor
```

Re-run your repro plus a couple of cycle tests:
1. `pair` + SYNC → assigned (1 flash). Turn Wii off → log shows `fully disconnected — re-arming HID servers`, LED → idle blip.
2. `pair` + SYNC again → should connect **without a reboot** now.
3. `unlink` → `pair` + SYNC → re-bonds cleanly.
4. Bonus: `reconnect` after a disconnect, then later `pair` — should also still work (the re-arm clears the outgoing-only state).

One caveat to be aware of: if you `unlink` while *still connected* (no disconnect first), the servers are still consumed until the link drops — so do an `unlink` after the Wii has disconnected, or I can make `unlink` force a disconnect if you find that flow useful.

If all four cycles work without a reset, that closes the bug and I'll fold it into the Step A commit (still holding until you confirm). What does the `reporting mode 0x..` line show when you pair, by the way? — that's the one data point I still want before building the IR pointer.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 14:56:11Z)**_

Two things in that log — one bug, one great data point.

**The data point:** `report_mode=0x33` — that's exactly what I needed for the IR pointer. Mode `0x33` = core buttons + accelerometer + **12 IR bytes (extended IR)**. So Step B needs to fill accel + 2 synthesized IR dots in that format.

**The bug:** `connected=1 assigned=0` after disconnect — `Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected()` clears LEDs/buttons/streaming but **not `s_data_fd`**, and `IsConnected()` is `s_data_fd >= 0`. I only clear `s_data_fd` in `Wiimote_NotifyFdClosed()` when the *data-channel* reader exits — and that reader (fd 4) hadn't exited yet (only fd 3's did). So we still looked "connected," and the LED would stay on the fast-blink "connecting" pattern instead of idle. Fix: clear `s_data_fd` immediately in `Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected()`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 15:02:57Z)**_

Now I see the real failure cascade, and it traces back to my re-arm fix interacting badly with the reader tasks:

1. On disconnect I re-arm the servers immediately — which allocates **new** VFS fds that can **reuse** the just-freed fd numbers.
2. The per-fd reader tasks decide to exit by watching `read()` return `-1`. But if a re-armed server grabbed the old reader's fd number, `read()` now returns `0` (new empty server) forever → that reader **never exits** → its link slot stays `in_use`.
3. With only 2 slots, the leaked slot means the next connection's second channel gets **"no free HID link slot for fd 6"** → reconnect half-fails.

So readers must exit **deterministically on their own channel's close**, not by guessing from `read()`. Fix: tag each link with its L2CAP `handle`, and have the `CLOSE` event signal that exact reader to stop. Let me also bump the slot pool for margin.

Now I see the deeper leak — and it's my auto-re-arm logic, not just the reader. The `btc_l2cap_connect unable to malloc L2CAP slot!` means Bluedroid's L2CAP slot pool is exhausted. Tracing it:

**I re-arm 2 servers on *every* disconnect. But `reconnect` uses *client* connects, so those re-armed *server* slots never get consumed — they just sit there listening. Each power-cycle adds 2 more idle server slots → pool exhausted after ~4-5 cycles.**

The fix is a cleaner model that matches how a real Wiimote actually works:
- **Servers (listeners) exist only during a `pair` window** — armed in `EnterPairing`, torn down in `StopPairing`. Once the Wii connects, they're consumed; on disconnect they're already freed. No idle accumulation.
- **Reconnect is device-initiated** (client connect) — needs no servers.
- **No auto-re-arm on disconnect.**

This also fixes "pair after disconnect" (pair re-arms fresh each time) without leaking. Let me restructure:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 15:17:49Z)**_

Restructured. The model now matches a real Wiimote and can't accumulate slots:

- **`pair`** → arms the two HID listeners + becomes discoverable (for this sync window).
- **`stop`** → tears down any armed listeners + idle.
- **Connect** → listeners are consumed; **disconnect** → freed. No auto-re-arm, so nothing piles up.
- **`reconnect`** → device-initiated client connect (no listeners involved); its slots free on close.

So each `pair` arms exactly 2 (consumed on connect), and `reconnect` uses transient client slots — steady-state, no leak. Removed the connection counter and the boot/disconnect server-arming.

Build/test:
```sh
idf.py build flash monitor
```

The stress test that was failing:
1. Repeat **many** `pair` → SYNC → assigned → Wii off → idle cycles. Should never exhaust slots or get stuck.
2. Repeat `reconnect` cycles after power-cycles — no more `unable to malloc L2CAP slot`.
3. `unlink` → `pair` still works.

Two caveats to keep in mind while testing:
- After a disconnect you're **idle with no listeners** (by design). To get back: `reconnect` (device-initiated) or `pair`+SYNC. The Wii won't reconnect to us on its own (it never does — the controller always initiates).
- **`reconnect` still has the ERTM/Basic-mode gap** I flagged (`l2c_fcr_adj_our_req_options ... BASIC mode`). It may connect but not fully behave, since the Wii's HID wants ERTM. If it's flaky, `pair`+SYNC is the reliable path; making device-initiated reconnect use ERTM is a separate fix (matters later for Marvin's auto-reconnect, not for core function now).

If the cycle stress test holds up (no slot exhaustion, no stuck state, no reboot needed), that closes out Step A and I'll commit it. Then Step B: the IR pointer for mode `0x33`.

```bash
  tears them down. Servers are armed per-pairing-window (not at boot / not auto-
  re-armed) — re-arming leaked Bluedroid L2CAP slots because device-initiated
  reconnect uses client connects that never consume the listeners.
- Honor the Wii's requested reporting mode (0x12): stream the requested report ID
  with buttons populated (accel/IR/ext zeroed for now). Wii menu uses 0x33.
- Wiimote_SetButton / Wiimote_TapButton (non-blocking; sender auto-releases taps).
- Bond persists in NVS; recalled at boot via esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list;
  `unlink` removes it (esp_bt_gap_remove_bond_device).
- Clean disconnect: Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected resets state immediately; HID readers
  exit by L2CAP handle (robust to fd reuse).
- status_led.c (GPIO13): blip every ~3 s = idle, fast blink = pairing/connecting,
  N flashes = assigned player N.

Known limitation: device-initiated `reconnect` connects in Basic L2CAP mode while
the Wii's HID expects ERTM, so it may misbehave; reliable reconnection is pair+SYNC.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -1
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 15:57:31Z)**_

Reason code `0x08` = **link supervision timeout** (the link lost contact), and right before it you see `hci cmd send: sniff` — the link dropped into **sniff (low-power) mode** and then timed out. Bluedroid's JV power-management puts the link into sniff during brief idle (earlier verbose logs showed constant sniff/unsniff churn on every write), and that's destabilizing the link. For a controller — especially a rhythm game — we want the link pinned **active**, not sniffing. Let me check what ESP-IDF exposes to control this:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 15:57:39Z)**_

That `0x08` after `hci cmd send: sniff` is the key. My read:

**The GH3 disconnect is most likely because GH3 won't engage a plain Wiimote — it's waiting for the *guitar extension*.** In the Wii menu the link survived for minutes because the menu actively polls the pointer; at GH3's controller check, neither side has reason to send traffic (it wants a guitar), the link goes idle, Bluedroid's power-mgmt drops it into **sniff**, and with no packets flowing it hits the **supervision timeout** (`rsn 0x08`). So this is really "Phase 3 isn't built yet" showing up as a link drop.

Two supporting points:
- The pointer **works** — you navigated to and launched GH3 with `point`/`tap`, so Step B (IR cursor) is verified on hardware. 
- Sniff has **no clean public disable** in ESP-IDF (only `esp_bt_gap_set_acl_pkt_types`, which doesn't help); it's driven by Bluedroid's internal JV power-mgmt. But it only bites on an *idle* link — during real gameplay GH3 polls the guitar continuously, so the link won't idle. If it still bites after Phase 3, the fallback is an IDF-internal PM patch to pin the link active.

So the productive next move is **Phase 3: the guitar extension** — which is required for GH3 to do anything *and* should resolve this disconnect (once GH3 detects the guitar it actively polls it, keeping the link alive). It means:
- Report a connected extension in the `0x20` status (extension bit)
- Serve the extension register bank: ID `00 00 A4 20 01 03` at `0xa400fa`, handle the init writes (`0x55`→`0xf0`, `0x00`→`0xfb`) via the register-space `0x16`/`0x17` we currently stub to error
- Stream report `0x34` (core + 19 ext bytes) with the 6-byte guitar payload (frets/strum/whammy) — driven by `Wiimote_SetButton`-style setters so the CLI (and later Marvin) can exercise it

Want me to **commit Step B (IR pointer)** and **start Phase 3 (guitar extension)**? That's the path to actually playing GH3.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 16:15:48Z)**_

That's the missing piece — it reframes everything:

1. **A real Wiimote's LED goes off ~1 s at game start, then comes back.** So the Wii *does* briefly drop the link when launching GH3 (it reinitializes Bluetooth as the game disc boots), and a real Wiimote **auto-reconnects** (that's the `HIDReconnectInitiate=true` we advertise — the *controller* re-initiates and the LED returns). So your very first instinct was correct.

2. **fauxmote doesn't auto-reconnect, and worse — after that drop it can't reconnect at all without a power-cycle.** And a fresh-booted fauxmote *can* connect to an already-running game. So the post-disconnect state is leaving something stuck in the BT stack that a reboot clears.

So there are two things to build, and they're the real "core Wiimote" gap:
- **Make reconnect work after a disconnect without rebooting** (fix the stuck state).
- **Auto-reconnect on an unexpected drop** (retry device-initiated reconnect, like a real Wiimote), so the game-start blip just self-heals.

The "needs a power-cycle" part is the crux, and I don't want to guess at the leftover state — one targeted log will pin it. **After GH3 disconnects fauxmote, without rebooting, run `reconnect` and paste the output.** That failed-reconnect log shows exactly what's stuck (stale ACL, slot not freed, Wii rejecting, etc.) versus the fresh-boot reconnect that works — and tells me whether the fix is state cleanup on our side, an ERTM/mode issue, or the Wii holding a half-open link.

Once I see that, the plan is: fix reconnect so it's repeatable without a reboot → then add auto-reconnect-with-retry on unexpected disconnect so the ~1 s game-start drop heals itself like a real Wiimote. (The guitar extension is still needed for actual gameplay, but this link-stability fix is the blocker in front of it.)

Can you grab that `reconnect`-after-GH3-disconnect log?

This log is gold — the reconnect actually *opened both channels and the Wii sent us `0x17`*, but two new errors expose the real culprit:

```
W BT_APPL: bta_jv_alloc_set_pm_profile_cb(jv_handle: 0x1, app_id: 1) return NULL
W BT_APPL: bta_jv_alloc_set_pm_profile_cb() failed
```

The **BTA power-management profile pool (max 5) is exhausted** — each connection allocates a PM profile (for sniff), and an abnormal disconnect (`rsn 0x08` supervision timeout) doesn't free it cleanly. So every sniff-timeout disconnect **leaks a PM slot**, and after a few you can't fully reconnect → power-cycle needed. And the disconnect itself (`sniff` → 15 s later `rsn 0x08`) is the **idle sniff timeout**, also a PM/sniff artifact.

So **sniff is the single root cause** of both problems: the supervision timeouts *and* the PM-slot leak. Kill sniff → link stays active (Wii polls us, no timeout) and no PM profiles get allocated/leaked. We're USB-powered, so there's zero downside to staying active. Now it all fits together — and the fix is cornered into Bluedroid internals. Here's the complete picture:

- The idle→sniff delay for our link is **5 s** (`BTA_FTC_OPS_IDLE_TO_SNIFF_DELAY_MS`). When our report stream pauses (e.g., GH3 stops polling a guitar-less Wiimote), the link idles, sniffs, and supervision-times-out (`rsn 0x08`).
- Each abnormal (timeout) disconnect **leaks a BTA power-management slot** (`bta_jv_alloc_set_pm_profile_cb ... return NULL`); the pool is only 5, so after a few drops you can't fully reconnect → the **power-cycle requirement** you saw.
- **Disabling sniff fixes both**: the link stays active (Wii keeps polling it → no timeout), and with no timeouts, no PM-slot leak.

The catch: the sniff config (`bta_dm_pm_spec`) is a **`const` table**, BTA issues *explicit* sniff commands (so `BTM_SetLinkPolicy` won't stop it), and ESP-IDF's `bdroid_buildcfg.h` override isn't wired into the build. So there's **no public or repo-local way to disable it** — it needs a one-line change to the ESP-IDF Bluedroid source (set the JV power-mgmt spec to never sniff). Separately, we also want **auto-reconnect** so the deliberate ~1 s game-start drop self-heals like a real Wiimote.

Great question — and the answer to "extend the sniff delay" is **yes, and it's the clean way to do it** (no editing the ESP-IDF source). Let me explain both, then check one detail.

**Auto-reconnect alone:** it heals a drop, but it doesn't stop the *cause*. Each sniff-timeout drop leaks a power-mgmt slot (pool of 5), so after a few reconnect cycles you'd still hit the power-cycle wall. So auto-reconnect is necessary but not sufficient on its own.

**Extending the sniff delay:** the delay is a `#define` (`BTA_FTC_OPS_IDLE_TO_SNIFF_DELAY_MS = 5000`) guarded by `#ifndef` — so I can override it with a **compiler `-D` flag from our CMake** (clean, repo-local, no touching the IDF tree). Push it from 5 s to something huge and the link effectively never idles into sniff → no supervision timeout → no PM-slot leak. That's the same end result as patching the const table, but done properly from our project.

- **fauxmote:** tap A → *many seconds* of nothing → eventually drops (`rsn 0x08`) → reconnects.

```text
70	| 2026-06-12 | **`esp_hidd` is a dead end for Wii emulation; the only working ESP-IDF path is a custom SDP record (internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) + raw L2CAP HID on PSM 0x11/0x13 (`esp_bt_l2cap`), with the hardcoded SDP buffer raised.** Two independent walls: (1) the Wii rejects esp_hidd's record even with a small descriptor (wrong HID attribute values — subclass/reconnect-initiate/etc., which esp_hidd hardcodes and doesn't expose); (2) the real 217-byte descriptor can't even be registered — `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` (the per-record attribute pad) is **hardcoded 300** (`sdp_db.c:495`, `bluedroid_user_config.h`; no menuconfig), and the full Wiimote record is ~463 B → `SDP_AddAttribute fail … ID 518`. Confirmed feasible building blocks in IDF v6.0.1: `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/`SDP_AddSequence` (private `stack/sdp_api.h`) and `esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(psm)`. | Bluedroid is the only Classic-BT stack on ESP32, and its public APIs can't host an arbitrary SDP record (`esp_sdp` RAW is search-only). So the path requires *unsupported internals*: raise `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` via an injected `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN` compile define, build the exact Wiimote record with the internal SDP DB API, skip esp_hidd, and serve HID over raw L2CAP + hand-rolled HIDP. Heavy + fragile across IDF updates, but it's the real route. The exact 463-byte record + 217-byte descriptor are saved at [`wiimote-sdp.md`](wiimote-sdp.md). |
```

```bash
git add firmware/fauxmote && git diff --cached --name-only | grep fauxmote && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
fauxmote: link stability — disable sniff (idle timeouts) + persistent auto-reconnect

Idle disconnects were Bluedroid sniff: the link idled into sniff, hit a supervision
timeout (rsn 0x08), and abnormal closes leaked BTA power-mgmt slots (pool of 5),
eventually forcing a power-cycle to reconnect. The sniff config is a const table with
no public override, but the JV idle->sniff delay is an #ifndef'd #define, so override
it to 65 s via a global -D in the top-level CMake (idf_build_set_property before
project(); the timeout field is UINT16 with a +197 ms offset, so keep < ~65338).
With sniff effectively off the link stays active, the Wii keeps polling it, and there
are no supervision timeouts or PM-slot leaks.

Also add a persistent auto-reconnect task: on any unexpected drop it re-initiates the
device-side connection (3 s x8, then every 8 s), suppressed by stop/unlink, cleared
once the Wii is talking to us again. Heals drops like a real Wiimote.

Known-open and documented in the journal: the GH3 game-launch handoff still drops the
link and isn't reliably usable after reconnect (the Wii goes HID-silent then drops;
fauxmote's logs don't show why). Needs a BT sniffer to diff vs a real Wiimote.
Workaround: restart fauxmote after the game starts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote/Extension_Controllers/Guitar_Hero_(Wii)_Guitars`

```text
# Guitar Hero Guitar Extension Data Format

## Extension ID Bytes
At register 0x(4)a400fa: **00 00 A4 20 01 03** (first byte 00 = guitar; 01 = drums)

## 6-Byte Data Layout (After Decryption)

| Byte | Bit 7 | Bit 6 | Bit 5 | Bit 4 | Bit 3 | Bit 2 | Bit 1 | Bit 0 |
|------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| 0 | GH3 | GH3 | SX | — | — | — | — | — |
| 1 | GH3 | GH3 | SY | — | — | — | — | — |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | TB | — | — | — | — |
| 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | WB | — | — | — | — |
| 4 | 1 | BD | 1 | B- | 1 | B+ | 1 | 1 |
| 5 | BO | BR | BB | BG | BY | PB | 1 | BU |

**Legend:** SX/SY = analog stick; TB = touchbar; WB = whammy bar; BG/BR/BY/BB/BO = fret buttons; B+/B- = plus/minus; BU/BD = strum up/down; PB = pedal button

Buttons are **active-high** (1 = pressed).

## Encryption & Initialization

Standard GH3 init writes 0 to 0x(4)a40040, producing **encrypted** data. For GHWT/3rd-party guitars, write 0x55 to 0x(4)a400f0, then 0 to 0x(4)a400fb to disable encryption and read identification bytes.
```
</details></tool-use>

Committed the link-stability work (`7968ced`) and the full Phase 3 spec (`04c4764`). 

**Phase 3 plan — and the one wrinkle you should know about going in:** it splits naturally into two parts:

- **3a — Framework (gets GH3 to *detect* a guitar):** set the extension-connected bit in the status report, serve the extension register bank (ID `00 00 A4 20 01 03`), handle the init register writes, stream report `0x34` with the 6-byte guitar payload, and add CLI setters (`fret g/r/y/b/o`, `strum up/down`, `whammy`). Testable on its own — GH3 should recognize a guitar is plugged in.

- **3b — Encryption (gets GH3 to actually *read the notes*):** GH3's Les Paul uses the **encrypted** extension protocol (it writes `0` to `0xa40040` and expects ciphertext). So with 3a alone GH3 will *detect* the guitar but read garbage for the buttons. I'll port the standard Wii extension cipher (`wm_crypto`) so the note data decodes correctly. This is the meatier, more delicate piece.

Both are spec'd in the journal now, so it's ready to build.
