55	    { "two",   1, 0x01 }, { "one",   1, 0x02 }, { "b",    1, 0x04 }, { "a",  1, 0x08 },
56	    { "minus", 1, 0x10 }, { "home",  1, 0x80 },
57	};
58	
59	/* Momentary taps: Wiimote_TapButton presses now and schedules a release that the
60	 * sender task applies, so callers (CLI, Marvin) don't block. */
61	#define TAP_SLOTS  4
62	#define TAP_MS     120
63	static struct { uint8_t byte; uint8_t mask; TickType_t release_at; bool active; } s_taps[TAP_SLOTS];
64	
65	static const wm_button_t *find_button(const char *name)
66	{
67	    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_buttons) / sizeof(k_buttons[0]); i++) {
68	        if (strcmp(name, k_buttons[i].name) == 0) return &k_buttons[i];
69	    }
70	    return NULL;
71	}
72	
73	static void apply_button(const wm_button_t *b, bool pressed)
74	{
75	    uint8_t *p = (b->byte == 0) ? &s_btn0 : &s_btn1;
76	    if (pressed) *p |= b->mask; else *p &= ~b->mask;
77	}
78	
79	static void wm_send(int fd, uint8_t report_id, const uint8_t *payload, int paylen)
80	{
81	    uint8_t frame[2 + 21];
82	    frame[0] = HIDP_INPUT;
83	    frame[1] = report_id;
84	    if (paylen > 0) {
85	        memcpy(frame + 2, payload, paylen);
86	    }
87	    write(fd, frame, 2 + paylen);
88	}
89	
90	static void send_status(int fd)
91	{
92	    uint8_t p[6] = {0};
93	    p[0] = s_btn0;
94	    p[1] = s_btn1;
95	    p[2] = (uint8_t)(s_leds << 4);   /* flags: LEDs in 4..7; no extension/speaker/IR */
96	    p[5] = 0xC0;                     /* battery level (near full) */
97	    wm_send(fd, 0x20, p, sizeof(p));
98	}
99	
100	static void send_ack(int fd, uint8_t report_id, uint8_t result)
101	{
102	    uint8_t p[4] = { s_btn0, s_btn1, report_id, result };
103	    wm_send(fd, 0x22, p, sizeof(p));
104	}
105	
106	/* 0x21 read-data: size_minus1 in 0..15, error in low nibble, 16-bit addr, data. */
107	static void send_read_data(int fd, uint8_t size_minus1, uint8_t error, uint16_t addr,
108	                           const uint8_t *data)
109	{
110	    uint8_t p[21] = {0};
111	    p[0] = s_btn0;
112	    p[1] = s_btn1;
113	    p[2] = (uint8_t)((size_minus1 << 4) | (error & 0x0F));
114	    p[3] = (uint8_t)(addr >> 8);
115	    p[4] = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
116	    if (data) {
117	        memcpy(p + 5, data, size_minus1 + 1);
118	    }
119	    wm_send(fd, 0x21, p, sizeof(p));
120	}
121	
122	static void read_eeprom(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
123	{
124	    if (size == 0 || offset + size > EEPROM_READ_MAX) {
125	        send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);   /* error: invalid address */
126	        return;
127	    }
128	    uint32_t addr = offset;
129	    uint16_t left = size;
130	    while (left > 0) {
131	        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
132	        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, &s_eeprom[addr]);
133	        addr += chunk;
134	        left -= chunk;
135	    }
136	}
137	
138	void Wiimote_HandleRx(int fd, const uint8_t *data, int len)
139	{
140	    if (len < 2 || data[0] != HIDP_OUTPUT) {
141	        return;   /* not a HID output report (e.g. control-channel HIDP transaction) */
142	    }
143	    s_data_fd = fd;                 /* this fd is the data channel — reply / stream here */
144	    uint8_t report = data[1];
145	    const uint8_t *p = data + 2;
146	    int plen = len - 2;
147	    if (plen >= 1) {
148	        s_rumble = p[0] & 0x01;     /* rumble bit rides the first payload byte of every report */
149	    }
150	
151	    switch (report) {
152	    case 0x11:                      /* player LEDs */
153	        if (plen >= 1) s_leds = (p[0] >> 4) & 0x0F;
154	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
155	        break;
156	    case 0x12:                      /* data reporting mode */
157	        if (plen >= 2) {
158	            s_reporting_continuous = (p[0] & 0x04) != 0;
159	            s_report_mode = p[1];
160	        }
161	        s_streaming = true;
162	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "reporting mode 0x%02x (continuous=%d)", s_report_mode, s_reporting_continuous);
163	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
164	        break;
165	    case 0x10:                      /* rumble only */
166	    case 0x13: case 0x1A:           /* IR camera enable */
167	    case 0x14: case 0x19:           /* speaker enable / mute */
168	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
169	        break;
170	    case 0x15:                      /* status request */
171	        send_status(fd);
172	        break;
173	    case 0x16:                      /* write memory/registers */
174	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
175	        break;
176	    case 0x17:                      /* read memory/registers */
177	        if (plen >= 6) {
178	            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
179	            uint16_t size = (uint16_t)((p[4] << 8) | p[5]);
180	            if (p[0] & 0x04) {      /* register space — no extension yet, report error */
181	                send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);
182	            } else {
183	                read_eeprom(fd, offset, size);
184	            }
185	        }
186	        break;
187	    default:
188	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
189	        break;
190	    }
191	}
192	
193	static void set_accel_level(uint8_t *a)
194	{
195	    a[0] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* X = 0 g */
196	    a[1] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* Y = 0 g */
197	    a[2] = 0xA0;            /* Z = +1 g (held level, no roll) */
198	}
199	
200	/* One extended-IR object: X/Y are 10-bit camera coords (1024x768), or x<0 = "not
201	 * visible". 3rd byte packs Y[9:8], X[9:8], size. */
202	static void put_ir_object(uint8_t *o, int x, int y, int size)
203	{
204	    if (x < 0) {
205	        o[0] = o[1] = o[2] = 0xFF;
206	        return;
207	    }
208	    o[0] = (uint8_t)(x & 0xFF);
209	    o[1] = (uint8_t)(y & 0xFF);
210	    o[2] = (uint8_t)((((y >> 8) & 0x03) << 6) | (((x >> 8) & 0x03) << 4) | (size & 0x0F));
211	}
212	
213	/* Extended IR (12 bytes = 4 objects). Synthesize the two sensor-bar dots from the
214	 * pointer state (camera is 1024x768, mirrored vs the screen); other two not visible.
215	 * If the axis comes out inverted on hardware, flip the (1.0f - …) terms. */
216	static void build_ir_extended(uint8_t *dst)
217	{
218	    int x0 = -1, y0 = 0, x1 = -1, y1 = 0;
219	    if (s_point_active) {
220	        int midx = IR_X_CENTER + (int)((0.5f - s_point_x) * (2 * IR_X_HALF));
221	        int midy = IR_Y_CENTER + (int)((s_point_y - 0.5f) * (2 * IR_Y_HALF));
222	        const int sep = 128;                 /* half sensor-bar separation, camera px */
223	        x0 = midx - sep;
224	        x1 = midx + sep;
225	        if (x0 < 0) x0 = 0;
226	        if (x1 > 1023) x1 = 1023;
227	        if (midy < 0) midy = 0;
228	        if (midy > 767) midy = 767;
229	        y0 = y1 = midy;
230	    }
231	    put_ir_object(&dst[0], x0, y0, 4);
232	    put_ir_object(&dst[3], x1, y1, 4);
233	    put_ir_object(&dst[6], -1, 0, 0);
234	    put_ir_object(&dst[9], -1, 0, 0);
235	}
236	
237	/* Build the input report the Wii's current mode expects: buttons in the first two
238	 * bytes (except 0x3d), level accelerometer where present, extended IR from the
239	 * pointer state. Returns the payload length, or 0 for an unknown mode. */
240	static int build_report(uint8_t mode, uint8_t *p)
241	{
242	    memset(p, 0, 21);
243	    if (mode != 0x3d) {
244	        p[0] = s_btn0;
245	        p[1] = s_btn1;
246	    }
247	    switch (mode) {
248	    case 0x30: return 2;
249	    case 0x31: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 5;
250	    case 0x32: return 10;
251	    case 0x33: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_ir_extended(&p[5]); return 17;
252	    case 0x34: return 21;
253	    case 0x35: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 21;
254	    case 0x36: return 21;                            /* 10-byte basic IR: not filled yet */
255	    case 0x37: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 21;    /* 10-byte basic IR: not filled yet */
256	    case 0x3d: case 0x3e: case 0x3f: return 21;
257	    default:   return 0;
258	    }
259	}
260	
261	bool Wiimote_SetButton(const char *name, bool pressed)
262	{
263	    const wm_button_t *b = find_button(name);
264	    if (!b) return false;
265	    apply_button(b, pressed);
266	    return true;
267	}
268	
269	bool Wiimote_TapButton(const char *name)
270	{
271	    const wm_button_t *b = find_button(name);
272	    if (!b) return false;
273	    apply_button(b, true);
274	
275	    int slot = -1;
276	    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
277	        if (!s_taps[i].active) { slot = i; break; }
278	    }
279	    if (slot < 0) slot = 0;     /* all busy: reuse the first */
280	    s_taps[slot].byte = b->byte;
281	    s_taps[slot].mask = b->mask;
282	    s_taps[slot].release_at = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(TAP_MS);
283	    s_taps[slot].active = true;
284	    return true;
285	}
286	
287	void Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected(void)
288	{
289	    s_data_fd = -1;          /* mark not-connected at once (don't wait for the reader to exit) */
290	    s_streaming = false;
291	    s_leds = 0;
292	    s_btn0 = s_btn1 = 0;
293	    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
294	        s_taps[i].active = false;
295	    }
296	}
297	
298	bool Wiimote_IsConnected(void)  { return s_data_fd >= 0; }
299	bool Wiimote_IsAssigned(void)   { return s_leds != 0; }
300	uint8_t Wiimote_ReportMode(void) { return s_report_mode; }
301	
302	int Wiimote_PlayerSlot(void)
303	{
304	    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
305	        if (s_leds & (1 << i)) return i + 1;
306	    }
307	    return 0;
308	}
309	
310	void Wiimote_SetPointer(float x, float y)
311	{
312	    if (x < 0.0f) x = 0.0f; else if (x > 1.0f) x = 1.0f;
313	    if (y < 0.0f) y = 0.0f; else if (y > 1.0f) y = 1.0f;
314	    s_point_x = x;
315	    s_point_y = y;
316	    s_point_active = true;
317	}
318	
319	void Wiimote_ClearPointer(void)
320	{
321	    s_point_active = false;
322	}
323	
324	static void sender_task(void *arg)
325	{
326	    (void)arg;
327	    uint8_t p[21];
328	    for (;;) {
329	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SENDER_PERIOD_MS));
330	
331	        /* Release any taps whose deadline has passed (tick-wrap safe). */
332	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
333	        for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
334	            if (s_taps[i].active && (int32_t)(now - s_taps[i].release_at) >= 0) {
335	                uint8_t *b = (s_taps[i].byte == 0) ? &s_btn0 : &s_btn1;
336	                *b &= ~s_taps[i].mask;
337	                s_taps[i].active = false;
338	            }
339	        }
340	
341	        if (s_streaming && s_data_fd >= 0) {
342	            uint8_t mode = s_report_mode;
343	            int len = build_report(mode, p);
344	            if (len == 0) {                 /* unknown mode → fall back to core buttons */
345	                mode = 0x30;
346	                len = build_report(mode, p);
347	            }
348	            wm_send(s_data_fd, mode, p, len);
349	        }
350	    }
351	}
352	
353	void Wiimote_Start(void)
354	{
355	    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x16], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
356	    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x20], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
357	    xTaskCreateStatic(sender_task, "wm_tx", SENDER_STACK, NULL, 6,
358	                      s_sender_stack, &s_sender_tcb);
359	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote report state machine started");
360	}

Phase 3a is implemented — fauxmote now presents a guitar extension. Build and test:

```sh
idf.py build flash monitor
```

What's new:
- The status report sets the **extension-connected bit**, and the register bank returns the **guitar ID** (`00 00 A4 20 01 03`) at `0xfa`, so the Wii/GH3 should now **detect a guitar is plugged in**.
- Streams the 6-byte guitar report inside mode `0x34`/`0x35`/`0x3d`.
- CLI: existing `btn`/`tap` now accept **guitar names** — `btn green 1`, `tap strumdown`, `btn orange 1`, etc. (frets green/red/yellow/blue/orange, strumup/strumdown, gplus/gminus, pedal), plus `whammy <0..31>` and `ext <on|off>`.

**Test for 3a (detection):**
1. `pair` + SYNC → assigned (the wiimote + pointer should still work in the Wii menu as before).
2. Launch GH3 — it should now recognize a **guitar controller** rather than complaining there's no guitar.

**Important expectation:** GH3's note input won't work yet. GH3's Les Paul uses the **encrypted** extension protocol, and we're sending plaintext — so GH3 should *detect* the guitar but read garbage for frets/strum. Making the notes actually register is **Phase 3b** (porting the extension cipher), which I'll do next.

Two things to watch:
- Does the Wii menu still pair + point normally with the extension on? (If the extension somehow disrupts it, `ext off` then re-`pair` to compare as a plain wiimote.)
- Does GH3 acknowledge a guitar (e.g., not showing "no guitar detected" / letting you into guitar gameplay)?

If it builds and GH3 sees a guitar, I'll commit 3a and move to the encryption (3b). Tell me what GH3 says about the controller.

87	/* Resolve a button name to its target byte, mask, and polarity. Core buttons are
88	 * active-high (core button bytes); guitar buttons active-low (guitar bytes). */
89	static bool resolve_button(const char *name, uint8_t **target, uint8_t *mask, bool *active_low)
90	{
91	    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_buttons) / sizeof(k_buttons[0]); i++) {
92	        if (strcmp(name, k_buttons[i].name) == 0) {
93	            *target = (k_buttons[i].byte == 0) ? &s_btn0 : &s_btn1;
94	            *mask = k_buttons[i].mask;
95	            *active_low = false;
96	            return true;
97	        }
98	    }
99	    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_guitar) / sizeof(k_guitar[0]); i++) {
100	        if (strcmp(name, k_guitar[i].name) == 0) {
101	            *target = (k_guitar[i].byte == 4) ? &s_g_btn4 : &s_g_btn5;
102	            *mask = k_guitar[i].mask;
103	            *active_low = true;
104	            return true;
105	        }
106	    }
107	    return false;
108	}

137	/* 0x21 read-data: size_minus1 in 0..15, error in low nibble, 16-bit addr, data. */
138	static void send_read_data(int fd, uint8_t size_minus1, uint8_t error, uint16_t addr,
139	                           const uint8_t *data)
140	{
141	    uint8_t p[21] = {0};
142	    p[0] = s_btn0;
143	    p[1] = s_btn1;
144	    p[2] = (uint8_t)((size_minus1 << 4) | (error & 0x0F));
145	    p[3] = (uint8_t)(addr >> 8);
146	    p[4] = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
147	    if (data) {
148	        memcpy(p + 5, data, size_minus1 + 1);
149	    }
150	    wm_send(fd, 0x21, p, sizeof(p));
151	}

153	static void read_eeprom(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
154	{
155	    if (size == 0 || offset + size > EEPROM_READ_MAX) {
156	        send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);   /* error: invalid address */
157	        return;
158	    }
159	    uint32_t addr = offset;
160	    uint16_t left = size;
161	    while (left > 0) {
162	        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
163	        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, &s_eeprom[addr]);
164	        addr += chunk;
165	        left -= chunk;
166	    }
167	}
168	
169	/* Register space (0xa4xxxx = extension). We use the low byte as the index into the
170	 * extension register bank, which holds the guitar ID at 0xfa and any host writes. */
171	static void read_register(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
172	{
173	    uint32_t addr = offset;
174	    uint16_t left = size;
175	    while (left > 0) {
176	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
177	        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
178	        if ((int)idx + chunk > 256) chunk = (uint8_t)(256 - idx);   /* don't run off the bank */
179	        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, &s_reg_a4[idx]);
180	        addr += chunk;
181	        left -= chunk;
182	        if (idx + chunk >= 256) break;
183	    }
184	}
185	
186	static void write_register(uint32_t offset, uint8_t size, const uint8_t *data)
187	{
188	    uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(offset & 0xFF);
189	    for (int i = 0; i < size && (idx + i) < 256; i++) {
190	        s_reg_a4[idx + i] = data[i];
191	    }
192	}

194	void Wiimote_HandleRx(int fd, const uint8_t *data, int len)
195	{
196	    if (len < 2 || data[0] != HIDP_OUTPUT) {
197	        return;   /* not a HID output report (e.g. control-channel HIDP transaction) */
198	    }
199	    s_data_fd = fd;                 /* this fd is the data channel — reply / stream here */
200	    uint8_t report = data[1];
201	    const uint8_t *p = data + 2;
202	    int plen = len - 2;
203	    if (plen >= 1) {
204	        s_rumble = p[0] & 0x01;     /* rumble bit rides the first payload byte of every report */
205	    }
206	
207	    switch (report) {
208	    case 0x11:                      /* player LEDs */
209	        if (plen >= 1) s_leds = (p[0] >> 4) & 0x0F;
210	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
211	        break;
212	    case 0x12:                      /* data reporting mode */
213	        if (plen >= 2) {
214	            s_reporting_continuous = (p[0] & 0x04) != 0;
215	            s_report_mode = p[1];
216	        }
217	        s_streaming = true;
218	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "reporting mode 0x%02x (continuous=%d)", s_report_mode, s_reporting_continuous);
219	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
220	        break;
221	    case 0x10:                      /* rumble only */
222	    case 0x13: case 0x1A:           /* IR camera enable */
223	    case 0x14: case 0x19:           /* speaker enable / mute */
224	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
225	        break;
226	    case 0x15:                      /* status request */
227	        send_status(fd);
228	        break;
229	    case 0x16:                      /* write memory/registers */
230	        if (plen >= 5) {
231	            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
232	            uint8_t wsize = p[4];
233	            if (p[0] & 0x04) write_register(offset, wsize, &p[5]);   /* extension register write */
234	        }
235	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
236	        break;
237	    case 0x17:                      /* read memory/registers */
238	        if (plen >= 6) {
239	            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
240	            uint16_t size = (uint16_t)((p[4] << 8) | p[5]);
241	            if (p[0] & 0x04) {      /* register space (extension) */
242	                read_register(fd, offset, size);
243	            } else {
244	                read_eeprom(fd, offset, size);
245	            }
246	        }
247	        break;
248	    default:
249	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
250	        break;
251	    }
252	}

254	static void set_accel_level(uint8_t *a)
255	{
256	    a[0] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* X = 0 g */
257	    a[1] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* Y = 0 g */
258	    a[2] = 0xA0;            /* Z = +1 g (held level, no roll) */
259	}

261	/* One extended-IR object: X/Y are 10-bit camera coords (1024x768), or x<0 = "not
262	 * visible". 3rd byte packs Y[9:8], X[9:8], size. */
263	static void put_ir_object(uint8_t *o, int x, int y, int size)
264	{
265	    if (x < 0) {
266	        o[0] = o[1] = o[2] = 0xFF;
267	        return;
268	    }
269	    o[0] = (uint8_t)(x & 0xFF);
270	    o[1] = (uint8_t)(y & 0xFF);
271	    o[2] = (uint8_t)((((y >> 8) & 0x03) << 6) | (((x >> 8) & 0x03) << 4) | (size & 0x0F));
272	}
273	
274	/* Extended IR (12 bytes = 4 objects). Synthesize the two sensor-bar dots from the
275	 * pointer state (camera is 1024x768, mirrored vs the screen); other two not visible.
276	 * If the axis comes out inverted on hardware, flip the (1.0f - …) terms. */
277	static void build_ir_extended(uint8_t *dst)
278	{
279	    int x0 = -1, y0 = 0, x1 = -1, y1 = 0;
280	    if (s_point_active) {
281	        int midx = IR_X_CENTER + (int)((0.5f - s_point_x) * (2 * IR_X_HALF));
282	        int midy = IR_Y_CENTER + (int)((s_point_y - 0.5f) * (2 * IR_Y_HALF));
283	        const int sep = 128;                 /* half sensor-bar separation, camera px */
284	        x0 = midx - sep;
285	        x1 = midx + sep;
286	        if (x0 < 0) x0 = 0;
287	        if (x1 > 1023) x1 = 1023;
288	        if (midy < 0) midy = 0;
289	        if (midy > 767) midy = 767;
290	        y0 = y1 = midy;
291	    }
292	    put_ir_object(&dst[0], x0, y0, 4);
293	    put_ir_object(&dst[3], x1, y1, 4);
294	    put_ir_object(&dst[6], -1, 0, 0);
295	    put_ir_object(&dst[9], -1, 0, 0);
296	}
297	
298	/* The 6-byte guitar extension report (plaintext). NOTE: GH3 expects this encrypted
299	 * (Phase 3b) — without the cipher the buttons read as garbage in-game. */
300	static void build_guitar_report(uint8_t *d)
301	{
302	    d[0] = s_g_sx;
303	    d[1] = s_g_sy;
304	    d[2] = s_g_tb;
305	    d[3] = s_g_whammy;
306	    d[4] = s_g_btn4;
307	    d[5] = s_g_btn5;
308	}
309	
310	/* Build the input report the Wii's current mode expects: core buttons in the first
311	 * two bytes (except 0x3d), level accelerometer where present, extended IR from the
312	 * pointer state, and the guitar report in the extension bytes. Returns the payload
313	 * length, or 0 for an unknown mode. */
314	static int build_report(uint8_t mode, uint8_t *p)
315	{
316	    memset(p, 0, 21);
317	    if (mode != 0x3d) {
318	        p[0] = s_btn0;
319	        p[1] = s_btn1;
320	    }
321	    switch (mode) {
322	    case 0x30: return 2;
323	    case 0x31: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 5;
324	    case 0x32: if (s_ext_connected) build_guitar_report(&p[2]); return 10;
325	    case 0x33: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_ir_extended(&p[5]); return 17;
326	    case 0x34: if (s_ext_connected) build_guitar_report(&p[2]); return 21;
327	    case 0x35: set_accel_level(&p[2]); if (s_ext_connected) build_guitar_report(&p[5]); return 21;
328	    case 0x36: return 21;                            /* 10-byte basic IR: not filled yet */
329	    case 0x37: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 21;    /* 10-byte basic IR: not filled yet */
330	    case 0x3d: if (s_ext_connected) build_guitar_report(&p[0]); return 21;
331	    case 0x3e: case 0x3f: return 21;
332	    default:   return 0;
333	    }
334	}

336	bool Wiimote_SetButton(const char *name, bool pressed)
337	{
338	    uint8_t *t; uint8_t m; bool al;
339	    if (!resolve_button(name, &t, &m, &al)) return false;
340	    if (pressed != al) *t |= m; else *t &= (uint8_t)~m;   /* active-low guitar bits invert */
341	    return true;
342	}
343	
344	bool Wiimote_TapButton(const char *name)
345	{
346	    uint8_t *t; uint8_t m; bool al;
347	    if (!resolve_button(name, &t, &m, &al)) return false;
348	    if (al) *t &= (uint8_t)~m; else *t |= m;   /* press */
349	
350	    int slot = -1;
351	    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
352	        if (!s_taps[i].active) { slot = i; break; }
353	    }
354	    if (slot < 0) slot = 0;     /* all busy: reuse the first */
355	    s_taps[slot].target = t;
356	    s_taps[slot].mask = m;
357	    s_taps[slot].active_low = al;
358	    s_taps[slot].release_at = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(TAP_MS);
359	    s_taps[slot].active = true;
360	    return true;
361	}

412	static void sender_task(void *arg)
413	{
414	    (void)arg;
415	    uint8_t p[21];
416	    for (;;) {
417	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SENDER_PERIOD_MS));
418	
419	        /* Release any taps whose deadline has passed (tick-wrap safe). */
420	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
421	        for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
422	            if (s_taps[i].active && (int32_t)(now - s_taps[i].release_at) >= 0) {
423	                if (s_taps[i].active_low) *s_taps[i].target |= s_taps[i].mask;
424	                else *s_taps[i].target &= (uint8_t)~s_taps[i].mask;
425	                s_taps[i].active = false;
426	            }
427	        }
428	
429	        if (s_streaming && s_data_fd >= 0) {
430	            uint8_t mode = s_report_mode;
431	            int len = build_report(mode, p);
432	            if (len == 0) {                 /* unknown mode → fall back to core buttons */
433	                mode = 0x30;
434	                len = build_report(mode, p);
435	            }
436	            wm_send(s_data_fd, mode, p, len);
437	        }
438	    }
439	}

441	void Wiimote_Start(void)
442	{
443	    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x16], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
444	    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x20], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
445	
446	    /* Guitar extension register bank: ID at 0xfa identifies a GH guitar. */
447	    static const uint8_t k_guitar_id[6] = { 0x00, 0x00, 0xA4, 0x20, 0x01, 0x03 };
448	    memcpy(&s_reg_a4[0xFA], k_guitar_id, sizeof(k_guitar_id));
449	
450	    xTaskCreateStatic(sender_task, "wm_tx", SENDER_STACK, NULL, 6,
451	                      s_sender_stack, &s_sender_tcb);
452	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote report state machine started");
453	}

#pragma once

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* A Wiimote extension controller (guitar, nunchuk, classic, …). The base Wiimote
 * owns the BT/HID link, the report sender, and the register/status plumbing; an
 * extension module registers itself and supplies its identity + data.
 *
 * An extension provides a 256-byte register bank (the host reads the ID at 0xfa and
 * may write init/encryption bytes), a function to fill its bytes in the data report,
 * an optional button-by-name setter (so the CLI/Marvin drive it through the same
 * Wiimote_SetButton API), and an optional reset hook for link drops. */
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    uint8_t    *regs;        /* 256-byte register bank, owned by the extension (ID at 0xfa) */
    uint8_t     report_len;  /* bytes the extension contributes to the data report */
    void (*build_report)(uint8_t *dst);                  /* fill report_len bytes */
    bool (*set_button)(const char *name, bool pressed);  /* ext button by name; false if unknown */
    void (*reset)(void);                                 /* release inputs on link drop (may be NULL) */
} wiimote_extension_t;

/* Attach an extension to the base Wiimote (one at a time). Pass NULL to detach. */
void Wiimote_RegisterExtension(const wiimote_extension_t *ext);

#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "esp_log.h"

#include "wiimote.h"
#include "wiimote_ext.h"

static const char *TAG = "fauxmote.wm";

#define EEPROM_SIZE       0x1700u   /* readable EEPROM range is 0x0000..0x16FF */
#define EEPROM_READ_MAX   0x16FFu
#define SENDER_PERIOD_MS  15
#define SENDER_STACK      3072
#define ACCEL_NEUTRAL     0x85      /* zero-g raw value (matches the EEPROM calibration) */

/* IR pointer calibration in camera coords (1024x768), from on-hardware edge
 * measurement. Pointer (0,0) = top-left, (1,1) = bottom-right maps to screen edges. */
#define IR_X_CENTER  512
#define IR_X_HALF    296
#define IR_Y_CENTER  487
#define IR_Y_HALF    165

/* HID transaction prefixes (HIDP): host->device output, device->host input. */
#define HIDP_OUTPUT  0xA2
#define HIDP_INPUT   0xA1

static int     s_data_fd = -1;       /* the HID data channel (carries 0xa2 output reports) */
static uint8_t s_leds;               /* player LEDs (nibble), set by the Wii via report 0x11 */
static uint8_t s_rumble;
static bool    s_streaming;          /* true once the Wii has set a reporting mode (0x12) */
static uint8_t s_report_mode = 0x30; /* report ID the Wii told us to send (default core buttons) */
static bool    s_reporting_continuous;
static uint8_t s_btn0, s_btn1;       /* core button state (0 = nothing pressed) */
static float   s_point_x, s_point_y; /* IR pointer position, 0..1 (0,0 = top-left) */
static bool    s_point_active;       /* false = no IR dots reported */
static uint8_t s_eeprom[EEPROM_SIZE];

static const wiimote_extension_t *s_ext;   /* registered extension, or NULL */
static bool    s_ext_connected;            /* report the extension as attached */

static StaticTask_t s_sender_tcb;
static StackType_t  s_sender_stack[SENDER_STACK];

/* Accelerometer calibration the Wii reads from EEPROM 0x16 (mirrored at 0x20).
 * Canonical zero-G 0x85 / 1G 0xA0 per axis + checksum (from a real RVL-CNT-01). */
static const uint8_t k_accel_cal[10] = {
    0x85, 0x85, 0x85, 0x00, 0xA0, 0xA0, 0xA0, 0x00, 0x40, 0x04,
};

/* Core button names → (byte index, bit mask) in the 2-byte core button field. */
static const struct { const char *name; uint8_t byte; uint8_t mask; } k_buttons[] = {
    { "left",  0, 0x01 }, { "right", 0, 0x02 }, { "down", 0, 0x04 }, { "up", 0, 0x08 },
    { "plus",  0, 0x10 },
    { "two",   1, 0x01 }, { "one",   1, 0x02 }, { "b",    1, 0x04 }, { "a",  1, 0x08 },
    { "minus", 1, 0x10 }, { "home",  1, 0x80 },
};

/* Momentary taps: Wiimote_TapButton presses now and schedules a release (by name,
 * so it works for core and extension buttons alike) that the sender task applies. */
#define TAP_SLOTS  4
#define TAP_MS     120
static struct { char name[16]; TickType_t release_at; bool active; } s_taps[TAP_SLOTS];

static void wm_send(int fd, uint8_t report_id, const uint8_t *payload, int paylen)
{
    uint8_t frame[2 + 21];
    frame[0] = HIDP_INPUT;
    frame[1] = report_id;
    if (paylen > 0) {
        memcpy(frame + 2, payload, paylen);
    }
    write(fd, frame, 2 + paylen);
}

static void send_status(int fd)
{
    uint8_t p[6] = {0};
    p[0] = s_btn0;
    p[1] = s_btn1;
    p[2] = (uint8_t)((s_leds << 4) | ((s_ext && s_ext_connected) ? 0x02 : 0x00));  /* LEDs 4..7, ext bit 1 */
    p[5] = 0xC0;                     /* battery level (near full) */
    wm_send(fd, 0x20, p, sizeof(p));
}

static void send_ack(int fd, uint8_t report_id, uint8_t result)
{
    uint8_t p[4] = { s_btn0, s_btn1, report_id, result };
    wm_send(fd, 0x22, p, sizeof(p));
}

/* 0x21 read-data: size_minus1 in 0..15, error in low nibble, 16-bit addr, data. */
static void send_read_data(int fd, uint8_t size_minus1, uint8_t error, uint16_t addr,
                           const uint8_t *data)
{
    uint8_t p[21] = {0};
    p[0] = s_btn0;
    p[1] = s_btn1;
    p[2] = (uint8_t)((size_minus1 << 4) | (error & 0x0F));
    p[3] = (uint8_t)(addr >> 8);
    p[4] = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
    if (data) {
        memcpy(p + 5, data, size_minus1 + 1);
    }
    wm_send(fd, 0x21, p, sizeof(p));
}

static void read_eeprom(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
{
    if (size == 0 || offset + size > EEPROM_READ_MAX) {
        send_read_data(fd, 0x0F, 0x08, (uint16_t)offset, NULL);   /* error: invalid address */
        return;
    }
    uint32_t addr = offset;
    uint16_t left = size;
    while (left > 0) {
        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, &s_eeprom[addr]);
        addr += chunk;
        left -= chunk;
    }
}

/* Register reads/writes. Only the extension space (0xa4xxxx) is backed (by the
 * registered extension's bank); other spaces (IR 0xb0, speaker 0xa2) read as zeros
 * and writes are accepted but ignored. */
static void read_register(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
{
    bool ext = (s_ext && ((offset >> 16) & 0xFE) == 0xA4);
    uint32_t addr = offset;
    uint16_t left = size;
    while (left > 0) {
        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
        if ((int)idx + chunk > 256) chunk = (uint8_t)(256 - idx);
        send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, ext ? &s_ext->regs[idx] : NULL);
        addr += chunk;
        left -= chunk;
        if (idx + chunk >= 256) break;
    }
}

static void write_register(uint32_t offset, uint8_t size, const uint8_t *data)
{
    if (!s_ext || ((offset >> 16) & 0xFE) != 0xA4) {
        return;   /* only the extension register space is backed */
    }
    uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(offset & 0xFF);
    for (int i = 0; i < size && (idx + i) < 256; i++) {
        s_ext->regs[idx + i] = data[i];
    }
}

void Wiimote_HandleRx(int fd, const uint8_t *data, int len)
{
    if (len < 2 || data[0] != HIDP_OUTPUT) {
        return;   /* not a HID output report (e.g. control-channel HIDP transaction) */
    }
    s_data_fd = fd;                 /* this fd is the data channel — reply / stream here */
    uint8_t report = data[1];
    const uint8_t *p = data + 2;
    int plen = len - 2;
    if (plen >= 1) {
        s_rumble = p[0] & 0x01;     /* rumble bit rides the first payload byte of every report */
    }

    switch (report) {
    case 0x11:                      /* player LEDs */
        if (plen >= 1) s_leds = (p[0] >> 4) & 0x0F;
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x12:                      /* data reporting mode */
        if (plen >= 2) {
            s_reporting_continuous = (p[0] & 0x04) != 0;
            s_report_mode = p[1];
        }
        s_streaming = true;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "reporting mode 0x%02x (continuous=%d)", s_report_mode, s_reporting_continuous);
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x10:                      /* rumble only */
    case 0x13: case 0x1A:           /* IR camera enable */
    case 0x14: case 0x19:           /* speaker enable / mute */
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x15:                      /* status request */
        send_status(fd);
        break;
    case 0x16:                      /* write memory/registers */
        if (plen >= 5) {
            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
            uint8_t wsize = p[4];
            if (p[0] & 0x04) write_register(offset, wsize, &p[5]);
        }
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    case 0x17:                      /* read memory/registers */
        if (plen >= 6) {
            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
            uint16_t size = (uint16_t)((p[4] << 8) | p[5]);
            if (p[0] & 0x04) {
                read_register(fd, offset, size);
            } else {
                read_eeprom(fd, offset, size);
            }
        }
        break;
    default:
        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
        break;
    }
}

static void set_accel_level(uint8_t *a)
{
    a[0] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* X = 0 g */
    a[1] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* Y = 0 g */
    a[2] = 0xA0;            /* Z = +1 g (held level, no roll) */
}

/* One extended-IR object: X/Y are 10-bit camera coords (1024x768), or x<0 = "not
 * visible". 3rd byte packs Y[9:8], X[9:8], size. */
static void put_ir_object(uint8_t *o, int x, int y, int size)
{
    if (x < 0) {
        o[0] = o[1] = o[2] = 0xFF;
        return;
    }
    o[0] = (uint8_t)(x & 0xFF);
    o[1] = (uint8_t)(y & 0xFF);
    o[2] = (uint8_t)((((y >> 8) & 0x03) << 6) | (((x >> 8) & 0x03) << 4) | (size & 0x0F));
}

/* Extended IR (12 bytes = 4 objects). Synthesize the two sensor-bar dots from the
 * pointer state (camera is 1024x768, mirrored vs the screen); other two not visible.
 * If the axis comes out inverted on hardware, flip the (… - …) terms. */
static void build_ir_extended(uint8_t *dst)
{
    int x0 = -1, y0 = 0, x1 = -1, y1 = 0;
    if (s_point_active) {
        int midx = IR_X_CENTER + (int)((0.5f - s_point_x) * (2 * IR_X_HALF));
        int midy = IR_Y_CENTER + (int)((s_point_y - 0.5f) * (2 * IR_Y_HALF));
        const int sep = 128;                 /* half sensor-bar separation, camera px */
        x0 = midx - sep;
        x1 = midx + sep;
        if (x0 < 0) x0 = 0;
        if (x1 > 1023) x1 = 1023;
        if (midy < 0) midy = 0;
        if (midy > 767) midy = 767;
        y0 = y1 = midy;
    }
    put_ir_object(&dst[0], x0, y0, 4);
    put_ir_object(&dst[3], x1, y1, 4);
    put_ir_object(&dst[6], -1, 0, 0);
    put_ir_object(&dst[9], -1, 0, 0);
}

/* Fill the registered extension's bytes at dst, if an extension is attached. */
static void build_extension(uint8_t *dst)
{
    if (s_ext && s_ext_connected && s_ext->build_report) {
        s_ext->build_report(dst);
    }
}

/* Build the input report the Wii's current mode expects: core buttons in the first
 * two bytes (except 0x3d), level accelerometer where present, extended IR from the
 * pointer state, and the extension's bytes in the extension field. Returns the
 * payload length, or 0 for an unknown mode. */
static int build_report(uint8_t mode, uint8_t *p)
{
    memset(p, 0, 21);
    if (mode != 0x3d) {
        p[0] = s_btn0;
        p[1] = s_btn1;
    }
    switch (mode) {
    case 0x30: return 2;
    case 0x31: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 5;
    case 0x32: build_extension(&p[2]); return 10;
    case 0x33: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_ir_extended(&p[5]); return 17;
    case 0x34: build_extension(&p[2]); return 21;
    case 0x35: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_extension(&p[5]); return 21;
    case 0x36: return 21;                            /* 10-byte basic IR: not filled yet */
    case 0x37: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 21;    /* 10-byte basic IR: not filled yet */
    case 0x3d: build_extension(&p[0]); return 21;
    case 0x3e: case 0x3f: return 21;
    default:   return 0;
    }
}

void Wiimote_RegisterExtension(const wiimote_extension_t *ext)
{
    s_ext = ext;
    s_ext_connected = (ext != NULL);
}

bool Wiimote_SetButton(const char *name, bool pressed)
{
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_buttons) / sizeof(k_buttons[0]); i++) {
        if (strcmp(name, k_buttons[i].name) == 0) {
            uint8_t *b = (k_buttons[i].byte == 0) ? &s_btn0 : &s_btn1;
            if (pressed) *b |= k_buttons[i].mask; else *b &= (uint8_t)~k_buttons[i].mask;
            return true;
        }
    }
    if (s_ext && s_ext->set_button) {
        return s_ext->set_button(name, pressed);
    }
    return false;
}

bool Wiimote_TapButton(const char *name)
{
    if (!Wiimote_SetButton(name, true)) {
        return false;
    }
    int slot = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
        if (!s_taps[i].active) { slot = i; break; }
    }
    if (slot < 0) slot = 0;     /* all busy: reuse the first */
    strncpy(s_taps[slot].name, name, sizeof(s_taps[slot].name) - 1);
    s_taps[slot].name[sizeof(s_taps[slot].name) - 1] = '\0';
    s_taps[slot].release_at = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(TAP_MS);
    s_taps[slot].active = true;
    return true;
}

void Wiimote_SetExtension(bool connected)
{
    s_ext_connected = connected;
}

void Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected(void)
{
    s_data_fd = -1;          /* mark not-connected at once (don't wait for the reader to exit) */
    s_streaming = false;
    s_leds = 0;
    s_btn0 = s_btn1 = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
        s_taps[i].active = false;
    }
    if (s_ext && s_ext->reset) {
        s_ext->reset();
    }
}

bool Wiimote_IsConnected(void)  { return s_data_fd >= 0; }
bool Wiimote_IsAssigned(void)   { return s_leds != 0; }
uint8_t Wiimote_ReportMode(void) { return s_report_mode; }

int Wiimote_PlayerSlot(void)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        if (s_leds & (1 << i)) return i + 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

void Wiimote_SetPointer(float x, float y)
{
    if (x < 0.0f) x = 0.0f; else if (x > 1.0f) x = 1.0f;
    if (y < 0.0f) y = 0.0f; else if (y > 1.0f) y = 1.0f;
    s_point_x = x;
    s_point_y = y;
    s_point_active = true;
}

void Wiimote_ClearPointer(void)
{
    s_point_active = false;
}

static void sender_task(void *arg)
{
    (void)arg;
    uint8_t p[21];
    for (;;) {
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SENDER_PERIOD_MS));

        /* Release any taps whose deadline has passed (tick-wrap safe). */
        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
        for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
            if (s_taps[i].active && (int32_t)(now - s_taps[i].release_at) >= 0) {
                Wiimote_SetButton(s_taps[i].name, false);
                s_taps[i].active = false;
            }
        }

        if (s_streaming && s_data_fd >= 0) {
            uint8_t mode = s_report_mode;
            int len = build_report(mode, p);
            if (len == 0) {                 /* unknown mode → fall back to core buttons */
                mode = 0x30;
                len = build_report(mode, p);
            }
            wm_send(s_data_fd, mode, p, len);
        }
    }
}

void Wiimote_Start(void)
{
    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x16], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x20], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
    xTaskCreateStatic(sender_task, "wm_tx", SENDER_STACK, NULL, 6,
                      s_sender_stack, &s_sender_tcb);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote report state machine started");
}

#include <string.h>

#include "wiimote_ext.h"
#include "guitar.h"

/* Guitar Hero guitar extension. 6-byte report (buttons active-low, rest = 1):
 *   0: stick X (bits 5-0)      1: stick Y (bits 5-0)
 *   2: touch bar (bits 4-0)    3: whammy (bits 4-0)
 *   4: bit6 strum-down, bit4 minus, bit2 plus (others 1)
 *   5: bit7 orange, bit6 red, bit5 blue, bit4 green, bit3 yellow, bit2 pedal,
 *      bit0 strum-up (bit1 = 1)
 * GH3 expects this encrypted — see Phase 3b (the cipher is not implemented yet). */

static uint8_t s_regs[256];                    /* register bank (ID at 0xfa) */
static uint8_t s_sx = 0x20, s_sy = 0x20;       /* analog stick, centered */
static uint8_t s_tb;                           /* touch bar (GH3 unused) */
static uint8_t s_whammy = 0x10;                /* whammy bar (rest) */
static uint8_t s_btn4 = 0xFF, s_btn5 = 0xFF;   /* button bytes, active-low (rest 0xFF) */

static const struct { const char *name; uint8_t byte; uint8_t mask; } k_btn[] = {
    { "green",   5, 0x10 }, { "red",    5, 0x40 }, { "yellow", 5, 0x08 },
    { "blue",    5, 0x20 }, { "orange", 5, 0x80 }, { "pedal",  5, 0x04 },
    { "strumup", 5, 0x01 }, { "strumdown", 4, 0x40 },
    { "gplus",   4, 0x04 }, { "gminus", 4, 0x10 },
};

static void guitar_build_report(uint8_t *d)
{
    d[0] = s_sx;
    d[1] = s_sy;
    d[2] = s_tb;
    d[3] = s_whammy;
    d[4] = s_btn4;
    d[5] = s_btn5;
}

static bool guitar_set_button(const char *name, bool pressed)
{
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_btn) / sizeof(k_btn[0]); i++) {
        if (strcmp(name, k_btn[i].name) == 0) {
            uint8_t *b = (k_btn[i].byte == 4) ? &s_btn4 : &s_btn5;
            if (pressed) *b &= (uint8_t)~k_btn[i].mask;   /* active-low: pressed = clear */
            else *b |= k_btn[i].mask;
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

static void guitar_reset(void)
{
    s_btn4 = s_btn5 = 0xFF;
    s_whammy = 0x10;
}

void Guitar_SetWhammy(uint8_t value)
{
    s_whammy = value & 0x1F;
}

static const wiimote_extension_t s_guitar = {
    .name        = "guitar",
    .regs        = s_regs,
    .report_len  = 6,
    .build_report = guitar_build_report,
    .set_button  = guitar_set_button,
    .reset       = guitar_reset,
};

void Guitar_Init(void)
{
    memset(s_regs, 0, sizeof(s_regs));
    static const uint8_t k_id[6] = { 0x00, 0x00, 0xA4, 0x20, 0x01, 0x03 };  /* GH guitar */
    memcpy(&s_regs[0xFA], k_id, sizeof(k_id));
    Wiimote_RegisterExtension(&s_guitar);
}

Great questions, and the wiibrew check resolves both. Let me lay it out:

**Polarity — both of us are right, about different things:**
- **Core Wiimote buttons** (A/B/+/dpad, report `0x30`): **active-high**, 1 = pressed.
- **Extension buttons** (guitar/nunchuk/classic): **active-low**, 0 = pressed (rest = 1).

So my code intentionally uses opposite polarities for the two — that's the apparent contradiction. The wiibrew table confirms the guitar bytes are active-low (all those fixed `1` bits are the rest state), and the clincher is that green/red **work** with my active-low encoding. So you're right that *core* buttons are 1-when-pressed; the guitar extension is the opposite.

**Encryption — not needed, confirmed.** wiibrew says the "new way" init (`0x55`→`0xf0`) makes data unencrypted, and since green/red register from our plaintext, GH3 is clearly reading us unencrypted. **So Phase 3b is off the table** — nice simplification.

**Strum bits — verified *correct*.** The wiibrew table you linked, verbatim:
- Byte 4: `1 BD 1 B- 1 B+ 1 1` → strum-down = bit 6 (`0x40`)
- Byte 5: `BO BR BB BG BY PB 1 BU` → strum-up = bit 0 (`0x01`)

That's *exactly* what I have. And strum-up is in byte 5 — the same byte where green/red work — so the encoding is definitely reaching GH3. That means the bug isn't the bits.

The most likely explanation: **the GH3 screen you tested doesn't use strum.** Some GH3 menus navigate with frets only (green = confirm, red = back), while strum scrolls in *song select* and, of course, hits notes *in a song*. So:

- **Where did you test** green/red/strum — main menu, a yes/no dialog, song select?
- The definitive strum test is **in a song**: hold the matching fret and `tap strumdown` (or strumup) as a note hits the line — does it score? Or in **song select**, does `tap strumdown` scroll the song list?

If strum still does nothing in actual gameplay, then it's a timing/edge thing (e.g., the 120 ms tap), and I'll adjust. But the encoding is correct.

This is a solid, working milestone — detection + frets, no encryption. Want me to **commit Phase 3a** (and drop 3b from the plan) while you try the in-song strum test?

3:These Guitars are identified by the '''6''' bytes: 00 00 A4 20 01 03 at register address 0x(4)a400fa. The first 00 indicates that it is a guitar and not drums (which would be 01). 
5:If you initialise the expansion the old way, by writing 0 to 0x(4)a40040, then on a Guitar Hero 3 Gibson Les Paul guitar those 6 bytes will be readable but encrypted, and on a Guitar Hero World Tour or 3rd party Guitar those bytes will be FF FF FF FF FF FF. To make a GHWT or 3rd Party guitar work, you need to write 0x55 to 0x(4)a400f0, then 0 to 0x(4)a400fb. That will allow the 6 bytes to be read, and has the side effect of making all the expansion data, including those 6 bytes, unencrypted. Testing with the old method first allows you to know whether it is a GH3 Guitar or a GHWT Guitar.
12:RAGE wireless guitar for Wii: Has another set of fret buttons lower down the neck, presumably these button trigger both the fret and one of the strum buttons at the same time.
20:TGC Wii Wireless Guitar: Has another set of fret buttons lower down, probably identical to upper buttons
22:Wii Dragon Wireless Guitar: Has another set of fret buttons lower down, probably identical to upper buttons
29:The Guitar reports its information as 6 bytes of data, readable at 0xa40008 and streamable using Data Reporting Modes that include Extension bytes (unused bytes are filled with 0x00). The data is packed into the six bytes as follows ('''after decryption'''):
36:| style="border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 0.2em; background-color: #ddd;" | '''Byte'''
88:SX,SY are the Analog Stick X and Y positions. BG,BR,BY,BB,BO are the fret buttons by color (Green, Red, Yellow, Blue, Orange). B-,B+ are the + and - buttons at the base of the controller, on the GHWT Guitars the B- is the StarPower button. BU and BD are up and down on the strum bar, respectively. WB is the analog whammy bar. PB is the button triggered by a cancelled effects pedal via the RJ11 expansion port at the controller base. Bits marked GH3 seem to be 1 on GH3 Gibson Les Paul Guitars and 0 on GHWT Guitars.
90:TB is the analog touchbar found on the neck of the Guitar Hero World Tour Guitars, which does not exist on Guitar Hero 3 Guitars.
92: Not touching it  -  0F
93: 1st (top) fret   -  04
103:You can hold two (touchbar) frets at once, as long as those two (touchbar) frets are adjacent, otherwise it will take the value of the lowest fret held (Eg, if you hold the highest and lowest fret, it reads 1F)

{
	__u8 sx, sy, tb, wb, bd, bm, bp, bo, br, bb, bg, by, bu;

	 *    1   |  0  |  0  |              SX <5:0>             |

	 *    3   |  0  |  0  |  0  |      TB <4:0>               |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----------------------------+
	 *    4   |  0  |  0  |  0  |      WB <4:0>               |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 *    5   |  1  | BD  |  1  | B-  |  1  | B+  |  1  |  1  |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 *    6   | BO  | BR  | BB  | BG  | BY  |  1  |  1  | BU  |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 * All buttons are 0 if pressed
	 *
	 * With Motion+ enabled, it will look like this:
	 *   Byte |  8  |  7  |  6  |  5  |  4  |  3  |  2  |  1  |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 *    1   |  0  |  0  |              SX <5:1>       | BU  |
	 *    2   |  0  |  0  |              SY <5:1>       |  1  |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----------------------+-----+
	 *    3   |  0  |  0  |  0  |      TB <4:0>               |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----------------------------+
	 *    4   |  0  |  0  |  0  |      WB <4:0>               |
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 *    5   |  1  | BD  |  1  | B-  |  1  | B+  |  1  |XXXXX|
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 *    6   | BO  | BR  | BB  | BG  | BY  |  1  |XXXXX|XXXXX|
	 *   -----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+
	 */

	sx = ext[0] & 0x3f;

	tb = ext[2] & 0x1f;

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 18:48:22Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 18:48:35Z)**_

Good question — there are **two completely separate "encryptions"** here, and conflating them is exactly the confusion. Let me separate them:

**1. Bluetooth link encryption (Wiimote ↔ Wii)**
This is normal Bluetooth security — the link key established during SYNC/pairing, used to encrypt the radio link. It's handled entirely by the Bluetooth stack (Bluedroid on our side). The Wii absolutely cares about it, but it's *already working* — it's what our pairing/bond code set up. It has nothing to do with frets or strum. Ignore it for this problem.

**2. Extension "encryption" (extension chip ↔ Wiimote, over the internal I²C bus)**
This is the weird one, and it's *not* a Bluetooth thing at all. Physically, a guitar/nunchuk is a little chip that plugs into the Wiimote's extension port and talks to the Wiimote over an internal I²C bus. The bytes on *that* bus are obfuscated with a trivial cipher. It lives entirely inside the (Wiimote + extension) assembly.

Here's the key part for us: the Wii doesn't read the extension chip directly. It reads the Wiimote's **register space** — addresses `0xa400xx` — either by a `0x17` register read or via the extension bytes embedded in a streamed data report. Whether the bytes sitting in that register space are encrypted or plaintext depends on how the *extension was initialized*:

- Game writes `0x55` → `0xa400f0` (the "new way") → extension reports **plaintext**, and the game reads them as-is.
- Game writes `0x00` → `0xa40040` (the "old way") → extension reports **encrypted**, and the game **decrypts in software** what it reads.

So **does the Wii/game care? Yes — but only because it performs the init and then interprets the bytes accordingly.** It's not a transport thing; it's "the game decrypts the data it reads *if* it set up encrypted mode."

**Why this matters for our bug:** we *are* the register space. Whatever bytes we put there, the game interprets based on the init *it* did. If GH3 did the old (encrypted) init and we hand it plaintext, GH3 runs our bytes through its decrypt routine → garbage. That could plausibly scramble strum while leaving some fret bits looking OK by luck.

That's *exactly* why I added the register logging — the `WR off=0x...0f0` (plaintext init) vs `WR off=0x...040` (encrypted init) line will tell us definitively which mode GH3 chose, and therefore whether we owe it encrypted data. So the trace settles both your question and the strum bug at once. Grab that log whenever you're ready.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 18:52:06Z)**_

This is the smoking gun. Look at the sequence GH3 ran:

```
WR off=0xa400f0  d=55         ← disable encryption (temporarily)
RD reg off=0xa400fa sz=6      ← read the ID in the clear → "ah, a GH3 Les Paul"
WR off=0xa400f0  d=aa         ← RE-ENABLE encryption
WR off=0xa40040  d=f1 f7 3a e9 59 bb ┐
WR off=0xa40046  d=71 a9 b6 5c ba c9 ├ 16-byte encryption KEY
WR off=0xa4004c  d=f3 dd 48 b1       ┘
RD reg off=0xa40020 sz=32     ← read calibration (now encrypted)
reporting mode 0x37
```

So I was **wrong** that encryption wasn't needed. GH3 deliberately:
1. turns encryption *off* just long enough to read the ID and decide "GH3 vs GHWT,"
2. then turns it **back on** (`0xAA` → `0xf0`) and writes a **16-byte key** to `0x40–0x4F`.

That means every extension byte GH3 reads from us — the streamed guitar report *and* the calibration — is run through its **decrypt** routine using that key. We're sending plaintext, so GH3 decrypts our bytes into garbage. Green/red "working" was a fluke: decrypting our plaintext happened to land the green/red bits often enough to look right, while the strum bits decrypted to noise. **Phase 3b (the cipher) is required after all.**

And this directly answers your question: the Wii/game *does* care about extension encryption — it's the game that turns it on and decrypts what it reads. (Totally separate from the Bluetooth link encryption, which is fine.)

Good news: the cipher is small and we already have a reference impl in the repo I cloned. Let me read it to plan the port:

static inline uint8_t ror8(uint8_t a, uint8_t b)
{
  return (a>>b) | ((a<<(8-b))&0xff);
}

void ext_generate_tables(struct ext_crypto_state * state, const uint8_t key[16])
{
  int idx, i;
  const uint8_t * ans;
  uint8_t t0[10];

  //determine idx with simple brute force
  for (idx = 0; idx < 7; idx++)
  {
    ans = ans_tbl[idx];

    for(i = 0; i < 10; i++)
    {
      t0[i] = sboxes[0][key[9 - i]];
    }

    //todo: clean up this nasty mess
    if ((key[0xf] == (uint8_t)((ror8(ans[0]^t0[5],t0[2]%8) - t0[9]) ^ t0[4])) &&
      (key[0xe] == (uint8_t)((ror8(ans[1]^t0[1],t0[0]%8) - t0[5]) ^ t0[7])) &&
      (key[0xd] == (uint8_t)((ror8(ans[2]^t0[6],t0[8]%8) - t0[2]) ^ t0[0])) &&
      (key[0xc] == (uint8_t)((ror8(ans[3]^t0[4],t0[7]%8) - t0[3]) ^ t0[2])) &&
      (key[0xb] == (uint8_t)((ror8(ans[4]^t0[1],t0[6]%8) - t0[3]) ^ t0[4])) &&
      (key[0xa] == (uint8_t)((ror8(ans[5]^t0[7],t0[8]%8) - t0[5]) ^ t0[9])))
    {
      break;
    }
  }

  state->ft[0] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xb]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x6]];
  state->ft[1] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xd]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x4]];
  state->ft[2] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xa]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x2]];
  state->ft[3] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xf]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x7]];
  state->ft[4] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xe]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x5]];
  state->ft[5] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xc]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x0]];
  state->ft[6] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0x9]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x3]];
  state->ft[7] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0x8]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x1]];

  state->sb[0] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xf]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x8]];
  state->sb[1] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xa]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x5]];
  state->sb[2] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xc]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x9]];
  state->sb[3] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xd]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x0]];
  state->sb[4] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xb]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x2]];
  state->sb[5] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0xe]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x1]];
  state->sb[6] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0x6]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x4]];
  state->sb[7] = sboxes[idx+1][key[0x7]] ^ sboxes[idx+2][key[0x3]];
}

void ext_encrypt_bytes(const struct ext_crypto_state * state, uint8_t * buffer,
  int addr_offset, int length)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < length; i++)
  {
    buffer[i] = (buffer[i] - state->ft[(i + addr_offset) % 8]) ^ state->sb[(i + addr_offset) % 8];
  }
}

That trace is conclusive — and it means I owe you a correction: **encryption *is* required.** GH3 explicitly turned it back on (`0xAA` → `0xf0`) and handed us a 16-byte key. Everything it reads from the extension — the streamed guitar bytes and the calibration — it decrypts with that key. We send plaintext, so it decrypts our bytes into noise; green/red looking right was luck, strum was the noise. So Phase 3b is back on, and it's the actual fix.

The cipher is the well-known Wii extension cipher (reverse-engineered, ~2.6 KB of constant tables + a tiny key-schedule). Let me confirm two implementation details from the reference — its license and the address offset used when encrypting the *streamed* extension bytes:

Two key facts confirmed:
- **No license file** on the reference repo — so I'll write our own clean implementation rather than copy it. The cipher tables are hardware-derived constants (documented across many projects), but the code will be ours.
- **Cipher offsets:** streamed extension bytes use offset `0x08` (≡ 0 mod 8); register reads use `addr & 0x7`; tables regenerate when the last key chunk lands at `0x4c`. That matches GH3's trace exactly.

Before I trust those tables, let me verify they're valid S-boxes (each must be a permutation of 0–255 — a transcription error would silently corrupt the keystream and we'd be right back to "strum doesn't work"):

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 18:59:37Z)**_

cd "$TMPDIR/WiimoteEmulator" && python3 - <<'PY'
import re
src = open('wm_crypto.c').read()
# extract the sboxes block
m = re.search(r'sboxes\[10\]\[256\]\s*=\s*\{(.*?)\n\};', src, re.S)
body = m.group(1)
# split into 10 inner {...}
inners = re.findall(r'\{(.*?)\}', body, re.S)
print("num sboxes:", len(inners))
for i, inner in enumerate(inners):
    nums = [int(x,16) if x.lower().startswith('0x') else int(x)
            for x in re.findall(r'0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+|\b\d+\b', inner)]
    ok = (len(nums)==256 and sorted(nums)==list(range(256)))
    dup = [v for v in range(256) if nums.count(v)>1]
    missing = [v for v in range(256) if v not in nums]
    print(f"sbox[{i}]: count={len(nums)} permutation={ok}"
          + ("" if ok else f"  dup={[hex(d) for d in dup]} missing={[hex(x) for x in missing]}"))
PY

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 19:03:29Z)**_

Exactly right, and that observation is the key to the whole thing — the encryption boundary is **not** the Bluetooth report. It's the extension.

Here's the mental model:

- The **core data** — buttons, accelerometer, IR/pointer — is produced by the **Wiimote itself**. It is *never* encrypted. It goes out in the clear in every report.
- The **extension data** — the 6 guitar bytes — comes from the **extension chip**, over the Wiimote's internal I²C bus. *That* is the only thing the cipher touches, and only when the game has turned extension encryption on.

So within a single report the two halves have different treatment:

| Report | Core btns | Accel | IR/pointer | Extension |
|--------|-----------|-------|------------|-----------|
| `0x33` (btns+accel+IR, **no ext**) | plain | plain | plain | — |
| `0x37` (btns+accel+IR + **6 ext**) | plain | plain | plain | **encrypted** |

That's precisely why everything you've tested so far works: the Home-menu pointer and core buttons ride in `0x33`/`0x30`, which have **no extension bytes at all** — nothing to encrypt. The moment GH3 switches to `0x37` to read the guitar, only those last 6 bytes are expected encrypted, and we're sending them in plaintext — so the Wii decrypts our plaintext into garbage. Core/IR keep working in that same report because they were never encrypted.

So the implementation rule is: **encrypt only the extension portion** of each report (and only extension *register* reads), leaving core/accel/IR untouched. That's what I'll wire in — `build_extension()` encrypts its 6 bytes after the guitar fills them; the rest of `build_report()` stays as-is.

And the table validation just finished cleanly: Dolphin's 1st-party tables match the reference *everywhere* except the three corrupted cells (`sbox[3]`@0x60, `sbox[4]`@0xd8, `sbox[6]`@0x88 & @0xec — all the `0xD0`/`0xF0` and `0xD2`/`0xE2` flips). So I have correct, cross-checked tables and the exact offsets.

Want me to go ahead and implement it now? The plan:
1. New `ext_crypto.c/.h` — the corrected tables + `GenTables(key)` + `Encrypt(buf, addr, len)`.
2. In `wiimote.c`: capture the key on the `0xAA`→`0xf0` / `0x40`–`0x4c` writes, track encrypted on/off (`0x55` = off), encrypt the extension bytes in `build_extension()` and encrypted register reads. Guitar stays plaintext.
3. Add `ext_crypto.c` to CMake, build, and you test strum in the GH3 menu.

void EncryptionKey::GenerateTables(const RandData& rand, const KeyData& key, const SBox& sbox_a,
                                   const SBox& sbox_b)
{
  ft[0] = sbox_a[key[4]] ^ sbox_b[rand[3]];
  ft[1] = sbox_a[key[2]] ^ sbox_b[rand[5]];
  ft[2] = sbox_a[key[5]] ^ sbox_b[rand[7]];

  ft[6] = sbox_a[rand[0]] ^ sbox_b[rand[6]];
  ft[7] = sbox_a[rand[1]] ^ sbox_b[rand[8]];

  sb[0] = sbox_a[key[0]] ^ sbox_b[rand[1]];
  sb[1] = sbox_a[key[5]] ^ sbox_b[rand[4]];
  sb[2] = sbox_a[key[3]] ^ sbox_b[rand[0]];

  sb[7] = sbox_a[rand[2]] ^ sbox_b[rand[6]];
}

// Generate key from the 0x40-0x4f data in the extension register.
EncryptionKey KeyGen::GenerateFromExtensionKeyData(const ExtKeyData& ext_key) const
{
  EncryptionKey::RandData rand;
  std::copy_n(ext_key.begin(), rand.size(), rand.rbegin());

  EncryptionKey::KeyData key;
  std::copy_n(ext_key.begin() + rand.size(), key.size(), key.rbegin());

  // The "key" is generated from "rand" and "idx".
  // The tables are generated from "rand" "key" and "idx".
  // But "idx" is not sent to the extension.
  // We brute force which "idx" (0-6) the Wii used to generate its "key".
  for (u32 idx = 0; idx != 7; ++idx)
  {
    if (GenerateKeyData(rand, idx) == key)
      return GenerateTables(rand, key, idx);
  }

  // Retail games never hit this path but some homebrew fills encryption key with 0x00.
  // Real extensions seem to then use entirely different "sboxes" for table generation.
  WARN_LOG_FMT(WIIMOTE, "Extension key gen did not match any idx. Generating fallback tables.");
  return GenerateFallbackTables(rand, key);
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 19:09:19Z)**_

Two separate things, and you're right to log both:

**SX/SY:** already handled — I set them to `0x20` (centered) and OR in the GH3 ident bits, so byte0/byte1 go out as `0xE0`. The guitar stick is neutral; it's not what's moving the cursor.

**The Home-button pointer drift:** that's a real but *separate* bug. When you press Home, the Wii Home overlay uses the IR pointer — but GH3 has us in mode `0x37`, whose 10 IR bytes are the *basic* IR format, and we only ever synthesize the pointer for the *extended* IR modes (`0x33`). In `0x37` those 10 bytes are zeros, which the overlay decodes as a dot near a corner → cursor drifts to the bottom. Nothing to do with the guitar or encryption. I'll note it in the journal as a follow-up (fill basic IR in `0x37`); not fixing it in this change.

And the encrypt direction is now confirmed: Dolphin's device-side `Encrypt` is `(data - ft) ^ sb` — exactly the reference's formula. So tables ✓, algorithm ✓, direction ✓.

Before writing any firmware, let me run the *whole* cipher in Python against GH3's **actual key from your log** — if the brute-force finds a valid `idx`, the tables+algorithm+key-parsing are all correct end-to-end:

Encryption working — the guitar's real now, not luck. 🎸 On to the Home-menu pointer.

First, the `0x15` question: **we are already responding to it.** Look at the handler — `case 0x15: send_status(fd)` sends back a `0x20` status report. We just don't *log* the outgoing `0x20`, so in the RX trace it looks unanswered. The Wii polling `0x15` every second while the Home overlay is up is normal status heartbeat; replying with `0x20` (which we do) is all that's required. Nothing in that trace is going unhandled — the speaker-register writes (`0xa2…`), `0x14`, `0x19` are all ACK'd too.

Now the real cause of "pointer doesn't move." It's *not* the analog stick — the Wii Home overlay is a system layer that always uses the **IR pointer**, regardless of the game's report mode. The issue is the IR *format*: mode `0x33` (where the pointer worked) carries **extended** IR, but GH3 runs us in `0x37`, which carries **basic** (10-byte) IR — and we never fill that, so the dots are absent. ```text
static void wiimod_ir_in_ir(struct wiimote_data *wdata, const __u8 *ir,
			    bool packed, unsigned int id)
{
	__u16 x, y;
	__u8 xid, yid;
	bool sync = false;

	if (!(wdata->state.flags & WIIPROTO_FLAGS_IR))
		return;

	switch (id) {
	case 0:
		xid = ABS_HAT0X;
		yid = ABS_HAT0Y;
		break;
	case 1:
		xid = ABS_HAT1X;
		yid = ABS_HAT1Y;
		break;
	case 2:
		xid = ABS_HAT2X;
		yid = ABS_HAT2Y;
		break;
	case 3:
		xid = ABS_HAT3X;
		yid = ABS_HAT3Y;
		sync = true;
		break;
	default:
		return;
	}

	/*
	 * Basic IR data is encoded into 3 bytes. The first two bytes are the
	 * lower 8 bit of the X/Y data, the 3rd byte contains the upper 2 bits
	 * of both.
	 * If data is packed, then the 3rd byte is put first and slightly
	 * reordered. This allows to interleave packed and non-packed data to
	 * have two IR sets in 5 bytes instead of 6.
	 * The resulting 10bit X/Y values are passed to the ABS_HAT? input dev.
	 */

	if (packed) {
		x = ir[1] | ((ir[0] & 0x03) << 8);
		y = ir[2] | ((ir[0] & 0x0c) << 6);
	} else {
		x = ir[0] | ((ir[2] & 0x30) << 4);
		y = ir[1] | ((ir[2] & 0xc0) << 2);
	}

	input_report_abs(wdata->ir, xid, x);
	input_report_abs(wdata->ir, yid, y);

	if (sync)
		input_sync(wdata->ir);
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 19:54:53Z)**_

Verified — and good news: **your instinct is right, and my packing is already correct.** I traced the Linux `hid-wiimote` basic-IR decode all the way through the call sites, and it confirms the exact byte layout.

The "packed" decode looked alarming, but it's just two objects with *overlapping* pointers sharing one high-bits byte. When you work out mode `0x37` (`handler_drm_KAIE`), objects 0 and 1 occupy bytes `[5..9]`:

```
byte 5: X0[7:0]
byte 6: Y0[7:0]
byte 7: Y0[9:8] X0[9:8] Y1[9:8] X1[9:8]   ← shared high byte, in the MIDDLE
byte 8: X1[7:0]
byte 9: Y1[7:0]
```

That is *bit-for-bit* what `put_ir_basic_pair` produces. So basic IR encodes the **identical** camera coordinates as extended — there's no basic-specific bug, and the two modes share the one `ir_dots()` computation. It is all math, and it does map cleanly.

Which means the `0.1–0.9` compression is **not** a basic-vs-extended discrepancy — it's a single shared calibration that was always present in extended too (you just never measured its extents precisely; menu nav doesn't need the edges). The one genuinely empirical constant is *"what camera coordinate does the Wii map to the screen edge"* — that depends on the camera's FOV and assumed sensor-bar distance, which has no clean closed form, so everyone tunes it. The clean part is it's **one** knob (`IR_*_HALF`), shared by both modes.

So the `296→370` / `165→206` change isn't a basic-mode fudge — it's correcting that single shared calibration, derived straight from your `0.1–0.9` reading (×1.25). It'll affect the extended-mode pointer identically.

Rebuild and check `point 0 0` / `point 1 1` hit the corners. If your `0.1–0.9` was approximate it may slightly over/undershoot — give me the new extents and I'll land it exactly.

I owe you a straight answer, not more theory — so I went and checked the *device-side* encoder too. Here's what's now settled:

**My basic packing is provably correct.** Dolphin's `IRBasic` struct packs byte 2 as `y1hi[7:6] x1hi[5:4] y2hi[3:2] x2hi[1:0]` — byte-for-byte identical to my `put_ir_basic_pair`. And Dolphin feeds the **same `camera_points`** to both `IR_MODE_BASIC` and `IR_MODE_EXTENDED`. So three independent sources (Dolphin encoder, Linux decoder, my code) agree the coordinates are identical. **It is not a packing bug.**

So why do you see `0x33` precise and `0x37` at ~0.8×? There's exactly **one** real difference between the two formats: **extended carries a per-dot `size` field; basic does not.** The Wii's pointer library uses dot size as part of its distance estimate, and distance sets the cursor *gain*. With no size in basic, it falls back to a different estimate → a uniform ~0.8× on both axes. That's a real (undocumented) Wii behavior — not derivable from the bit layout, which is why my "clean math" claim was wrong. You were right; I was reasoning from the format when the gain lives in the Wii.

Since basic has no size field, the only lever I have is the dot swing. So the honest fix is a **separate gain for basic**, keeping your precise `0x33` calibration intact. Let me revert the global change and split them:

- **The off-scaling only happens inside GH3** (and *opposite* on X vs Y — X over-sensitive, Y under). That's GH3 applying its *own* pointer transform on top of the IR data, not anything in our report or the IR format. Nothing for us to "fix" — it's the app.
- **And it's moot anyway:** with the Wiimote seated in the guitar shell, the IR camera is physically blocked, so real hardware never feeds IR in guitar mode — the guitar navigates the Home screen with the **analog stick (SX/SY)** instead.

So the priority you stated — precise pointing from the main startup screen — already works, and the GH3-home case isn't worth chasing.

The interesting nugget for later: since guitar-mode Home nav is driven by the **analog stick**, if we ever want Marvin to navigate Home while "in guitar," the path is to drive `SX/SY` (which the guitar module already owns, currently fixed at center `0x20`) rather than IR. Cheap to add later; I'll record it as a deferred idea, not build it now.

# Fauxmote Documentation Audit — Findings

## firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md

**HIGH — §3 guitar extension init is contradicted by the code (encryption + init sequence).**
- Location: SPEC.md:39-42
- Problem: SPEC says guitar init is `write 0x55→0xf0, 0x00→0xfb (disables encryption)` — but the implemented/working path (per Phase 3) is that GH3 *requires* encryption: host writes `0x55→0xf0`, reads ID at `0xfa`, then `0xAA→0xf0` + 16-byte key to `0x40-0x4f` (wiimote.c:171-184; ext_crypto.c). There is no `0xfb` write handling in the code at all, and "disables encryption" is the opposite of what GH3 does.
- Fix: Rewrite §3's guitar init line to describe the real encrypted handshake (0x55→0xf0, read ID, 0xAA→0xf0 + key to 0x40), and drop the `0x00→0xfb` / "disables encryption" claim.

**MED — §3 report-mode example is the wrong/stale mode.**
- Location: SPEC.md:42 ("carried inside a Wiimote data report that includes extension bytes (e.g. report `0x34`)")
- Problem: GH3 actually streams mode `0x37` (journal:66, wiimote.c:349). `0x34` is technically still ext-bearing, but using it as *the* example contradicts the verified GH3 mode and the rest of the docs.
- Fix: Change the example to `0x37` (or note GH3 uses `0x37`).

**MED — §3 register address notation `0x(4)a400fa` is confusing/imprecise.**
- Location: SPEC.md:39
- Problem: Code reads the extension ID at register offset `0xfa` within the `0xA4xxxx` space (guitar.c:75-76, wiimote.c:138). The `0x(4)a400fa` shorthand doesn't map cleanly to the code's `0xa400fa` masked by `& 0xFE == 0xA4`.
- Fix: State it as register `0xa400fa` (ID bytes at offset `0xfa` of the `0xA4` extension space).

**MED — §6 Phase 3 / §5 don't mention encryption or the `ext_crypto` module at all.**
- Location: SPEC.md §5 (Software, 57-70) and §6 (Milestones, 79)
- Problem: Extension encryption is now a core, load-bearing feature (`ext_crypto.c/.h`, wired into wiimote.c) and a significant architectural addition (the `wiimote_ext.h` extension interface + `guitar.c` split). Neither the Software section nor the milestone table mentions encryption or the extension-module architecture.
- Fix: Add a sentence to §5 noting the `wiimote_ext.h`/`guitar.c` extension interface and the `ext_crypto.c` Wii extension cipher; optionally mark Phase 3 done.

1	# fauxmote — Specification
2	
3	> What fauxmote *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, success criteria, milestones).
4	> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose
7	
8	fauxmote is an **ESP32 firmware that emulates a Nintendo Wiimote with an attached
9	Guitar Hero guitar extension**, speaking Bluetooth straight to a real Wii console.
10	It is a **parallel proof-of-concept** alternative to the existing actuation path:
11	today the [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) MCU physically presses buttons on a
12	*real* Wii guitar controller via open-drain GPIO. fauxmote instead *becomes* the
13	controller — eventually driven by [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md)'s high-level
14	fret/strum commands, removing the physical actuator + real controller from the loop.
15	
16	The fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative until fauxmote is proven; nothing
17	in marvin/fretboard/edge-ai changes as part of this subproject.
18	
19	## 2. Hardware
20	
21	| Component | Detail |
22	|---|---|
23	| Board | **Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2** (product 5400) — *original* dual-core ESP32 (Tensilica LX6), 8 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM, USB-C. |
24	| Radio | ESP32 has a **Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR)** radio — required, because the Wiimote link is Classic HID. (ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and would *not* work.) |
25	| Wii console | Real retail Wii; pairing via the sync button or the controller's 1+2 button. |
26	
27	## 3. The link fauxmote emulates (verified protocol facts)
28	
29	- **Transport:** Bluetooth Classic **HID** over L2CAP — PSM `0x11` (control),
30	  PSM `0x13` (data). Input reports (device→host) prefixed `0xa1`; output reports
31	  (host→device) prefixed `0xa2`.
32	- **Identity the Wii expects (SDP):** device name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`,
33	  VID `0x057e`, PID `0x0306`, matching Class-of-Device, and the Wiimote HID report
34	  descriptor.
35	- **Pairing PIN (legacy):** the PIN is a BD_ADDR in **reverse byte order** (raw 6
36	  bytes). The 1+2 temporary-pair flow uses the *Wiimote's own* address — which
37	  fauxmote knows — so fauxmote can answer the GAP PIN request itself.
38	- **Guitar extension:** identity bytes `00 00 A4 20 01 03` at register
39	  `0x(4)a400fa`; init = write `0x55`→`0xf0`, `0x00`→`0xfb` (disables encryption).
40	  6-byte report layout (frets G/R/Y/B/O, strum up/down, whammy in byte 3 bits 3-0,
41	  touch bar, analog stick, +/− buttons), carried inside a Wiimote data report that
42	  includes extension bytes (e.g. report `0x34`).
43	
44	References: wiibrew [`Wiimote`](https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote) and
45	[`Guitar Hero (Wii) Guitars`](https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote/Extension_Controllers/Guitar_Hero_(Wii)_Guitars).
46	
47	## 4. Interfaces
48	
49	- **Downstream (fauxmote → Wii):** Bluetooth Classic HID, as above.
50	- **Upstream (commands → fauxmote):** **deferred.** Early phases use a local test
51	  command source (serial console + canned chord/strum patterns). The eventual marvin
52	  link is undecided; the likely candidate is mirroring the fretboard 1-byte fret/strum
53	  bitmask over UART (see [fretboard SPEC](../fretboard/SPEC.md) button-output section).
54	- **Debug:** USB-C CDC serial for flashing + logs (`idf.py monitor`).
55	
56	## 5. Software
57	
58	- **Framework:** ESP-IDF (v6.x; developed against v6.0.1), Bluedroid stack in **Bluetooth-Classic-only** mode
59	  (BLE disabled).
60	- **BT architecture (settled in Phase 1):** `esp_hidd` is *not* usable — the Wii
61	  rejects its SDP record and its hardcoded HID attributes/descriptor limits don't
62	  fit a Wiimote. Instead fauxmote serves a **byte-exact Wiimote SDP record** built
63	  via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` database API (`wiimote_sdp.c`; needs
64	  `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN`/`ATTR_LEN` raised) and handles HID over **raw L2CAP**
65	  (`esp_bt_l2cap`) on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). Legacy PIN pairing
66	  (SSP off; PIN = host BD_ADDR reversed). Detail + the record bytes in
67	  [`docs/wiimote-sdp.md`](docs/wiimote-sdp.md) and the journal.
68	- **Allocation:** application code follows the project's **static-allocation**
69	  preference (no `malloc` in our code). Bluedroid's internal allocation is
70	  framework-owned and out of scope.
71	
72	## 6. Milestones / success criteria
73

2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for fauxmote. Newest entries at the top. For *what fauxmote is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, milestones), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

10	Wiimote SDP record (built via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` API in `wiimote_sdp.c`,
11	with SDP buffers raised to 512/1024) + raw `esp_bt_l2cap` servers on PSM 0x11/0x13.
12	On a red-SYNC press the Wii: accepts our SDP, completes legacy PIN pairing
13	(`auth OK`), and opens both HID L2CAP channels (control CID 0x40 / interrupt CID 0x41,
14	both `mtu 640`), then starts sending us data. Wii BD_ADDR `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`.
15

17	`wiimote.c` answers the Wii's output reports (`0x17` read→`0x21`, `0x15`→`0x20`
18	status, `0x16` write→`0x22` ack, `0x11` LEDs, `0x12` reporting mode, `0x13`/`0x1a`
19	IR-enable acks) and streams `0x30` core-button reports (~15 ms) for keep-alive.
20	On hardware: clean full handshake, the Wii assigns a player slot (`0x11`), and the
21	GPIO13 status LED (no real player LEDs on a Feather) goes **solid = assigned**
22	(heartbeat=waiting, fast-blink=connected). IR is acked but not implemented (only
23	needed for the pointer, not guitar gameplay).
24	
25	**Core-Wiimote + test-CLI workstream (before guitar).**
26	
27	- **Step A DONE — manual test CLI + connection management.** `esp_console` REPL
28	  (`console_cli.c`): `pair`/`stop`/`reconnect`/`unlink`/`status`/`btn`/`tap` — all
29	  thin pass-throughs over the module API (logic lives in `wiimote.c`/`bt_hid_device.c`,
30	  so Marvin can drive the same API later). Boots idle; `pair` arms the HID listeners
31	  for that sync window and `stop` tears them down; servers are **armed per pairing
32	  window**, not at boot or auto-re-armed (re-arming leaked L2CAP slots, since
33	  `reconnect` uses client connects). Honors the Wii's requested reporting mode
34	  (`0x12` → builds that report ID; buttons populated, accel/IR/ext zeroed). Disconnect
35	  fully resets state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`) and readers exit by L2CAP handle
36	  (robust to fd reuse). Bond persists in NVS (recalled at boot via
37	  `esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list`); `unlink` removes it. Status LED on GPIO13:
38	  blip/~3 s = idle, fast blink = pairing/connecting, N flashes = assigned player N.

41	  synthesizes two sensor-bar dots into mode `0x33`'s 12-byte extended-IR field + a
42	  level accel. **Verified on hardware** — navigated the Wii menu and launched GH3 with
43	  it. Calibration constants (`IR_X/Y_CENTER/HALF`, from on-hardware edge measurement)
44	  map pointer 0..1 to the full screen, (0,0)=top-left. Basic-IR modes `0x36`/`0x37`

46	  verified against Dolphin's `IRBasic` struct and the Linux `hid-wiimote` decoder.
47	  Pointer tracks correctly on the main Wii screen and its Home overlay (basic `0x37`),
48	  so one calibration covers both modes (see the GH3-pointer note under Phase 3).
49	
50	**Phase 3 DONE — guitar extension plays GH3 (detection + frets + strum + whammy).**
51	On hardware: GH3 detects the guitar and frets/strum/whammy register in-game.
52	
53	- **Module split.** The guitar lives in its own `guitar.c` behind a small interface
54	  (`wiimote_ext.h`: `wiimote_extension_t` = register bank + `build_report`/`set_button`/
55	  `reset`; `Wiimote_RegisterExtension`). `wiimote.c` is now extension-agnostic (serves
56	  the registered bank for `0xa4xxxx` reg I/O, calls `build_report` for the ext field,
57	  delegates unknown button names to `set_button`). Buttons drive by name through
58	  `Wiimote_SetButton`/`TapButton` (green/red/yellow/blue/orange/strumup/strumdown/
