```text
60	  nunchuk/classic later is just another self-registering `*.c`.
61	- **Report bit layout** (buttons **active-low**, rest = 1; verified against wiibrew +
62	  Linux `hid-wiimote`): byte0/1 = stick X/Y (bits5-0); **byte0/1 bits7-6 = 1 to
63	  identify a GH3 Les Paul** (0 = GHWT — with them clear GH3 treats us as GHWT and
64	  ignores the strum bar, which cost real debugging time); byte2 touchbar; byte3
65	  whammy; byte4 bit6 BD / bit4 B− / bit2 B+; byte5 bit7 BO / bit6 BR / bit5 BB /
66	  bit4 BG / bit3 BY / bit2 pedal / bit0 BU. GH3 streams mode **`0x37`** (not `0x34`);
67	  the ext field is filled for every ext-bearing mode (`0x32/34/35/36/37/3d`).
68	- **ENCRYPTION is required and now implemented** (`ext_crypto.c/.h`). GH3's actual
69	  handshake (from a register trace), *not* the old `0→0x40` init the plan guessed:
70	  `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID at `0xfa` in the clear (decide GH3 vs GHWT) →
71	  `0xAA`→`0xf0` (re-enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. Everything the game then
72	  reads (streamed ext bytes + the `0x20` calibration) is decrypted with that key, so
73	  plaintext reads as garbage. The base Wiimote captures the key, derives the ft/sb
74	  tables, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes at reg offset `0x08`; reg
75	  reads at `addr & 7`); the guitar module stays plaintext. Cipher = the marcan Wii
76	  extension cipher; **rnconrad's `wm_crypto.c` tables are corrupted** (sbox[3]@0x60,
77	  [4]@0xd8, [6]@0x88/0xec — `0xD0`/`0xF0` & `0xD2`/`0xE2` flips, not valid
78	  permutations), so the tables were taken from **Dolphin's 1st-party** set and the
79	  algorithm verified term-for-term against Dolphin; round-trip validated against GH3's
80	  real key (idx 0 matched, encrypt→decrypt identity). Earlier "green/red work without
81	  encryption" was a decryption fluke.
82	- **Guitar-mode pointer (informational, not pursued).** Basic-IR pointer is correct on
83	  the main Wii screen + its Home overlay. *Inside GH3*, the Home-overlay cursor scales
84	  wrong — X over-sensitive, Y under, **opposite per axis** — which is GH3 applying its
85	  own pointer transform, not our IR (packing is verified identical to extended). Moot
86	  in practice: **with the Wiimote seated in the guitar the IR camera is physically
87	  blocked**, so guitar-mode Home nav uses the **analog stick (SX/SY)** instead. Kept a
88	  single IR calibration. Deferred idea: drive `SX/SY` (guitar module already owns them,
89	  fixed at center `0x20`) for guitar-mode Home navigation if Marvin ever needs it.
90	
91	**Link stability (done):** idle disconnects are fixed — Bluedroid's JV idle→sniff
92	delay (default 5 s) is overridden to 65 s via a `-D BTA_FTC_OPS_IDLE_TO_SNIFF_DELAY_MS`
93	in the top-level CMake (`#ifndef`'d `#define`; the timeout field is UINT16 + a 197 ms
94	offset, so stay < ~65338). With sniff effectively off the link stays active (Wii keeps
95	polling), so no supervision timeouts and no BTA PM-slot leak (the leak that previously
96	forced a power-cycle). A persistent **auto-reconnect** task re-initiates the link on
97	any unexpected drop (3 s × 8 then every 8 s), suppressed by `stop`/`unlink`.
98	
99	**OPEN — GH3 game-launch handoff (needs a BT sniffer):** when a game disc boots, the
100	Wii goes HID-silent toward fauxmote for many seconds, then drops the link (`rsn 0x08`).
101	Auto-reconnect re-establishes it, but the session isn't reliably usable in-game.
102	A real Wiimote rides the handoff with a quick ~2 s LED off/on. fauxmote's own logs
103	don't show *why* the Wii goes silent on us vs a real Wiimote — there's no command we
104	visibly mishandle (zero RX reports during the gap). Diagnosing needs a Bluetooth
105	sniffer to diff a real Wiimote vs fauxmote through the GH3 launch. **Workaround for
106	now: restart fauxmote after the game has started** (a fresh boot reconnects cleanly).
107	The recurring `mode 3 … BASIC mode` reconnect warning is likely a red herring (real
108	Wiimotes use Basic-mode L2CAP for HID). Revisit after the guitar extension — GH3 may
109	engage the controller differently once it sees a guitar.
110	
111	**Other notes:**
112	- **Keep-awake:** the Wii idle-disconnects on lack of *input*; streaming reports +
113	  occasional button activity keeps it alive (free during gameplay).
114	- **Caveat:** a Wiimote cannot power a Wii on from standby (BT radio off); "wake" only
115	  means reconnecting while the console is already running.
116	
117	Phase progression and success criteria are in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) §6.

125	| 2026-06-13 | **Extension encryption is mandatory for GH3 and implemented in the base Wiimote (`ext_crypto.c`); the guitar module stays plaintext.** GH3's real key handshake (register trace): `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID `0xfa` in clear → `0xAA`→`0xf0` (enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. The base captures the key, derives ft/sb, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes @ offset `0x08`; reg reads @ `addr & 7`). | Everything GH3 reads from the extension is decrypted with that key, so plaintext is garbage (the "green/red worked unencrypted" observation was a decryption coincidence). Encryption is a generic Wiimote feature (nunchuk/classic encrypt too), so it belongs in the base, not the guitar. Corrects the plan's guess that GH3 used the old `0→0x40` init. |
126	| 2026-06-13 | **Cipher tables come from Dolphin's 1st-party set, not `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator`'s `wm_crypto.c`.** rnconrad's S-boxes are corrupted (sbox[3]@0x60, [4]@0xd8, [6]@0x88/0xec are `0xD0`/`0xF0` & `0xD2`/`0xE2` transcription flips → not valid permutations). Used Dolphin's `keygen_sbox_1st_party` + `sboxes_1st_party[8]`; verified the key-schedule/encrypt algorithm term-for-term against Dolphin and round-tripped GH3's real key (idx 0, encrypt→decrypt identity). | Wrong table bytes silently corrupt the keystream → undebuggable "notes are garbage." Dolphin is GPL and validated against real games; the marcan tables are reverse-engineered hardware constants (facts), reproduced with our own code. |
127	| 2026-06-13 | **Guitar is a self-registering extension module behind `wiimote_ext.h`; `wiimote.c` is extension-agnostic.** `wiimote_extension_t` = register bank + `build_report`/`set_button`/`reset`; `Wiimote_RegisterExtension`. Buttons drive by name via `Wiimote_SetButton`/`TapButton`. | Plans for other extensions (nunchuk/classic) as drop-in `*.c` files, keeps the base generic, and keeps the CLI as thin pass-throughs over the same API Marvin will use. |
128	| 2026-06-13 | **Byte0/1 bits 7-6 must be set (GH3 Les Paul ident); single IR calibration kept.** Clear ident bits make GH3 treat us as a GHWT guitar and ignore the strum bar. Basic-IR pointer is correct on the main Wii screen with the same calibration as extended; the GH3-internal Home-overlay mis-scaling is GH3's own transform and is moot (IR is physically blocked when the Wiimote is in the guitar — guitar-mode Home nav uses the analog stick). | Found by hardware testing. No second/basic-mode calibration: the format packing is provably identical to extended (Dolphin + Linux), so the only real difference (GH3) isn't ours to fix and doesn't matter on real hardware. |
129	| 2026-06-12 | **`esp_hidd` is a dead end for Wii emulation; the only working ESP-IDF path is a custom SDP record (internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) + raw L2CAP HID on PSM 0x11/0x13 (`esp_bt_l2cap`), with the hardcoded SDP buffer raised.** Two independent walls: (1) the Wii rejects esp_hidd's record even with a small descriptor (wrong HID attribute values — subclass/reconnect-initiate/etc., which esp_hidd hardcodes and doesn't expose); (2) the real 217-byte descriptor can't even be registered — `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` (the per-record attribute pad) is **hardcoded 300** (`sdp_db.c:495`, `bluedroid_user_config.h`; no menuconfig), and the full Wiimote record is ~463 B → `SDP_AddAttribute fail … ID 518`. Confirmed feasible building blocks in IDF v6.0.1: `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/`SDP_AddSequence` (private `stack/sdp_api.h`) and `esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(psm)`. | Bluedroid is the only Classic-BT stack on ESP32, and its public APIs can't host an arbitrary SDP record (`esp_sdp` RAW is search-only). So the path requires *unsupported internals*: raise `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` via an injected `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN` compile define, build the exact Wiimote record with the internal SDP DB API, skip esp_hidd, and serve HID over raw L2CAP + hand-rolled HIDP. Heavy + fragile across IDF updates, but it's the real route. The exact 463-byte record + 217-byte descriptor are saved at [`wiimote-sdp.md`](wiimote-sdp.md). |
130	| 2026-06-12 | **Q1 resolved: ESP-IDF `esp_hidd`'s auto-generated SDP record is NOT accepted by the Wii → pivot to raw L2CAP (listen on PSM 0x11 control / 0x13 data) + a hand-built SDP record matching a real Wiimote.** Verbose Bluedroid logs: the Wii opens an ACL link, connects to our SDP server (PSM 1), reads our records (we send 14/250/37-byte SDP responses), then disconnects the SDP channel and terminates the ACL (`rsn 0x13` = remote user terminated) **without ever opening the HID PSMs**. SSP was confirmed off this round (legacy pairing) and discovery works (limited-discoverable + COD `0x002504`), so SDP content is the only remaining blocker. Wii BD_ADDR observed: `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`. | The Wii validates the SDP record against a real Wiimote's; esp_hidd's generic HID record (right VID/PID, wrong attributes + HID descriptor) fails the check, so it never proceeds to HID. Matches why `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator` replaces the host BT stack to serve the exact SDP. Open: whether ESP-IDF lets us serve a fully custom SDP record (esp_sdp API vs internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) and listen on the fixed HID PSMs via `esp_bt_l2cap`. |
131	| 2026-06-12 | **Phase 1 first attempt uses ESP-IDF's unified `esp_hidd` BT-classic HID device wearing the Wiimote identity, not a hand-rolled raw-L2CAP/SDP stack.** `bt_hid_device.c`: `esp_hidd_dev_init(ESP_HID_TRANSPORT_BT)` with VID `0x057e`/PID `0x0306`/version `0x0100`/name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`, COD set to `0x002504` (peripheral/joystick), a minimal vendor-defined report map (just report IDs 0x30 in / 0x12 out), **SSP disabled** (`CONFIG_BT_SSP_ENABLED=n`) for legacy PIN pairing, and a GAP `PIN_REQ` handler that replies with the requesting host's BD_ADDR reversed. | The stack already implements HIDP + L2CAP (PSM 0x11/0x13) + auth, so this is the cheapest probe of Q1: if a real Wii connects + authenticates against the auto-generated SDP, we avoid hand-building raw SDP entirely. If it rejects it, fall back to raw L2CAP + the exact SDP record from `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator` (cloned locally for byte-exact bytes; WebFetch can't reproduce the ~463-byte blob). |
132	| 2026-06-12 | **Target the console-SYNC *bonding* flow, not the 1+2 temporary flow.** PIN handler returns the connecting host's (Wii's) BD_ADDR reversed (`param->pin_req.bda` byte-reversed). | Bonding (red SYNC button under the Wii's SD cover + controller in sync mode) is how a controller gets *persistently* registered, which is what a robot wants. The 1+2 flow is one-time/temporary and uses the controller's own address instead. Resolves Q2. |
133	| 2026-06-12 | **Build fauxmote as a parallel, independent proof-of-concept subproject; the fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative.** New top-level firmware subproject `firmware/fauxmote/`. | Device-side Wiimote *emulation* to a real Wii is rare/novel (host-side use is common), so de-risk it in isolation before touching marvin/fretboard/edge-ai. Nothing in the existing actuation path changes until fauxmote is proven. |
134	| 2026-06-12 | **Framework = ESP-IDF (v6.x; v6.0.1 installed), Bluedroid in Bluetooth-Classic-only mode (BLE disabled).** | Wiimote uses Bluetooth Classic HID; ESP-IDF exposes the BT-Classic HID-device API (`esp_hidd_api.h`), custom SDP records, BD_ADDR control, and raw L2CAP — all of which emulation needs. Arduino-ESP32's BT-Classic HID-device support is too thin for the custom SDP/descriptor the Wiimote requires. |
135	| 2026-06-12 | **Board = Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2 (product 5400); its *original* ESP32 is the load-bearing choice.** | The original ESP32 has a Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR) radio. ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and cannot emulate a Wiimote. Confirmed the product 5400 is the Feather V2 (not a QT Py S3). |
136	| 2026-06-12 | **marvin↔fauxmote command link is deferred; early phases use a local test command source.** | Lets the hard part (ESP32↔Wii Bluetooth emulation) be developed and validated standalone. The likely eventual link mirrors the fretboard 1-byte fret/strum bitmask over UART, but that's a later-session decision. |
```

```text
129	        left -= chunk;

136	static void read_register(int fd, uint32_t offset, uint16_t size)
137	{
138	    bool ext = (s_ext && ((offset >> 16) & 0xFE) == 0xA4);
139	    uint32_t addr = offset;
140	    uint16_t left = size;
141	    while (left > 0) {
142	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(addr & 0xFF);
143	        uint8_t chunk = left > 16 ? 16 : (uint8_t)left;
144	        if ((int)idx + chunk > 256) chunk = (uint8_t)(256 - idx);
145	        if (ext) {
146	            uint8_t buf[16];
147	            memcpy(buf, &s_ext->regs[idx], chunk);
148	            if (s_crypt_on) {
149	                ExtCrypto_Encrypt(&s_crypt, buf, idx, chunk);  /* data is read encrypted */
150	            }
151	            send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, buf);
152	        } else {
153	            send_read_data(fd, chunk - 1, 0x00, (uint16_t)addr, NULL);
154	        }
155	        addr += chunk;
156	        left -= chunk;
157	        if (idx + chunk >= 256) break;
158	    }
159	}

164	        return;   /* only the extension register space is backed */
165	    }
166	    uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(offset & 0xFF);
167	    for (int i = 0; i < size && (idx + i) < 256; i++) {
168	        s_ext->regs[idx + i] = data[i];
169	    }
170	
171	    /* Extension encryption handshake. The host writes 0x55→0xf0 to disable, or
172	     * 0xAA→0xf0 then a 16-byte key to 0x40-0x4f to enable. */
173	    if (idx == 0xf0 && size >= 1) {
174	        if (data[0] == 0x55) {
175	            s_crypt_on = s_crypt_armed = false;
176	        } else if (data[0] == 0xAA) {
177	            s_crypt_armed = true;
178	        }
179	    }
180	    if (s_crypt_armed && idx >= 0x40 && idx <= 0x4F) {
181	        ExtCrypto_GenTables(&s_crypt, &s_ext->regs[0x40]);  /* last key chunk completes it */
182	        s_crypt_on = true;
183	    }
184	}

208	        }
209	        s_streaming = true;
210	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "reporting mode 0x%02x (continuous=%d)", s_report_mode, s_reporting_continuous);
211	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
212	        break;
213	    case 0x10:                      /* rumble only */
214	    case 0x13: case 0x1A:           /* IR camera enable */
215	    case 0x14: case 0x19:           /* speaker enable / mute */
216	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
217	        break;
218	    case 0x15:                      /* status request */
219	        send_status(fd);
220	        break;
221	    case 0x16:                      /* write memory/registers */
222	        if (plen >= 5) {
223	            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
224	            uint8_t wsize = p[4];
225	            if (p[0] & 0x04) write_register(offset, wsize, &p[5]);
226	        }
227	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
228	        break;
229	    case 0x17:                      /* read memory/registers */
230	        if (plen >= 6) {
231	            uint32_t offset = ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
232	            uint16_t size = (uint16_t)((p[4] << 8) | p[5]);
233	            if (p[0] & 0x04) {
234	                read_register(fd, offset, size);
235	            } else {
236	                read_eeprom(fd, offset, size);
237	            }
238	        }
239	        break;
240	    default:
241	        send_ack(fd, report, 0x00);
242	        break;
243	    }
244	}
245	
246	static void set_accel_level(uint8_t *a)
247	{
248	    a[0] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* X = 0 g */
249	    a[1] = ACCEL_NEUTRAL;   /* Y = 0 g */
250	    a[2] = 0xA0;            /* Z = +1 g (held level, no roll) */
251	}
252	
253	/* One extended-IR object: X/Y are 10-bit camera coords (1024x768), or x<0 = "not
254	 * visible". 3rd byte packs Y[9:8], X[9:8], size. */
255	static void put_ir_object(uint8_t *o, int x, int y, int size)
256	{
257	    if (x < 0) {
258	        o[0] = o[1] = o[2] = 0xFF;
259	        return;
260	    }
261	    o[0] = (uint8_t)(x & 0xFF);
262	    o[1] = (uint8_t)(y & 0xFF);
263	    o[2] = (uint8_t)((((y >> 8) & 0x03) << 6) | (((x >> 8) & 0x03) << 4) | (size & 0x0F));
264	}
265	
266	/* Synthesize the two sensor-bar dots from the pointer state (camera is 1024x768,
267	 * mirrored vs the screen). Returns false (dots left untouched) when the pointer is
268	 * inactive. If an axis comes out inverted on hardware, flip the (… - …) terms. */
269	static bool ir_dots(int *x0, int *y0, int *x1, int *y1)
270	{
271	    if (!s_point_active) {
272	        return false;
273	    }
274	    int midx = IR_X_CENTER + (int)((0.5f - s_point_x) * (2 * IR_X_HALF));
275	    int midy = IR_Y_CENTER + (int)((s_point_y - 0.5f) * (2 * IR_Y_HALF));
276	    const int sep = 128;                     /* half sensor-bar separation, camera px */
277	    if (midy < 0) midy = 0;
278	    if (midy > 767) midy = 767;
279	    *x0 = (midx - sep < 0) ? 0 : midx - sep;
280	    *x1 = (midx + sep > 1023) ? 1023 : midx + sep;
281	    *y0 = *y1 = midy;
282	    return true;
283	}
284	
285	/* Extended IR (12 bytes = 4 objects): two pointer dots, two not visible. */
286	static void build_ir_extended(uint8_t *dst)
287	{
288	    int x0 = -1, y0 = 0, x1 = -1, y1 = 0;
289	    ir_dots(&x0, &y0, &x1, &y1);
290	    put_ir_object(&dst[0], x0, y0, 4);
291	    put_ir_object(&dst[3], x1, y1, 4);
292	    put_ir_object(&dst[6], -1, 0, 0);
293	    put_ir_object(&dst[9], -1, 0, 0);
294	}
295	
296	/* Basic IR packs two objects into 5 bytes (X/Y high bits share byte 2). x<0 = not
297	 * visible (max coord). */
298	static void put_ir_basic_pair(uint8_t *o, int xa, int ya, int xb, int yb)
299	{
300	    if (xa < 0) { xa = ya = 0x3FF; }
301	    if (xb < 0) { xb = yb = 0x3FF; }
302	    o[0] = (uint8_t)(xa & 0xFF);
303	    o[1] = (uint8_t)(ya & 0xFF);
304	    o[2] = (uint8_t)((((ya >> 8) & 3) << 6) | (((xa >> 8) & 3) << 4)
305	                   | (((yb >> 8) & 3) << 2) | ((xb >> 8) & 3));
306	    o[3] = (uint8_t)(xb & 0xFF);
307	    o[4] = (uint8_t)(yb & 0xFF);
308	}
309	
310	/* Basic IR (10 bytes = 4 objects, packed in pairs): same two dots as extended. */
311	static void build_ir_basic(uint8_t *dst)
312	{
313	    int x0 = -1, y0 = 0, x1 = -1, y1 = 0;
314	    ir_dots(&x0, &y0, &x1, &y1);
315	    put_ir_basic_pair(&dst[0], x0, y0, x1, y1);
316	    put_ir_basic_pair(&dst[5], -1, 0, -1, 0);
317	}
318	
319	/* Fill the registered extension's bytes at dst, if an extension is attached. */
320	static void build_extension(uint8_t *dst)
321	{
322	    if (s_ext && s_ext_connected && s_ext->build_report) {
323	        s_ext->build_report(dst);
324	        if (s_crypt_on) {
325	            ExtCrypto_Encrypt(&s_crypt, dst, EXT_DATA_OFFSET, s_ext->report_len);
326	        }
327	    }
328	}
329	
330	/* Build the input report the Wii's current mode expects: core buttons in the first
331	 * two bytes (except 0x3d), level accelerometer where present, extended IR from the
332	 * pointer state, and the extension's bytes in the extension field. Returns the
333	 * payload length, or 0 for an unknown mode. */
334	static int build_report(uint8_t mode, uint8_t *p)
335	{
336	    memset(p, 0, 21);
337	    if (mode != 0x3d) {
338	        p[0] = s_btn0;
339	        p[1] = s_btn1;
340	    }
341	    switch (mode) {
342	    case 0x30: return 2;
343	    case 0x31: set_accel_level(&p[2]); return 5;
344	    case 0x32: build_extension(&p[2]); return 10;
345	    case 0x33: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_ir_extended(&p[5]); return 17;
346	    case 0x34: build_extension(&p[2]); return 21;
347	    case 0x35: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_extension(&p[5]); return 21;
348	    case 0x36: build_ir_basic(&p[2]); build_extension(&p[12]); return 21;   /* btn + 10 IR + 9 ext */
349	    case 0x37: set_accel_level(&p[2]); build_ir_basic(&p[5]); build_extension(&p[15]); return 21;  /* + 10 IR + 6 ext */
350	    case 0x3d: build_extension(&p[0]); return 21;
351	    case 0x3e: case 0x3f: return 21;
352	    default:   return 0;
353	    }
354	}
355	
356	void Wiimote_RegisterExtension(const wiimote_extension_t *ext)
357	{
358	    s_ext = ext;
359	    s_ext_connected = (ext != NULL);
360	}

362	bool Wiimote_SetButton(const char *name, bool pressed)
363	{
364	    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_buttons) / sizeof(k_buttons[0]); i++) {
365	        if (strcmp(name, k_buttons[i].name) == 0) {
366	            uint8_t *b = (k_buttons[i].byte == 0) ? &s_btn0 : &s_btn1;
367	            if (pressed) *b |= k_buttons[i].mask; else *b &= (uint8_t)~k_buttons[i].mask;
368	            return true;
369	        }
370	    }
371	    if (s_ext && s_ext->set_button) {
372	        return s_ext->set_button(name, pressed);
373	    }
374	    return false;
375	}
376	
377	bool Wiimote_TapButton(const char *name)
378	{
379	    if (!Wiimote_SetButton(name, true)) {
380	        return false;
381	    }
382	    int slot = -1;
383	    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
384	        if (!s_taps[i].active) { slot = i; break; }
385	    }
386	    if (slot < 0) slot = 0;     /* all busy: reuse the first */
387	    strncpy(s_taps[slot].name, name, sizeof(s_taps[slot].name) - 1);
388	    s_taps[slot].name[sizeof(s_taps[slot].name) - 1] = '\0';
389	    s_taps[slot].release_at = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(TAP_MS);
390	    s_taps[slot].active = true;
391	    return true;
392	}
393	
394	void Wiimote_SetExtension(bool connected)
395	{
396	    s_ext_connected = connected;
397	}
398	
399	void Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected(void)
400	{
401	    s_data_fd = -1;          /* mark not-connected at once (don't wait for the reader to exit) */
402	    s_streaming = false;
403	    s_leds = 0;
404	    s_btn0 = s_btn1 = 0;
405	    s_crypt_on = s_crypt_armed = false;   /* host re-inits encryption on reconnect */
406	    for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
407	        s_taps[i].active = false;
408	    }
409	    if (s_ext && s_ext->reset) {
410	        s_ext->reset();
411	    }
412	}
413	
414	bool Wiimote_IsConnected(void)  { return s_data_fd >= 0; }
415	bool Wiimote_IsAssigned(void)   { return s_leds != 0; }
416	uint8_t Wiimote_ReportMode(void) { return s_report_mode; }
417	
418	int Wiimote_PlayerSlot(void)
419	{
420	    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
421	        if (s_leds & (1 << i)) return i + 1;
422	    }
423	    return 0;
424	}
425	
426	void Wiimote_SetPointer(float x, float y)
427	{
428	    if (x < 0.0f) x = 0.0f; else if (x > 1.0f) x = 1.0f;
429	    if (y < 0.0f) y = 0.0f; else if (y > 1.0f) y = 1.0f;
430	    s_point_x = x;
431	    s_point_y = y;
432	    s_point_active = true;
433	}
434	
435	void Wiimote_ClearPointer(void)
436	{
437	    s_point_active = false;
438	}
439	
440	static void sender_task(void *arg)
441	{
442	    (void)arg;
443	    uint8_t p[21];
444	    for (;;) {
445	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SENDER_PERIOD_MS));
446	
447	        /* Release any taps whose deadline has passed (tick-wrap safe). */
448	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
449	        for (int i = 0; i < TAP_SLOTS; i++) {
450	            if (s_taps[i].active && (int32_t)(now - s_taps[i].release_at) >= 0) {
451	                Wiimote_SetButton(s_taps[i].name, false);
452	                s_taps[i].active = false;
453	            }
454	        }
455	
456	        if (s_streaming && s_data_fd >= 0) {
457	            uint8_t mode = s_report_mode;
458	            int len = build_report(mode, p);
459	            if (len == 0) {                 /* unknown mode → fall back to core buttons */
460	                mode = 0x30;
461	                len = build_report(mode, p);
462	            }
463	            wm_send(s_data_fd, mode, p, len);
464	        }
465	    }
466	}
467	
468	void Wiimote_Start(void)
469	{
470	    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x16], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
471	    memcpy(&s_eeprom[0x20], k_accel_cal, sizeof(k_accel_cal));
472	    xTaskCreateStatic(sender_task, "wm_tx", SENDER_STACK, NULL, 6,
473	                      s_sender_stack, &s_sender_tcb);
474	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote report state machine started");
475	}
```

```text
6	/* A Wiimote extension controller (guitar, nunchuk, classic, …). The base Wiimote
7	 * owns the BT/HID link, the report sender, and the register/status plumbing; an
8	 * extension module registers itself and supplies its identity + data.
9	 *
10	 * An extension provides a 256-byte register bank (the host reads the ID at 0xfa and
11	 * may write init/encryption bytes), a function to fill its bytes in the data report,
12	 * an optional button-by-name setter (so the CLI/Marvin drive it through the same
13	 * Wiimote_SetButton API), and an optional reset hook for link drops. */
14	typedef struct {
15	    const char *name;
16	    uint8_t    *regs;        /* 256-byte register bank, owned by the extension (ID at 0xfa) */
17	    uint8_t     report_len;  /* bytes the extension contributes to the data report */
18	    void (*build_report)(uint8_t *dst);                  /* fill report_len bytes */
19	    bool (*set_button)(const char *name, bool pressed);  /* ext button by name; false if unknown */
20	    void (*reset)(void);                                 /* release inputs on link drop (may be NULL) */
21	} wiimote_extension_t;
22	
23	/* Attach an extension to the base Wiimote (one at a time). Pass NULL to detach. */
24	void Wiimote_RegisterExtension(const wiimote_extension_t *ext);
```

```text
6	/* Guitar Hero guitar extension. 6-byte report (buttons active-low, rest = 1):
7	 *   0: bits7-6 = 1 (GH3 Les Paul ident; 0 = GHWT), bits5-0 stick X
8	 *   1: bits7-6 = 1 (GH3 ident),                    bits5-0 stick Y
9	 *   2: touch bar (bits 4-0; GHWT only)  3: whammy (bits 4-0)
10	 *   4: bit6 strum-down, bit4 minus, bit2 plus (others 1)
11	 *   5: bit7 orange, bit6 red, bit5 blue, bit4 green, bit3 yellow, bit2 pedal,
12	 *      bit0 strum-up (bit1 = 1)
13	 * The GH3 ident bits matter: with them clear, GH3 treats us as a GHWT guitar and
14	 * ignores the strum bar. See firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md. */
15	
16	static uint8_t s_regs[256];                    /* register bank (ID at 0xfa) */
17	static uint8_t s_sx = 0x20, s_sy = 0x20;       /* analog stick, centered */
18	static uint8_t s_tb;                           /* touch bar (GH3 unused) */
19	static uint8_t s_whammy = 0x10;                /* whammy bar (rest) */
20	static uint8_t s_btn4 = 0xFF, s_btn5 = 0xFF;   /* button bytes, active-low (rest 0xFF) */
21	
22	static const struct { const char *name; uint8_t byte; uint8_t mask; } k_btn[] = {
23	    { "green",   5, 0x10 }, { "red",    5, 0x40 }, { "yellow", 5, 0x08 },
24	    { "blue",    5, 0x20 }, { "orange", 5, 0x80 }, { "pedal",  5, 0x04 },
25	    { "strumup", 5, 0x01 }, { "strumdown", 4, 0x40 },
26	    { "gplus",   4, 0x04 }, { "gminus", 4, 0x10 },
27	};
28	
29	static void guitar_build_report(uint8_t *d)
30	{
31	    d[0] = 0xC0 | (s_sx & 0x3F);   /* bits7-6 = 1: identify as a GH3 Les Paul guitar */
32	    d[1] = 0xC0 | (s_sy & 0x3F);
33	    d[2] = s_tb;
34	    d[3] = s_whammy;
35	    d[4] = s_btn4;
36	    d[5] = s_btn5;
37	}
38	
39	static bool guitar_set_button(const char *name, bool pressed)
40	{

42	        if (strcmp(name, k_btn[i].name) == 0) {
43	            uint8_t *b = (k_btn[i].byte == 4) ? &s_btn4 : &s_btn5;
44	            if (pressed) *b &= (uint8_t)~k_btn[i].mask;   /* active-low: pressed = clear */
45	            else *b |= k_btn[i].mask;
46	            return true;
47	        }
48	    }
49	    return false;
50	}
51

55	    s_whammy = 0x10;
```

```text
180	static const uint8_t k_ans[7][6] = {
181	    { 0xa8, 0x77, 0xa6, 0xe0, 0xf7, 0x43 },
182	    { 0x5a, 0x35, 0x85, 0xe2, 0x72, 0x97 },
183	    { 0x8f, 0xb7, 0x1a, 0x62, 0x87, 0x38 },

186	    { 0xa9, 0x26, 0x3f, 0x2b, 0x10, 0xe3 },

188	};

190	static inline uint8_t ror8(uint8_t v, uint8_t n)
191	{
192	    n &= 7;
193	    return (uint8_t)((v >> n) | (v << (8 - n)));
194	}
195	
196	void ExtCrypto_GenTables(ext_crypto_t *st, const uint8_t key[16])
197	{
198	    uint8_t t0[10];
199	    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
200	        t0[i] = k_keygen[key[9 - i]];
201	    }
202	
203	    /* idx is not transmitted; brute-force the one the host used (0..6). */
204	    int idx = 0;
205	    for (; idx < 7; idx++) {
206	        const uint8_t *a = k_ans[idx];
207	        if (key[0xf] == (uint8_t)((ror8(a[0] ^ t0[5], t0[2]) - t0[9]) ^ t0[4]) &&
208	            key[0xe] == (uint8_t)((ror8(a[1] ^ t0[1], t0[0]) - t0[5]) ^ t0[7]) &&
209	            key[0xd] == (uint8_t)((ror8(a[2] ^ t0[6], t0[8]) - t0[2]) ^ t0[0]) &&
210	            key[0xc] == (uint8_t)((ror8(a[3] ^ t0[4], t0[7]) - t0[3]) ^ t0[2]) &&
211	            key[0xb] == (uint8_t)((ror8(a[4] ^ t0[1], t0[6]) - t0[3]) ^ t0[4]) &&
212	            key[0xa] == (uint8_t)((ror8(a[5] ^ t0[7], t0[8]) - t0[5]) ^ t0[9])) {
213	            break;
214	        }
215	    }
216	    if (idx > 6) idx = 6;   /* no match (e.g. all-zero homebrew key); fall back */
217	
218	    const uint8_t *sa = k_sbox[idx];
219	    const uint8_t *sc = k_sbox[idx + 1];
220	
221	    st->ft[0] = sa[key[0xb]] ^ sc[key[0x6]];
222	    st->ft[1] = sa[key[0xd]] ^ sc[key[0x4]];
223	    st->ft[2] = sa[key[0xa]] ^ sc[key[0x2]];
224	    st->ft[3] = sa[key[0xf]] ^ sc[key[0x7]];
225	    st->ft[4] = sa[key[0xe]] ^ sc[key[0x5]];
226	    st->ft[5] = sa[key[0xc]] ^ sc[key[0x0]];
227	    st->ft[6] = sa[key[0x9]] ^ sc[key[0x3]];
228	    st->ft[7] = sa[key[0x8]] ^ sc[key[0x1]];
229	
230	    st->sb[0] = sa[key[0xf]] ^ sc[key[0x8]];
231	    st->sb[1] = sa[key[0xa]] ^ sc[key[0x5]];
232	    st->sb[2] = sa[key[0xc]] ^ sc[key[0x9]];
233	    st->sb[3] = sa[key[0xd]] ^ sc[key[0x0]];
234	    st->sb[4] = sa[key[0xb]] ^ sc[key[0x2]];
235	    st->sb[5] = sa[key[0xe]] ^ sc[key[0x1]];
236	    st->sb[6] = sa[key[0x6]] ^ sc[key[0x4]];
237	    st->sb[7] = sa[key[0x7]] ^ sc[key[0x3]];
238	}
239	
240	void ExtCrypto_Encrypt(const ext_crypto_t *st, uint8_t *buf, int addr, int len)
241	{
242	    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
243	        int k = (i + addr) & 7;
244	        buf[i] = (uint8_t)((buf[i] - st->ft[k]) ^ st->sb[k]);
245	    }
246	}
```

```text
140	static void register_cmd(const char *name, const char *help, esp_console_cmd_func_t fn)
141	{
142	    const esp_console_cmd_t cmd = { .command = name, .help = help, .hint = NULL, .func = fn };

144	}

146	void Cli_Start(void)
147	{
148	    esp_console_repl_t *repl = NULL;
149	    esp_console_repl_config_t repl_config = ESP_CONSOLE_REPL_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
150	    repl_config.prompt = "fauxmote>";
151	    esp_console_dev_uart_config_t uart_config = ESP_CONSOLE_DEV_UART_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
152	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_console_new_repl_uart(&uart_config, &repl_config, &repl));
153	
154	    register_cmd("pair", "enter pairing/sync mode (then press the Wii SYNC button)", cmd_pair);
155	    register_cmd("stop", "leave pairing mode (idle)", cmd_stop);
156	    register_cmd("reconnect", "device-initiated reconnect to the last bonded Wii", cmd_reconnect);
157	    register_cmd("unlink", "erase the bond (link key) from NVS", cmd_unlink);
158	    register_cmd("status", "show BT / connection state", cmd_status);
159	    register_cmd("btn", "btn <name> <0|1> — hold/release a button (core or guitar)", cmd_btn);
160	    register_cmd("tap", "tap <name> — brief press+release (e.g. tap strumdown)", cmd_tap);
161	    register_cmd("point", "point <x 0..1> <y 0..1> | point off — IR cursor", cmd_point);
162	    register_cmd("whammy", "whammy <0..31> — guitar whammy bar", cmd_whammy);
163	    register_cmd("ext", "ext <on|off> — attach/detach the guitar extension", cmd_ext);
164	    esp_console_register_help_command();
165	
166	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_console_start_repl(repl));
167	}
```

```text
41	    uint32_t h = SDP_CreateRecord();
42	    if (h == 0) {
43	        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "SDP_CreateRecord failed");
44	        return false;
45	    }
46	
47	    bool ok = true;
48	    uint16_t u16;
49	    uint8_t *p;
50	    const uint8_t bool_true = 1, bool_false = 0;
51	
52	    /* Service Class ID List: HID */
53	    uint16_t hid_uuid = UUID_SERVCLASS_HUMAN_INTERFACE;
54	    ok &= SDP_AddServiceClassIdList(h, 1, &hid_uuid);
55	
56	    /* Protocol Descriptor List: L2CAP (PSM 0x11 = HID control) + HIDP */
57	    tSDP_PROTOCOL_ELEM proto[2];
58	    proto[0].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_L2CAP; proto[0].num_params = 1; proto[0].params[0] = BT_PSM_HIDC;
59	    proto[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;  proto[1].num_params = 0;
60	    ok &= SDP_AddProtocolList(h, 2, proto);
61	
62	    /* Language Base Attribute ID List */
63	    ok &= SDP_AddLanguageBaseAttrIDList(h, LANG_ID_CODE_ENGLISH, LANG_ID_CHAR_ENCODE_UTF8, LANGUAGE_BASE_ID);
64	
65	    /* Additional Protocol Descriptor List: L2CAP (PSM 0x13 = HID interrupt) + HIDP */
66	    tSDP_PROTO_LIST_ELEM add_proto;
67	    add_proto.num_elems = 2;
68	    add_proto.list_elem[0].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_L2CAP; add_proto.list_elem[0].num_params = 1; add_proto.list_elem[0].params[0] = BT_PSM_HIDI;
69	    add_proto.list_elem[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;  add_proto.list_elem[1].num_params = 0;
70	    ok &= SDP_AddAdditionProtoLists(h, 1, &add_proto);
71	
72	    /* Names */
73	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_SERVICE_NAME, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, sizeof(k_name), (uint8_t *)k_name);
74	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_SERVICE_DESCRIPTION, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, sizeof(k_name), (uint8_t *)k_name);
75	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_PROVIDER_NAME, TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE, sizeof(k_provider), (uint8_t *)k_provider);
76	
77	    /* Bluetooth Profile Descriptor List: HID v1.00 */
78	    ok &= SDP_AddProfileDescriptorList(h, UUID_SERVCLASS_HUMAN_INTERFACE, 0x0100);
79	
80	    /* HID attribute values — Wiimote-exact (cf. docs/wiimote-sdp.md). */
81	    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0100);
82	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_DEVICE_RELNUM, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
83	    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0111);
84	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_PARSER_VERSION, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
85	    const uint8_t subclass = 0x04;
86	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_DEVICE_SUBCLASS, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&subclass);
87	    const uint8_t country = 0x33;
88	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_COUNTRY_CODE, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&country);
89	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_VIRTUAL_CABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
90	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_RECONNECT_INITIATE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
91	
92	    /* HID Descriptor List: sequence{ uint8 descriptor-type 0x22, text-string descriptor }. */
93	    static uint8_t desc_attr[8 + sizeof(s_hid_descriptor)];
94	    p = desc_attr;
95	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
96	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (uint8_t)(4 + sizeof(s_hid_descriptor)));
97	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_ONE_BYTE);
98	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x22);
99	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (TEXT_STR_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
100	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (uint8_t)sizeof(s_hid_descriptor));
101	    ARRAY_TO_BE_STREAM(p, s_hid_descriptor, (int)sizeof(s_hid_descriptor));
102	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_DESCRIPTOR_LIST, DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE, (uint32_t)(p - desc_attr), desc_attr);
103	
104	    /* HID Language ID Base List: English / base 0x0100. */
105	    uint8_t lang[8];
106	    p = lang;
107	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_IN_NEXT_BYTE);
108	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 6);
109	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_TWO_BYTES);
110	    UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0409);
111	    UINT8_TO_BE_STREAM(p, (UINT_DESC_TYPE << 3) | SIZE_TWO_BYTES);
112	    UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, LANGUAGE_BASE_ID);
113	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_LANGUAGE_ID_BASE, DATA_ELE_SEQ_DESC_TYPE, (uint32_t)(p - lang), lang);
114	
115	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_SDP_DISABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
116	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_BATTERY_POWER, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
117	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_REMOTE_WAKE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_true);
118	    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0100);
119	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_PROFILE_VERSION, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
120	    p = (uint8_t *)&u16; UINT16_TO_BE_STREAM(p, 0x0C80);
121	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_SUPERVISION_TIMEOUT, UINT_DESC_TYPE, 2, (uint8_t *)&u16);
122	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_NORMALLY_CONNECTABLE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
123	    ok &= SDP_AddAttribute(h, ATTR_ID_HID_BOOT_DEVICE, BOOLEAN_DESC_TYPE, 1, (uint8_t *)&bool_false);
124	
125	    /* Browse group */
126	    uint16_t browse = UUID_SERVCLASS_PUBLIC_BROWSE_GROUP;
127	    ok &= SDP_AddUuidSequence(h, ATTR_ID_BROWSE_GROUP_LIST, 1, &browse);
128	
129	    if (!ok) {
130	        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "failed building Wiimote SDP record");
131	        return false;
132	    }
133	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wiimote SDP record registered (handle 0x%08x)", (unsigned)h);
134	    return true;
135	}
```

```text
42	/* Advertise as a Wiimote: Class of Device 0x002504 (peripheral/joystick, with the
43	 * limited-discoverable service bit) + limited-discoverable scan mode. The Wii's
44	 * SYNC scan uses a limited inquiry (LIAC), so general discovery isn't enough. */
45	static void set_wiimote_discoverable(void)
46	{
47	    esp_bt_cod_t cod = {0};
48	    cod.minor = 0x01;
49	    cod.major = ESP_BT_COD_MAJOR_DEV_PERIPHERAL;
50	    cod.service = 0x01;

55	static void gap_cb(esp_bt_gap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_gap_cb_param_t *param)
56	{
57	    switch (event) {
58	    case ESP_BT_GAP_PIN_REQ_EVT: {
59	        /* Console-SYNC (bonding) pairing: PIN = the host's BD_ADDR, reversed. */
60	        esp_bt_pin_code_t pin;
61	        for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
62	            pin[i] = param->pin_req.bda[5 - i];
63	        }
64	        log_bda("PIN request from", param->pin_req.bda);
65	        esp_bt_gap_pin_reply(param->pin_req.bda, true, 6, pin);
66	        break;
67	    }
68	    case ESP_BT_GAP_AUTH_CMPL_EVT:
69	        if (param->auth_cmpl.stat == ESP_BT_STATUS_SUCCESS) {
70	            memcpy(s_wii_bda, param->auth_cmpl.bda, sizeof(s_wii_bda));
71	            s_have_wii = true;
72	            log_bda("auth OK with", param->auth_cmpl.bda);
73	        } else {
74	            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "auth FAILED, status=%d", param->auth_cmpl.stat);
75	        }
76	        break;
77	    default:
78	        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "gap event %d", event);
79	        break;
80	    }

83	#define HID_LINK_MAX  4
84	#define HID_RX_LEN    64
85	#define HID_RX_STACK  3072
86	
87	typedef struct {
88	    bool          in_use;
89	    volatile bool stop;     /* set by the CLOSE handler to make this reader exit */
90	    int           fd;
91	    uint32_t      handle;   /* L2CAP connection handle, matched against CLOSE events */
92	    StaticTask_t  tcb;
93	    StackType_t   stack[HID_RX_STACK];
94	    uint8_t       rx[HID_RX_LEN];
95	} hid_link_t;
96	
97	static hid_link_t s_links[HID_LINK_MAX];
98	
99	/* Read HIDP frames from one HID channel and dispatch them to the Wiimote module.
100	 * Exits when its CLOSE handler sets `stop` — not by watching read() return codes,
101	 * since re-armed servers can recycle this fd number out from under us. */
102	static void hid_reader_task(void *arg)
103	{
104	    hid_link_t *l = (hid_link_t *)arg;
105	    while (!l->stop) {
106	        int n = read(l->fd, l->rx, sizeof(l->rx));
107	        if (l->stop) break;
108	        if (n > 0) {
109	            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "fd %d RX report 0x%02x (%d B)", l->fd,
110	                     n > 1 ? l->rx[1] : 0, n);
111	            Wiimote_HandleRx(l->fd, l->rx, n);
112	        } else if (n < 0) {
113	            break;                          /* genuine close of our fd */
114	        } else {
115	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));  /* non-blocking VFS: 0 = no data yet */
116	        }
117	    }
118	    l->in_use = false;
119	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
120	}
121	
122	static void hid_link_start(int fd, uint32_t handle)
123	{
124	    for (int i = 0; i < HID_LINK_MAX; i++) {
125	        if (!s_links[i].in_use) {
126	            s_links[i].in_use = true;
127	            s_links[i].stop = false;
128	            s_links[i].fd = fd;
129	            s_links[i].handle = handle;
130	            xTaskCreateStatic(hid_reader_task, "hid_rx", HID_RX_STACK,
131	                              &s_links[i], 5, s_links[i].stack, &s_links[i].tcb);
132	            return;
133	        }
134	    }
135	    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "no free HID link slot for fd %d", fd);
136	}
137	
138	static void hid_link_stop(uint32_t handle)
139	{
140	    for (int i = 0; i < HID_LINK_MAX; i++) {
141	        if (s_links[i].in_use && s_links[i].handle == handle) {
142	            s_links[i].stop = true;
143	            return;
144	        }
145	    }
146	}

148	/* Bluedroid consumes the listening server slot when a connection opens, so the
149	 * HID PSMs are armed per pairing window (EnterPairing) and torn down in StopPairing
150	 * — re-arming on every disconnect leaks slots when reconnect uses client connects. */
151	static void start_hid_servers(void)
152	{
153	    esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_CONTROL);
154	    esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT);
155	}
156	
157	static void l2cap_cb(esp_bt_l2cap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_l2cap_cb_param_t *param)
158	{
159	    switch (event) {
160	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_INIT_EVT:
161	        /* The L2CAP data path is fd-based; the VFS must be registered before a
162	         * server can allocate a slot/fd. */
163	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP init status=%d; registering VFS", param->init.status);
164	        esp_bt_l2cap_vfs_register();
165	        break;
166	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_VFS_REGISTER_EVT:
167	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP VFS registered status=%d", param->vfs_register.status);
168	        break;
169	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_START_EVT:
170	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP server up status=%d handle=%u",
171	                 param->start.status, (unsigned)param->start.handle);
172	        break;
173	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT:
174	        log_bda("L2CAP OPEN from", param->open.rem_bda);
175	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "  status=%d handle=%u fd=%d mtu=%d",
176	                 param->open.status, (unsigned)param->open.handle,
177	                 param->open.fd, (int)param->open.tx_mtu);
178	        hid_link_start(param->open.fd, param->open.handle);
179	        /* Connected — stop being discoverable (stay connectable for reconnects),
180	         * matching a real Wiimote which doesn't advertise once connected. */
181	        esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
182	        s_discoverable = false;
183	        if (s_reconnecting) {
184	            /* control channel re-opened — now open the interrupt channel. */
185	            s_reconnecting = false;
186	            esp_bt_l2cap_connect(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT, s_wii_bda);
187	        }
188	        break;
189	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_CLOSE_EVT:
190	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "L2CAP CLOSE handle=%u async=%d",
191	                 (unsigned)param->close.handle, param->close.async);
192	        /* Signal this channel's reader to exit (by handle, robust to fd reuse). */
193	        hid_link_stop(param->close.handle);
194	        /* Stop streaming + reset controller state immediately so the sender
195	         * doesn't write into the dying channel and the LED returns to idle. */
196	        Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected();
197	        /* Arm auto-reconnect unless this was a user-requested stop/unlink. */
198	        if (s_have_wii && !s_suppress_reconnect) {
199	            s_want_reconnect = true;
200	        }
201	        s_suppress_reconnect = false;
202	        break;
203	    default:
204	        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "l2cap event %d", event);
205	        break;
206	    }
207	}
208	
209	/* Heal an unexpected link drop (e.g. the Wii's brief disconnect when a game boots)
210	 * by re-initiating the connection, like a real Wiimote. Bounded retries; cleared
211	 * once the Wii is talking to us again, or on a user stop/unlink. */
212	static void reconnect_task(void *arg)
213	{
214	    (void)arg;
215	    for (;;) {
216	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1000));
217	        if (Wiimote_IsConnected()) {
218	            s_want_reconnect = false;
219	            s_reconnect_tries = 0;
220	            continue;
221	        }
222	        if (!s_want_reconnect || !s_have_wii) {
223	            continue;
224	        }
225	        /* Keep trying like a real Wiimote — a game disc can take a while to boot and
226	         * re-accept the controller. Back off after a few quick tries so we don't
227	         * hammer the link while the Wii is still reinitializing. */
228	        s_reconnect_tries++;
229	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "auto-reconnect attempt %d", s_reconnect_tries);
230	        Fauxmote_Reconnect();
231	        int wait_ms = (s_reconnect_tries < AUTO_RECONNECT_MAX) ? 3000 : 8000;
232	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(wait_ms));
233	    }
234	}

236	void Fauxmote_BtStart(void)
237	{
238	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_mem_release(ESP_BT_MODE_BLE));
239	    esp_bt_controller_config_t cfg = BT_CONTROLLER_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
240	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_init(&cfg));
241	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_enable(ESP_BT_MODE_CLASSIC_BT));
242	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_init());
243	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_enable());
244	
245	    const uint8_t *bda = esp_bt_dev_get_address();
246	    if (bda) {
247	        /* Our BD_ADDR — also the 1+2 temporary-pairing PIN (this, reversed). */
248	        log_bda("BD_ADDR", bda);
249	    }
250	
251	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_register_callback(gap_cb));
252	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_set_device_name(FAUXMOTE_BT_NAME));
253	
254	    /* Legacy PIN pairing (SSP disabled in sdkconfig): we answer each PIN request. */
255	    esp_bt_gap_set_pin(ESP_BT_PIN_TYPE_VARIABLE, 0, NULL);
256	
257	    /* Serve the exact Wiimote SDP record, then listen for the Wii's HID L2CAP
258	     * connections on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). */
259	    if (!WiimoteSdp_Register()) {
260	        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Wiimote SDP registration failed");
261	    }
262	    Wiimote_Start();
263	
264	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_register_callback(l2cap_cb));
265	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_init());
266	
267	    xTaskCreateStatic(reconnect_task, "reconnect", AUTO_RECONNECT_STACK, NULL, 4,
268	                      s_recon_stack, &s_recon_tcb);
269	
270	    /* The stack persists the bond (link key) in NVS and reloads it at boot — recall
271	     * the bonded Wii's address so `reconnect` works after a power cycle. */
272	    int bonded = esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_num();
273	    if (bonded > 0) {
274	        esp_bd_addr_t devs[8];
275	        int n = bonded > 8 ? 8 : bonded;
276	        if (esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list(&n, devs) == ESP_OK && n > 0) {
277	            memcpy(s_wii_bda, devs[0], sizeof(s_wii_bda));
278	            s_have_wii = true;
279	            log_bda("recalled bonded Wii", s_wii_bda);
280	        }
281	    }
282	
283	    /* Stay idle (not discoverable/connectable) until the operator runs `pair`. */
284	    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_NON_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
285	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "fauxmote up (idle). Use the `pair` console command to sync with a Wii.");
286	}
287	
288	void Fauxmote_EnterPairing(void)
289	{
290	    if (s_discoverable || Wiimote_IsConnected()) {
291	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "pairing: already discoverable/connected");
292	        return;
293	    }
294	    start_hid_servers();          /* arm the HID listeners for this sync window */
295	    set_wiimote_discoverable();
296	    s_discoverable = true;
297	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "pairing mode ON — limited-discoverable as a Wiimote (sync the Wii now)");
298	}
299	
300	void Fauxmote_StopPairing(void)
301	{
302	    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_NON_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
303	    esp_bt_l2cap_stop_all_srv();  /* tear down any armed (unconsumed) HID listeners */
304	    s_discoverable = false;
305	    s_want_reconnect = false;     /* deliberate idle — don't auto-reconnect */
306	    s_suppress_reconnect = true;
307	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "pairing mode OFF (idle)");
308	}
309	
310	void Fauxmote_Reconnect(void)
311	{
312	    if (!s_have_wii) {
313	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "reconnect: no bonded Wii yet — run `pair` first");
314	        return;
315	    }
316	    log_bda("reconnect: connecting to", s_wii_bda);
317	    s_reconnecting = true;
318	    esp_bt_l2cap_connect(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_CONTROL, s_wii_bda);
319	}
320	
321	void Fauxmote_Unlink(void)
322	{
323	    if (!s_have_wii) {
324	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "unlink: no bonded Wii");
325	        return;
326	    }
327	    log_bda("unlink: removing bond", s_wii_bda);
328	    esp_bt_gap_remove_bond_device(s_wii_bda);   /* erases the link key from NVS */
329	    s_have_wii = false;
330	    s_want_reconnect = false;
331	    s_suppress_reconnect = true;
332	    memset(s_wii_bda, 0, sizeof(s_wii_bda));
333	}
334	
335	bool Fauxmote_IsDiscoverable(void) { return s_discoverable; }
336	
337	const uint8_t *Fauxmote_WiiAddr(void) { return s_have_wii ? s_wii_bda : NULL; }
338
```

```text
23	/* Patterns (re-evaluated each cycle):
24	 *  - assigned   : N short flashes = player slot 1..4, then a pause, repeat
25	 *  - pairing/connecting : fast continuous blink
26	 *  - idle       : a brief blip ~1 Hz */
27	static void led_task(void *arg)
28	{
29	    (void)arg;
30	    gpio_reset_pin(LED_GPIO);
31	    gpio_set_direction(LED_GPIO, GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT);
32	
33	    for (;;) {
34	        int slot = Wiimote_PlayerSlot();
35	        if (Wiimote_IsConnected() && slot > 0) {
36	            for (int i = 0; i < slot; i++) {
37	                blink(180, 180);
38	            }
39	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(800));     /* gap before repeating the count */
40	        } else if (Fauxmote_IsDiscoverable() || Wiimote_IsConnected()) {
41	            blink(100, 100);                    /* fast blink = pairing/connecting */
42	        } else {
43	            blink(30, 2970);                    /* brief blip every ~3 s = idle */
44	        }
45	    }
46	}
47	
48	void StatusLed_Start(void)
49	{
50	    xTaskCreateStatic(led_task, "status_led", LED_STACK, NULL, 3, s_stack, &s_tcb);
51	}
```

# Fauxmote Documentation Audit — Findings

## firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md

**HIGH — §3 guitar extension init is contradicted by the code (encryption + init sequence).**
- Location: SPEC.md:39-42
- Problem: SPEC says guitar init is `write 0x55→0xf0, 0x00→0xfb (disables encryption)` — but the implemented/working path (per Phase 3) is that GH3 *requires* encryption: host writes `0x55→0xf0`, reads ID at `0xfa`, then `0xAA→0xf0` + 16-byte key to `0x40-0x4f` (wiimote.c:171-184; ext_crypto.c). There is no `0xfb` write handling in the code at all, and "disables encryption" is the opposite of what GH3 does.
- Fix: Rewrite §3's guitar init line to describe the real encrypted handshake (0x55→0xf0, read ID, 0xAA→0xf0 + key to 0x40), and drop the `0x00→0xfb` / "disables encryption" claim.

**MED — §3 report-mode example is the wrong/stale mode.**
- Location: SPEC.md:42 ("carried inside a Wiimote data report that includes extension bytes (e.g. report `0x34`)")
- Problem: GH3 actually streams mode `0x37` (journal:66, wiimote.c:349). `0x34` is technically still ext-bearing, but using it as *the* example contradicts the verified GH3 mode and the rest of the docs.
- Fix: Change the example to `0x37` (or note GH3 uses `0x37`).

**MED — §3 register address notation `0x(4)a400fa` is confusing/imprecise.**
- Location: SPEC.md:39
- Problem: Code reads the extension ID at register offset `0xfa` within the `0xA4xxxx` space (guitar.c:75-76, wiimote.c:138). The `0x(4)a400fa` shorthand doesn't map cleanly to the code's `0xa400fa` masked by `& 0xFE == 0xA4`.
- Fix: State it as register `0xa400fa` (ID bytes at offset `0xfa` of the `0xA4` extension space).

**MED — §6 Phase 3 / §5 don't mention encryption or the `ext_crypto` module at all.**
- Location: SPEC.md §5 (Software, 57-70) and §6 (Milestones, 79)
- Problem: Extension encryption is now a core, load-bearing feature (`ext_crypto.c/.h`, wired into wiimote.c) and a significant architectural addition (the `wiimote_ext.h` extension interface + `guitar.c` split). Neither the Software section nor the milestone table mentions encryption or the extension-module architecture.
- Fix: Add a sentence to §5 noting the `wiimote_ext.h`/`guitar.c` extension interface and the `ext_crypto.c` Wii extension cipher; optionally mark Phase 3 done.

```text
1	# fauxmote — Specification
2	
3	> What fauxmote *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, success criteria, milestones).
4	> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose
7	
8	fauxmote is an **ESP32 firmware that emulates a Nintendo Wiimote with an attached
9	Guitar Hero guitar extension**, speaking Bluetooth straight to a real Wii console.
10	It is a **parallel proof-of-concept** alternative to the existing actuation path:
11	today the [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) MCU physically presses buttons on a
12	*real* Wii guitar controller via open-drain GPIO. fauxmote instead *becomes* the
13	controller — eventually driven by [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md)'s high-level
14	fret/strum commands, removing the physical actuator + real controller from the loop.
15	
16	The fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative until fauxmote is proven; nothing
17	in marvin/fretboard/edge-ai changes as part of this subproject.
18	
19	## 2. Hardware
20	
21	| Component | Detail |
22	|---|---|
23	| Board | **Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2** (product 5400) — *original* dual-core ESP32 (Tensilica LX6), 8 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM, USB-C. |
24	| Radio | ESP32 has a **Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR)** radio — required, because the Wiimote link is Classic HID. (ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and would *not* work.) |
25	| Wii console | Real retail Wii; pairing via the sync button or the controller's 1+2 button. |
26	
27	## 3. The link fauxmote emulates (verified protocol facts)
28	
29	- **Transport:** Bluetooth Classic **HID** over L2CAP — PSM `0x11` (control),
30	  PSM `0x13` (data). Input reports (device→host) prefixed `0xa1`; output reports
31	  (host→device) prefixed `0xa2`.
32	- **Identity the Wii expects (SDP):** device name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`,
33	  VID `0x057e`, PID `0x0306`, matching Class-of-Device, and the Wiimote HID report
34	  descriptor.
35	- **Pairing PIN (legacy):** the PIN is a BD_ADDR in **reverse byte order** (raw 6
36	  bytes). The 1+2 temporary-pair flow uses the *Wiimote's own* address — which
37	  fauxmote knows — so fauxmote can answer the GAP PIN request itself.
38	- **Guitar extension:** identity bytes `00 00 A4 20 01 03` at register
39	  `0x(4)a400fa`; init = write `0x55`→`0xf0`, `0x00`→`0xfb` (disables encryption).
40	  6-byte report layout (frets G/R/Y/B/O, strum up/down, whammy in byte 3 bits 3-0,
41	  touch bar, analog stick, +/− buttons), carried inside a Wiimote data report that
42	  includes extension bytes (e.g. report `0x34`).
43	
44	References: wiibrew [`Wiimote`](https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote) and
45	[`Guitar Hero (Wii) Guitars`](https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote/Extension_Controllers/Guitar_Hero_(Wii)_Guitars).
46	
47	## 4. Interfaces
48	
49	- **Downstream (fauxmote → Wii):** Bluetooth Classic HID, as above.
50	- **Upstream (commands → fauxmote):** **deferred.** Early phases use a local test
51	  command source (serial console + canned chord/strum patterns). The eventual marvin
52	  link is undecided; the likely candidate is mirroring the fretboard 1-byte fret/strum
53	  bitmask over UART (see [fretboard SPEC](../fretboard/SPEC.md) button-output section).
54	- **Debug:** USB-C CDC serial for flashing + logs (`idf.py monitor`).
55	
56	## 5. Software
57	
58	- **Framework:** ESP-IDF (v6.x; developed against v6.0.1), Bluedroid stack in **Bluetooth-Classic-only** mode
59	  (BLE disabled).
60	- **BT architecture (settled in Phase 1):** `esp_hidd` is *not* usable — the Wii
61	  rejects its SDP record and its hardcoded HID attributes/descriptor limits don't
62	  fit a Wiimote. Instead fauxmote serves a **byte-exact Wiimote SDP record** built
63	  via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` database API (`wiimote_sdp.c`; needs
64	  `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN`/`ATTR_LEN` raised) and handles HID over **raw L2CAP**
65	  (`esp_bt_l2cap`) on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). Legacy PIN pairing
66	  (SSP off; PIN = host BD_ADDR reversed). Detail + the record bytes in
67	  [`docs/wiimote-sdp.md`](docs/wiimote-sdp.md) and the journal.
68	- **Allocation:** application code follows the project's **static-allocation**
69	  preference (no `malloc` in our code). Bluedroid's internal allocation is
70	  framework-owned and out of scope.
71	
72	## 6. Milestones / success criteria
73	
74	| Phase | Goal | Done when |
75	|---|---|---|
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 20:45:04Z)**_

Good question, and the two symptoms have different answers:

**The per-keystroke "cursor flashes to the start of the line" is normal — not a bug.** That's `linenoise` (the line editor inside `esp_console`) doing a full-line redraw on every keypress: it emits `\r`, reprints the prompt + your current buffer, then repositions the cursor. You're seeing it because linenoise detected an ANSI terminal and is in full-edit mode. Expected behavior.

**The phantom line-commit is the real issue, and it's most likely the terminal layer (`idf.py monitor`), not our firmware.** Reasoning:
- We removed the concurrent log writes, so nothing in the firmware is writing to the UART between your keystrokes anymore — the thing that was *definitely* corrupting the line is gone.
- A spurious `\n` on the **input** stream can't come from our output; it comes from the terminal/transport. `idf.py monitor` is a Python wrapper that re-processes interactive input and is widely flaky for REPLs — dropped/duplicated bytes there show up exactly as "it pressed enter for me" and desynced redraws.

**Decisive test — drop `idf.py monitor`, use a raw serial terminal:**
```sh
ls /dev/cu.*                       # find the Feather (likely /dev/cu.usbserial-… or SLAB_USBtoUART)
screen /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX 115200    # exit with Ctrl-A then K
```
(or `tio /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX` if you have it). If the flakiness disappears on a raw terminal, it's the monitor — done.

**If it *still* misbehaves on a raw terminal, it's firmware**, and there are two cheap fixes I can make in `console_cli.c`:
1. Force linenoise **dumb mode** (`linenoiseSetDumbMode(1)`) — disables the fancy per-key redraw and escape-sequence parsing, which is more robust over a lossy link (you lose arrow-key editing/history, fine for a test CLI).
2. Bump the REPL task stack/priority and the UART RX buffer, in case the 15 ms sender + BT stack are starving the console task and overflowing the RX FIFO.

Try the raw terminal first — that tells us which side to fix without guessing. Want me to make the dumb-mode change preemptively, or wait on the terminal result?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 20:49:41Z)**_

That it happens on a raw terminal too tells us it's **firmware-side** (the console line editor), not the monitor — good, that isolates it. And the two symptoms are actually the *same* cause.

Here's what's going on: ESP-IDF's `linenoise` has no `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` to get the terminal width, so on **every refresh (every keystroke)** it falls back to *measuring* the width by writing a `\x1b[6n` cursor-position query, parking the cursor at the far right/start, and **reading the terminal's reply back from stdin**. That cursor dance is the "flash to the beginning of the line" you see. And the bug: that read-back of the position report **races with the bytes you're typing** — occasionally your input and the terminal's reply interleave, linenoise misparses it, and a stray CR slips through → the line commits mid-typing.

So it's the ANSI editing machinery fighting your keystrokes. The clean fix is to put linenoise in **dumb mode** — no per-key refresh, no width probe, no escape parsing; it just accumulates characters until a real newline. You lose arrow-key history editing (irrelevant for this test CLI, and Marvin will drive the API directly anyway), and the phantom commits go away:

```text
=== getCursorPosition (269-) + getColumns (326-) ===
/* Use the ESC [6n escape sequence to query the horizontal cursor position
 * and return it. On error -1 is returned, on success the position of the
 * cursor. */
static int getCursorPosition(void) {
    char buf[LINENOISE_COMMAND_MAX_LEN] = { 0 };
    int cols = 0;
    int rows = 0;
    int i = 0;
    const int out_fd = fileno(stdout);
    const int in_fd = fileno(stdin);
    /* The following ANSI escape sequence is used to get from the TTY the
     * cursor position. */
    const char get_cursor_cmd[] = "\x1b[6n";

    /* Send the command to the TTY on the other end of the UART.
     * Let's use unistd's write function. Thus, data sent through it are raw
     * reducing the overhead compared to using fputs, fprintf, etc... */
    int num_written = write(out_fd, get_cursor_cmd, sizeof(get_cursor_cmd));
    if (num_written != sizeof(get_cursor_cmd)) {
        return -1;
    }

    /* For USB CDC, it is required to flush the output. */
    flushWrite();

    /* The other end will send its response which format is ESC [ rows ; cols R
     * We don't know exactly how many bytes we have to read, thus, perform a
     * read for each byte.
     * Stop right before the last character of the buffer, to be able to NULL
     * terminate it. */
    while (i < sizeof(buf)-1) {
        /* Keep using unistd's functions. Here, using `read` instead of `fgets`
         * or `fgets` guarantees us that we we can read a byte regardless on
         * whether the sender sent end of line character(s) (CR, CRLF, LF). */
        if (read_func(in_fd, buf + i, 1) != 1 || buf[i] == 'R') {
            /* If we couldn't read a byte from STDIN or if 'R' was received,
             * the transmission is finished. */
            break;
        }

        /* For some reasons, it is possible that we receive new line character
         * after querying the cursor position on some UART. Let's ignore them,
         * this will not affect the rest of the program. */
        if (buf[i] != '\n') {
            i++;
        }
    }

    /* NULL-terminate the buffer, this is required by `sscanf`. */
    buf[i] = '\0';

    /* Parse the received data to get the position of the cursor. */
    if (buf[0] != ESC || buf[1] != '[' || sscanf(buf+2,"%d;%d",&rows,&cols) != 2) {
        return -1;
    }
    return cols;
}

/* Try to get the number of columns in the current terminal, or assume 80
 * if it fails. */
static int getColumns(void) {
    int start = 0;
    int cols = 0;
    int written = 0;
    char seq[LINENOISE_COMMAND_MAX_LEN] = { 0 };
    const int fd = fileno(stdout);

    /* The following ANSI escape sequence is used to tell the TTY to move
     * the cursor to the most-right position. */
    const char move_cursor_right[] = "\x1b[999C";
    const size_t cmd_len = sizeof(move_cursor_right);

    /* This one is used to set the cursor position. */
    const char set_cursor_pos[] = "\x1b[%dD";

    /* Get the initial position so we can restore it later. */
    start = getCursorPosition();
    if (start == -1) {
        goto failed;
    }

    /* Send the command to go to right margin. Use `write` function instead of
     * `fwrite` for the same reasons explained in `getCursorPosition()` */
    if (write(fd, move_cursor_right, cmd_len) != cmd_len) {
        goto failed;
    }
    flushWrite();

    /* After sending this command, we can get the new position of the cursor,
     * we'd get the size, in columns, of the opened TTY. */
    cols = getCursorPosition();
    if (cols == -1) {
        goto failed;
    }

    /* Restore the position of the cursor back. */
    if (cols > start) {
        /* Generate the move cursor command. */
        written = snprintf(seq, LINENOISE_COMMAND_MAX_LEN, set_cursor_pos, cols-start);
```

```text
=== linenoiseEdit head + ENTER/ESC handling ===
/* This function is the core of the line editing capability of linenoise.
 * It expects 'fd' to be already in "raw mode" so that every key pressed
 * will be returned ASAP to read().
 *
 * The resulting string is put into 'buf' when the user type enter, or
 * when ctrl+d is typed.
 *
 * The function returns the length of the current buffer. */
static int linenoiseEdit(char *buf, size_t buflen, const char *prompt)
{
    uint32_t t1 = 0;
    struct linenoiseState l;
    int out_fd = fileno(stdout);
    int in_fd = fileno(stdin);

    /* Populate the linenoise state that we pass to functions implementing
     * specific editing functionalities. */
    l.buf = buf;
    l.buflen = buflen;
    l.prompt = prompt;
    l.plen = strlen(prompt);
    l.oldpos = l.pos = 0;
    l.len = 0;
    l.cols = getColumns();
    l.maxrows = 0;
    l.history_index = 0;

    /* Buffer starts empty. */
    l.buf[0] = '\0';
    l.buflen--; /* Make sure there is always space for the nulterm */

    /* The latest history entry is always our current buffer, that
     * initially is just an empty string. */
    linenoiseHistoryAdd("");

    if (write(out_fd, prompt,l.plen) == -1) {
        return -1;
    }
    flushWrite();

    /* If the prompt has been registered with ANSI escape sequences
     * for terminal colors then we remove them from the prompt length
     * calculation. */
    l.plen = prompt_len_ignore_escape_seq(prompt);

    while(1) {
        char c;

        /**
         * To determine whether the user is pasting data or typing itself, we
         * need to calculate how many milliseconds elapsed between two key
         * presses. Indeed, if there is less than LINENOISE_PASTE_KEY_DELAY
         * (typically 30-40ms), then a paste is being performed, else, the
         * user is typing.
         * NOTE: pressing a key down without releasing it will also spend
         * about 40ms (or even more)
         */
        t1 = getMillis();
        int nread = read_func(in_fd, &c, 1);
        if (nread <= 0) {
            return l.len;
        }

        if ( (getMillis() - t1) < LINENOISE_PASTE_KEY_DELAY && c != ENTER) {
            /* Pasting data, insert characters without formatting.
             * This can only be performed when the cursor is at the end of the
             * line. */
            if (linenoiseInsertPastedChar(&l,c)) {
                return -1;
            }
            continue;
        }

        /* Only autocomplete when the callback is set. It returns < 0 when
         * there was an error reading from fd. Otherwise it will return the
         * character that should be handled next. */
        if (c == 9 && completionCallback != NULL) {
            int c2 = completeLine(&l);
            /* Return on errors */
            if (c2 < 0) return l.len;
            /* Read next character when 0 */
            if (c2 == 0) continue;
            c = c2;
        }

        switch(c) {
        case ENTER:    /* enter */
            history_len--;
            free(history[history_len]);
            if (mlmode) linenoiseEditMoveEnd(&l);
            if (hintsCallback) {
                /* Force a refresh without hints to leave the previous
                 * line as the user typed it after a newline. */
                linenoiseHintsCallback *hc = hintsCallback;
                hintsCallback = NULL;
                refreshLine(&l);
                hintsCallback = hc;
            }
            return (int)l.len;
        case CTRL_C:     /* ctrl-c */
            errno = EAGAIN;
            return -1;
        case BACKSPACE:   /* backspace */
        case CTRL_H:     /* ctrl-h */
            linenoiseEditBackspace(&l);
            break;
        case CTRL_D:     /* ctrl-d, remove char at right of cursor, or if the
                            line is empty, act as end-of-file. */
            if (l.len > 0) {
                linenoiseEditDelete(&l);
            } else {
                history_len--;
                free(history[history_len]);
                return -1;
            }
            break;
        case CTRL_T:    /* ctrl-t, swaps current character with previous. */
            if (l.pos > 0 && l.pos < l.len) {
                int aux = buf[l.pos-1];
                buf[l.pos-1] = buf[l.pos];
                buf[l.pos] = aux;
                if (l.pos != l.len-1) l.pos++;
                refreshLine(&l);
            }
            break;
        case CTRL_B:     /* ctrl-b */
            linenoiseEditMoveLeft(&l);
            break;
        case CTRL_F:     /* ctrl-f */
            linenoiseEditMoveRight(&l);
            break;
```

Key facts from the source: the probe uses **blocking** reads, and `getColumns()` runs at the very start of each line — *before* the prompt is written. So when you fire off the next command quickly after Enter (type-ahead), your keystrokes block-feed the probe and get eaten. That's the race, and it's inherent to ESP-IDF's linenoise in ANSI mode. There's no Kconfig/API to set a fixed width or skip it.

Let me check whether the REPL even enables history, and how dumb-mode branches, so I pick the right fix:

```text
char *linenoise(const char *prompt) {
    char *buf = calloc(1, max_cmdline_length);
    int count = 0;
    if (buf == NULL) {
        return NULL;
    }
    if (!dumbmode) {
        count = linenoiseRaw(buf, max_cmdline_length, prompt);
    } else {
        count = linenoiseDumb(buf, max_cmdline_length, prompt);
    }
    if (count > 0) {
        sanitize(buf);
        count = strlen(buf);
    } else if (count == 0 && allow_empty) {
        /* will return an empty (0-length) string */
    } else {
        free(buf);
        return NULL;
    }
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-13 21:03:06Z)**_

Now I understand it fully — and history is the deciding factor:

- History (up/down) is already enabled by default (`max_history_len = 32`), but it **only works in ANSI mode** (`linenoiseRaw`). My `linenoiseSetDumbMode(1)` routes to the dumb reader, which has no history or arrow keys — that's why you lost it.
- The probe race is inherent to ANSI mode and there's **no config knob** to set a fixed width or skip it.

So the honest tradeoff is: dumb mode = stable but no history; ANSI = history but the per-line cursor probe can eat type-ahead. To get *both*, the fix is to **flush any pending input right before each prompt** so there's nothing queued for the probe to swallow — but that means running our own small REPL loop instead of `esp_console_start_repl` (it doesn't expose a hook between lines).

```bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fauxmote: Phase 3 — guitar extension plays GH3 (module + encryption + basic IR)

Implement the Guitar Hero guitar extension end to end; GH3 detects the guitar
and frets/strum/whammy register in-game.

- Refactor the guitar into its own module behind an extension interface
  (wiimote_ext.h: wiimote_extension_t + Wiimote_RegisterExtension). wiimote.c is
  now extension-agnostic — serves the registered register bank for 0xa4xxxx I/O,
  calls build_report for the extension field, and delegates unknown button names.
  guitar.c owns the report, register bank (ID 00 00 A4 20 01 03 at 0xfa), and
  state; buttons drive by name via Wiimote_SetButton/TapButton.

- Implement the Wii extension cipher (ext_crypto.c/.h) in the base Wiimote. GH3
  requires it: it writes 0x55 to 0xf0 and reads the ID in the clear, then 0xAA to
  0xf0 plus a 16-byte key to 0x40-0x4f, after which the streamed extension bytes
  and the 0x20 calibration must be encrypted. The base captures the key, derives
  the ft/sb tables, and encrypts outgoing extension data (streamed bytes at reg
  offset 0x08; register reads at addr & 7); the guitar stays plaintext. Tables are
  the marcan 1st-party set taken from Dolphin (rnconrad's wm_crypto.c S-boxes are
  corrupted); the algorithm was cross-checked against Dolphin and round-tripped
  against GH3's real key.

- Set byte 0/1 bits 7-6 to identify a GH3 Les Paul (clear = GHWT, which makes GH3
  ignore the strum bar).

- Fill basic IR (modes 0x36/0x37) via build_ir_basic + a shared ir_dots, so the
  Home-overlay pointer works in the guitar report mode. Packing verified against
  Dolphin's IRBasic struct and the Linux hid-wiimote decoder.

- console: force linenoise dumb mode (the per-line cursor-position probe races
  with typed input over the UART and spuriously commits lines); demote the
  per-report RX log to debug.

- Update SPEC.md and the journal (encryption is required, the real GH3 key
  handshake, the extension-module architecture, pointer findings); mark Phases
  2 and 3 done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
```

```text
99	/* Read HIDP frames from one HID channel and dispatch them to the Wiimote module.
100	 * Exits when its CLOSE handler sets `stop` — not by watching read() return codes,
101	 * since re-armed servers can recycle this fd number out from under us. */
102	static void hid_reader_task(void *arg)
103	{
104	    hid_link_t *l = (hid_link_t *)arg;
105	    while (!l->stop) {
106	        int n = read(l->fd, l->rx, sizeof(l->rx));
107	        if (l->stop) break;
108	        if (n > 0) {
109	            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "fd %d RX report 0x%02x (%d B)", l->fd,
110	                     n > 1 ? l->rx[1] : 0, n);
111	            Wiimote_HandleRx(l->fd, l->rx, n);
112	        } else if (n < 0) {
113	            break;                          /* genuine close of our fd */
114	        } else {
115	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));  /* non-blocking VFS: 0 = no data yet */
116	        }
117	    }
118	    l->in_use = false;
119	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
120	}

123	{

126	            s_links[i].in_use = true;
127	            s_links[i].stop = false;
128	            s_links[i].fd = fd;
129	            s_links[i].handle = handle;
130	            xTaskCreateStatic(hid_reader_task, "hid_rx", HID_RX_STACK,
131	                              &s_links[i], 5, s_links[i].stack, &s_links[i].tcb);
132	            return;
133	        }
134	    }

157	static void l2cap_cb(esp_bt_l2cap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_l2cap_cb_param_t *param)
158	{
159	    switch (event) {
160	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_INIT_EVT:
161	        /* The L2CAP data path is fd-based; the VFS must be registered before a
162	         * server can allocate a slot/fd. */
163	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP init status=%d; registering VFS", param->init.status);
164	        esp_bt_l2cap_vfs_register();
165	        break;
166	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_VFS_REGISTER_EVT:
167	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP VFS registered status=%d", param->vfs_register.status);
168	        break;
169	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_START_EVT:
170	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP server up status=%d handle=%u",
171	                 param->start.status, (unsigned)param->start.handle);
172	        break;
173	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT:
174	        log_bda("L2CAP OPEN from", param->open.rem_bda);
175	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "  status=%d handle=%u fd=%d mtu=%d",
176	                 param->open.status, (unsigned)param->open.handle,
177	                 param->open.fd, (int)param->open.tx_mtu);
178	        hid_link_start(param->open.fd, param->open.handle);
179	        /* Connected — stop being discoverable (stay connectable for reconnects),
180	         * matching a real Wiimote which doesn't advertise once connected. */
181	        esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
182	        s_discoverable = false;
183	        if (s_reconnecting) {
184	            /* control channel re-opened — now open the interrupt channel. */
185	            s_reconnecting = false;
186	            esp_bt_l2cap_connect(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT, s_wii_bda);
187	        }
188	        break;
189	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_CLOSE_EVT:
190	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "L2CAP CLOSE handle=%u async=%d",
191	                 (unsigned)param->close.handle, param->close.async);
192	        /* Signal this channel's reader to exit (by handle, robust to fd reuse). */
193	        hid_link_stop(param->close.handle);
194	        /* Stop streaming + reset controller state immediately so the sender
195	         * doesn't write into the dying channel and the LED returns to idle. */
196	        Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected();
197	        /* Arm auto-reconnect unless this was a user-requested stop/unlink. */
198	        if (s_have_wii && !s_suppress_reconnect) {
199	            s_want_reconnect = true;
200	        }
201	        s_suppress_reconnect = false;
202	        break;
203	    default:
204	        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "l2cap event %d", event);
205	        break;
206	    }
207	}

209	/* Heal an unexpected link drop (e.g. the Wii's brief disconnect when a game boots)
210	 * by re-initiating the connection, like a real Wiimote. Bounded retries; cleared
211	 * once the Wii is talking to us again, or on a user stop/unlink. */
212	static void reconnect_task(void *arg)
213	{
214	    (void)arg;
215	    for (;;) {
216	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1000));
217	        if (Wiimote_IsConnected()) {
218	            s_want_reconnect = false;
219	            s_reconnect_tries = 0;
220	            continue;
221	        }
222	        if (!s_want_reconnect || !s_have_wii) {
223	            continue;
224	        }
225	        /* Keep trying like a real Wiimote — a game disc can take a while to boot and
226	         * re-accept the controller. Back off after a few quick tries so we don't
227	         * hammer the link while the Wii is still reinitializing. */
228	        s_reconnect_tries++;
229	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "auto-reconnect attempt %d", s_reconnect_tries);
230	        Fauxmote_Reconnect();
231	        int wait_ms = (s_reconnect_tries < AUTO_RECONNECT_MAX) ? 3000 : 8000;
232	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(wait_ms));
233	    }
234	}

236	void Fauxmote_BtStart(void)
237	{
238	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_mem_release(ESP_BT_MODE_BLE));
239	    esp_bt_controller_config_t cfg = BT_CONTROLLER_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
240	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_init(&cfg));

242	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_init());
243	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_enable());
244	
245	    const uint8_t *bda = esp_bt_dev_get_address();
246	    if (bda) {
247	        /* Our BD_ADDR — also the 1+2 temporary-pairing PIN (this, reversed). */
248	        log_bda("BD_ADDR", bda);

250	
251	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_register_callback(gap_cb));
252	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_set_device_name(FAUXMOTE_BT_NAME));
253	
254	    /* Legacy PIN pairing (SSP disabled in sdkconfig): we answer each PIN request. */
255	    esp_bt_gap_set_pin(ESP_BT_PIN_TYPE_VARIABLE, 0, NULL);
256	
257	    /* Serve the exact Wiimote SDP record, then listen for the Wii's HID L2CAP
258	     * connections on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). */
259	    if (!WiimoteSdp_Register()) {
260	        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Wiimote SDP registration failed");
261	    }
262	    Wiimote_Start();
263	
264	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_register_callback(l2cap_cb));
265	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_init());
266	
267	    xTaskCreateStatic(reconnect_task, "reconnect", AUTO_RECONNECT_STACK, NULL, 4,
268	                      s_recon_stack, &s_recon_tcb);
269	
270	    /* The stack persists the bond (link key) in NVS and reloads it at boot — recall
271	     * the bonded Wii's address so `reconnect` works after a power cycle. */
272	    int bonded = esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_num();
273	    if (bonded > 0) {
274	        esp_bd_addr_t devs[8];
275	        int n = bonded > 8 ? 8 : bonded;
276	        if (esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list(&n, devs) == ESP_OK && n > 0) {
277	            memcpy(s_wii_bda, devs[0], sizeof(s_wii_bda));
278	            s_have_wii = true;
279	            log_bda("recalled bonded Wii", s_wii_bda);
280	        }
281	    }
282	
283	    /* Stay idle (not discoverable/connectable) until the operator runs `pair`. */
284	    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_NON_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
285	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "fauxmote up (idle). Use the `pair` console command to sync with a Wii.");
```

Done. Auto-reconnect is fully removed:

- Deleted the `reconnect_task`, its startup, the `s_want_reconnect`/`s_suppress_reconnect`/`s_reconnect_tries` state, and the arming in the L2CAP `CLOSE` handler. A drop now just resets state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`) and stops there.
- **Kept the manual `reconnect` CLI command** for deliberate recovery.
- **Kept the sniff-delay override** (idle→sniff = 65 s) — that's a different mechanism that genuinely prevents idle *supervision-timeout* drops, not a reconnect.

On keep-awake: you're right that reconnecting was never going to do it.
